When the iBudget handbook, rate rules or other waiver rules change, the Administrator, with the billing lead, reviews the affected policies (especially GOV-05, STF-04 and BSP-01) within 30 days of the effective date and revises them as needed.

A revision is drafted by the policy owner, reviewed by the Administrator for accuracy and consistency with related policies, and approved by the governing body or its authorized designee. The approval is signed and dated.

The Policy Coordinator updates the version number, effective date and version history, removes superseded copies from all homes, and archives each old version with its dates of use for at least [RETENTION PERIOD] years.

Each revision is trained and acknowledged. The Administrator or Home Manager gives staff a summary of what changed and how it affects their work, and each staff member signs the acknowledgment. Revisions are effective for staff only after they have signed the acknowledgment, except where urgent safety or legal changes require immediate interim written direction.
Acknowledgments are placed in each staff member's personnel record (STF-06). The Policy Coordinator tracks acknowledgments and reports to the Administrator any not signed within 14 days.
New hires receive the manual's resident-rights, abuse reporting, emergency and medication policies during orientation, and sign for the entire manual before working alone (STF-04).

Before submitting policies with a license application or the waiver provider packet, the Policy Coordinator confirms the version being sent is current and records the version number and the submission date.

If a deficiency or incident review shows a policy is unclear or has failed, the Administrator may issue an interim revision outside the annual cycle. It follows the same approval and acknowledgment steps and is reviewed fully at the next annual review.
The governing body receives a document-control report at least annually. It covers review completion, revisions made, acknowledgment rates and any overdue policy reviews.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the manual and material revisions and receives the annual document-control report.
Leads the annual review, monitors rule changes, and ensures revisions are approved, trained and acknowledged.
Maintains the master manual, version history, controlled copies and acknowledgment tracking.
Review assigned policies at least annually and when rules or practice change, and draft revisions.
Keep only controlled copies in the home, replace superseded copies, and make sure staff sign acknowledgments.
Follow the current policies and sign acknowledgment of each revision.

documentation: Master manual with headers showing version, effective date and approval
Version history log
Annual policy review checklist, including the CEMP update date
Rule-monitoring log (dates checked and changes found)
Governing body approval minutes
Staff acknowledgments in personnel records
Archive of superseded versions
Record of versions submitted to APD with license and waiver provider applications

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, Home Managers, Nurse/health care coordinator and the Quality Improvement Designee
policies.purpose: To make [AGENCY NAME] review its own incident, health, behavior and monitoring data on a regular schedule, review every death, and use the results to improve safety and services.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will run a quality improvement program that reviews incident reports (APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006), follow-up measures and trends at least quarterly. It will track medication errors, restraint use, elopements and injuries. Every death will be reviewed, using the death-notification steps in HW-05 and BSP-04. The verified rules available to the agency do not set out specific mortality-review steps, so the Administrator will confirm APD's current requirements and adopt them in writing. Findings from APD's monthly monitoring visits (Rule 65G-2.0032) will feed corrective action. The program also uses what the iBudget Handbook requires of the provider: implementation plans, quarterly summaries and annual reports. For residents with a behavior focus or intensive behavioral designation, it uses the monitoring and staff training the handbook requires. The quality program supports, and never replaces, the agency's reporting duties under Rule 65G-2.010: the Abuse Hotline immediately, initial notice of a critical incident within 4 hours and the completed Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day, reportable incidents within 1 calendar day, and follow-up within 5 days.

definitions.definition: The person appointed by the Administrator to compile data, schedule reviews and track corrective actions.
A pattern across incidents, residents, staff, shifts, locations or times that suggests a systemic cause.
A written plan naming the problem, root cause, action, responsible person, due date and method of checking that the action worked.
A review of the circumstances, care and records leading to a resident's death, done to find preventable factors and improve practice.

procedures: The Administrator appoints a Quality Improvement Designee and records the appointment. The governing body approves the annual quality plan, listing the indicators to be tracked.

Each home logs every incident, medication error, restraint, elopement or missing person event, injury, hospital or ER visit, rights restriction and grievance on a standard tracking sheet. The Home Manager enters each within 2 business days of the incident.

Incident reporting happens first and is never delayed for review. Staff report to the Abuse Hotline immediately where required, notify APD of a critical incident within 4 hours, and send the completed OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day (BSP-03, BSP-04). Other reportable incidents are reported within 1 calendar day, and follow-up is sent within 5 days.
At least monthly, the Home Manager reviews the home's incident and medication error log, checks that every follow-up measure on each OP 3-0006 was completed, and sends a summary to the Administrator.

At least quarterly, the Quality Improvement Designee compiles data for each home covering incident counts and types, medication errors by type, restraint use, elopements, injuries and falls, ER visits and hospitalizations, and grievances. The designee looks for trends by resident, staff member, shift, time of day and location.

The Administrator, nurse or health care coordinator, and a behavior analyst or behavior services provider (where the agency has residents with behavior supports) meet quarterly to review the data. The meeting is recorded in minutes with attendance, findings and decisions.
Any medication error pattern or serious error triggers review of the staff member's medication competency, retraining where needed, and a check of the medication system (HW-01).

Any use of restraint is reviewed in detail. The team reviews whether it was permitted, whether it was documented and reported as required, whether less restrictive options were used first, and whether the behavior support plan needs revision (BSP-01, BSP-02).
Every elopement or missing person event is reviewed to determine how it happened, how fast the response was, and what supervision, environmental or planning changes are needed (BSP-05).

Each quarter the team reviews a sample of resident records. The sample covers whether implementation plans, daily documentation, quarterly summaries and annual reports are complete and on time, as the iBudget Handbook requires. Gaps go on the corrective action log.

For residents with a behavior focus or intensive behavioral designation, the team confirms that monitoring by a BCBA or Ch. 490/491 professional is occurring as the handbook requires, and that direct staff have completed the required training.

When APD monitors the home (at least monthly), the Administrator obtains the written findings. Each finding goes on the corrective action log with a root cause, action, owner and due date. The Administrator verifies completion, and unresolved items are escalated to the governing body.

Within 7 days of any death, the Administrator confirms the required notifications were made under HW-05 and BSP-04 and secures the resident's record, medication administration records, incident reports and staff schedule.

The Administrator checks APD's current requirements for mortality review and records them in writing. Until confirmed requirements say otherwise, the agency convenes an internal review within 30 days of each death with the nurse or health care coordinator, the Home Manager, and, where available, the resident's support coordinator. The review looks at the resident's health history, recent changes in condition, response to the emergency, staffing at the time, and any care or system factors. It produces a written summary and any corrective actions. Any APD or other external review request is answered promptly and in full.
The designee tracks every corrective action to completion and re-checks the related data the next quarter to confirm the action worked. Actions that did not work are reopened.

The designee prepares an annual quality report for the governing body summarizing the data, trends, corrective actions, mortality reviews and recommended policy changes. Results go to the annual policy review under GOV-03.

Quality records contain resident information and are kept confidential and protected in keeping with IR-05. Reports for outside distribution remove personal identifiers unless a law or rule requires disclosure.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the quality plan, reviews the quarterly and annual reports, and ensures corrective actions are resourced.
Leads quarterly reviews, assigns corrective actions, manages APD findings and death reviews, and confirms current APD mortality review requirements.
Compiles data, prepares reports, tracks corrective actions and schedules reviews.
Keeps logs current, verifies incident follow-up and implements corrective actions in the home.
Reviews health-related data including medication errors, injuries, hospitalizations and deaths, and advises on clinical corrective actions.
Reviews restraint and behavior data and recommends plan changes.

documentation: Quality plan and designee appointment
Monthly home incident and medication error summaries
Quarterly data compilations and trend analysis
Quarterly quality review minutes
Corrective action log with closure verification
Copies of OP 3-0006 reports and follow-up submissions
APD monitoring reports and responses
Mortality review summaries and APD requirement confirmation
Annual quality report to the governing body

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing and Service Documentation
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, billing staff, Home Managers and all direct support staff who document services
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] bills Medicaid iBudget only for authorized services actually delivered, at the correct rate, with complete documentation, and that room and board and personal funds are handled correctly.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will bill only for services covered by an authorization issued by the resident's waiver support coordinator (WSC). It bills Residential Habilitation under the iBudget Waiver Services Coverage and Limitations Handbook (Rule 59G-13.070). It bills the monthly rate when the resident was in the home for 24 or more days in the month and the daily rate otherwise. It never bills days the resident was absent. Rates are those in Rule 59G-13.081, which are set by support level and county group; the Oct. 1, 2025 table is the table in effect, and a July 2026 table is in rulemaking and will be applied only when it is effective. The agency will meet the handbook's minimum direct-care hours per resident per 24 hours: Basic 2, Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8, Extensive 2 11. It documents services in APD iConnect, and staff who use it complete iConnect training, including the test (75% passing). It claims room and board on Form 65G-13.008A within 90 days after month end, at no more than the APD standard of $583.42 a month, and it protects each resident's personal needs allowance (at least 18% of the SSI federal benefit rate, $178.92 a month at the 2026 rate of $994). Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) in iConnect applies to personal care and home health, not residential habilitation. Services will be delivered in settings that meet the federal HCBS settings requirements at 42 CFR 441.301(c) (see IR-01). False, inflated or unsupported billing is prohibited.

definitions.definition: The approved service, level and period issued through the resident's WSC and APD that permits the provider to deliver and bill a service.
The monthly rate is billed when the resident was in the home 24 or more days in the month. The daily rate is billed per day otherwise.
The resident's assigned Basic, Minimal, Moderate, Extensive 1 or Extensive 2 level, which determines the rate and minimum direct-care hours.
APD's web-based system used by waiver providers for documentation, notes and related functions.
The portion of the resident's income reserved for personal use, at least 18% of the SSI federal benefit rate ($178.92 a month at the 2026 rate).
The form used to claim APD room and board payment.

procedures: Before a resident's first day of service and at each authorization change, the Administrator or billing lead obtains the WSC-issued authorization and enters the service, support level, rate, county group and effective dates in the resident's billing file. Services are never started or billed ahead of an authorization.

The Administrator and billing lead verify the rate against Rule 59G-13.081 (support level and county group) each time the rule table changes and at least annually. The July 2026 table is applied only on its effective date. The check and its date are recorded.

Each Home Manager tracks daily attendance on a resident census/attendance sheet that records the days each resident was in the home, absent (hospital, family visit or other), or discharged. Staff sign each day's entry.

At month end, the Home Manager sends the attendance sheet to the billing lead by the [DAY] of the following month. The billing lead counts the days in the home. If the resident was in the home 24 or more days, the monthly rate is billed. Otherwise, the daily rate is billed for each day the resident was in the home. Absent days are never billed.

The billing lead checks the claim against the authorization, attendance sheet, support level and the resident's service documentation before submission, and a second person (the Administrator or designee) reviews each batch before it is released.

Residents' direct-care staffing hours are totaled daily and reconciled monthly against the handbook minimum for the resident's support level: Basic 2, Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8, Extensive 2 11 hours per resident per 24 hours. Any shortfall is reported to the Administrator and corrected under STF-01. Staffing to the minimum is not a substitute for the ratios and supervision required under STF-01.

The behavior focus or intensive behavioral rate is billed only when APD has approved that designation for the resident and for the agency, and when the required monitoring by a BCBA or Ch. 490/491 professional and staff training are in place (BSP-01). Otherwise the standard rate is billed.

Staff document resident services daily as set out in PCS-03, and the Home Manager completes the implementation plan, quarterly summary and annual report that the handbook requires, on time. Documentation is entered in APD iConnect where required.

Every staff member who uses iConnect completes iConnect training and passes the test (75%) before getting independent access. The certificate is kept in the personnel record (STF-04, STF-06). Staff never share log-in credentials.
Documentation errors are corrected by a dated, initialed addendum that keeps the original entry visible. Staff never backdate, pre-chart or alter records to support a claim.

Room and board is calculated by the billing lead for each resident at no more than the APD standard of $583.42 a month, in a way that never reduces the resident's personal needs allowance below $178.92 a month. The billing lead completes Form 65G-13.008A and submits it within 90 days after month end. The submission date is recorded.
Personal funds are handled under IR-06. The billing lead and Home Manager reconcile room and board charges and the PNA to the resident's ledger each month.
The agency does not apply EVV to residential habilitation. The billing lead keeps a note of the current rule on EVV so that the practice is rechecked if the handbook changes.
The Administrator performs a quarterly internal billing audit of a sample of at least [NUMBER] claims per home. The audit checks the authorization, rate, attendance, documentation and staffing hours.

Any overpayment or billing error found is corrected within [NUMBER] days of discovery, and the Administrator reports it to AHCA or APD as required. The Administrator retains a written record of the cause and prevention steps (GOV-04).
The Administrator reports compliance concerns directly to the governing body. No staff member is penalized for raising a billing or documentation concern in good faith.
Billing and documentation records are kept as required by REC-01, and made available to APD, AHCA and other authorized reviewers on request.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures resources and oversight for compliant billing, reviews audit results and receives reports of compliance concerns.
Owns Medicaid compliance, approves claim batches, directs the quarterly audit, and corrects errors and overpayments.
Verifies authorizations and rates, calculates and submits claims and Form 65G-13.008A, and keeps billing files.
Keeps accurate attendance, staffing-hour and service documentation and submits them on time.
Document services truthfully and promptly, complete iConnect training, and never alter records.
Issues authorizations and support-level information used for billing.

documentation: WSC-issued authorizations and support level documentation
Resident daily attendance/census sheets
Daily staffing-hour reconciliation
Claim batches, second-person review records and remittance records
Rate verification record (Rule 59G-13.081 table used and date checked)
Implementation plans, quarterly summaries and annual reports
iConnect training certificates (75% test)
Form 65G-13.008A submissions with dates
Room and board and PNA ledgers
Quarterly billing audit reports and overpayment correction records

policies.title: Financial Ability, Annual Cost Statement and Insurance
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator and the person responsible for the agency's finances and insurance
policies.purpose: To show and maintain [AGENCY NAME]'s financial ability to operate each home, to file the annual sworn statement of costs, and to carry the insurance the agency is required or has chosen to carry.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will keep current proof of financial ability to operate each licensed home, as required by s. 393.067, F.S. APD may ask for proof that the agency can operate 60 days without state payment (Rule 65G-2.0032), and the agency will keep that proof ready at all times. It will file the annual sworn statement of costs for APD-funded clients required by s. 393.067(10), F.S. It will carry workers' compensation insurance whenever it has four or more employees (s. 440.02, F.S.), counted conservatively and including part-time staff. The rules cited in this policy do not set a minimum liability limit, so the governing body will set liability and automobile coverage limits with its insurance broker based on risk, document them, and keep them in force without gaps.

definitions.definition: Documents that show the agency has the funds or credit to start and operate each home, such as bank statements, a budget, lines of credit or financial statements.
The funds or credit that would cover the agency's operating costs for 60 days without payment from the state.
The annual statement, sworn to under oath, of the agency's costs for APD-funded clients, filed as s. 393.067(10), F.S. requires.
The insurer's document showing the coverage types, limits and policy period.

procedures: Before the initial license application, the Administrator and the governing body prepare an operating budget for each home covering start-up costs and at least 12 months of operating costs, including payroll, rent or mortgage, food, utilities, insurance, vehicle costs and supplies. The budget is signed by the governing body.

The Administrator assembles proof of financial ability for each home (bank statements, financing commitments, financial statements or other documents the APD application accepts) and includes it in the application and every renewal packet (GOV-02).

The Administrator calculates monthly operating costs for each home and maintains a documented 60-day operating reserve in cash or an available credit line of at least [AMOUNT]. The calculation is updated at least quarterly and whenever a home opens, closes or changes capacity.

If APD asks for proof of ability to operate 60 days without state payment, the Administrator sends the reserve calculation and supporting bank or credit documents within the deadline APD gives, and keeps a copy and the date sent.
The Administrator watches cash flow monthly. If the reserve falls below the 60-day level, the Administrator tells the governing body within 5 business days and presents a written plan to restore it.

The agency keeps the books on a basis that tracks revenue and cost separately for each home and each APD-funded resident, so costs can be reported accurately. The accounting records are kept in line with REC-01.

Each year, the Administrator, with the agency's accountant, prepares the annual sworn statement of costs for APD-funded clients using the form and instructions APD provides, from the general ledger and payroll records.

The person signing the statement swears to it before a notary or other authorized officer, after reviewing the supporting schedules. The Administrator files it with APD by the deadline in the APD instructions and keeps proof of filing.
The governing body reviews the draft statement and supporting schedules before it is signed.

The Administrator keeps workers' compensation insurance in force. The agency counts its employees each month, including part-time and temporary staff on payroll, and obtains coverage before the agency reaches four employees. Proof of coverage is kept in the licensing binder (see STF-08).

The agency carries general liability, professional liability, and automobile liability (including any hired and non-owned vehicle coverage) in the limits set by the governing body, and sets limits at least yearly with its broker. Property coverage on each home is also maintained, as the lease or mortgage requires.
The Administrator keeps a certificate for each policy, an insurance schedule showing coverage type, limit, insurer, policy number and expiration, and reminders 60 days before each expiration.

Insurance is renewed before expiration with no gap in coverage. If any coverage lapses or is cancelled, the Administrator tells the governing body the same day and arranges replacement, and does not allow vehicle use or resident care to continue under an uninsured activity.
The Administrator reports any claim or potential claim to the insurer promptly in line with the policy terms, and tells the governing body.
The governing body reviews financial ability, the reserve, the sworn cost statement filing and the insurance schedule at least quarterly and records the review in minutes (GOV-01).

responsibilities.duty: Provides funding, approves budgets and insurance limits, and reviews financial and insurance status quarterly.
Maintains proof of financial ability and the 60-day reserve calculation, prepares and files the annual sworn cost statement, and manages insurance renewals.
Keeps home-by-home records, prepares cost schedules and supports the sworn statement.
Advises on coverage and provides certificates and renewal notices.

documentation: Operating budgets and proof of financial ability submitted with applications and renewals
60-day reserve calculation and supporting bank or credit documents
Annual sworn statement of costs with proof of filing and supporting schedules
Insurance schedule and certificates (workers' compensation, liability, auto, property)
Employee headcount record used for the four-employee test
Governing body minutes showing quarterly review

policies.title: Facility Siting, Zoning and Licensed Capacity Compliance
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, Home Managers and the admissions team
policies.purpose: To make sure each home is lawfully sited and zoned, operates within the capacity and resident characteristics on its license, and that changes in capacity or census are requested and reported as required.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will site and operate each home in compliance with s. 419.001, F.S., Rule 65G-2.015, and Rule 65G-2.006, F.A.C. A home of 6 or fewer residents is a single-family use. A home of 7 to 14 residents must be in multifamily zoning, and the local government has 60 days to approve or deny. No more than three APD facilities may be within 1,000 feet. The agency will notify local zoning when the home receives its first resident. A group home facility is defined as 4 to 15 residents and a foster care facility as 3 or fewer (s. 393.063, F.S.). A change in licensed capacity will be requested from APD 30 days ahead, with a passed fire inspection and zoning compliance. Census changes will be reported to APD in writing. The home will serve only residents whose characteristics match its license. It will never exceed licensed capacity, except as APD allows during an emergency under the CEMP.

definitions.definition: The maximum number of residents APD authorizes for the home on its license.
The categories of residents (for example, age, gender, or support needs) the license permits the home to serve.
The zoning treatment given to a community residential home of 6 or fewer residents.
The zoning category in which homes of 7 to 14 residents must be located.
Any change in the number or identity of residents in the home, including admission, discharge, transfer or death.

procedures: Before purchasing or leasing a property, the Administrator confirms the proposed capacity and obtains the zoning designation for the address from the local zoning authority, in writing where possible.

The Administrator checks, with APD and the local government, whether any other APD-licensed facilities are within 1,000 feet of the proposed address, and records the finding. No more than three APD facilities may be within 1,000 feet. If the count would exceed three, the agency does not proceed with that site.

For a proposed home of 6 or fewer residents, the Administrator obtains written confirmation that the site is zoned for single-family use. For a proposed home of 7 to 14 residents, the Administrator confirms the site is in multifamily zoning, submits the notice to the local government as s. 419.001 requires, and calendars the 60-day approval or denial period.

The statutory siting provisions address homes of 6 or fewer and of 7 to 14 residents. Any proposal for a 15-resident group home is confirmed in writing with APD and the local zoning authority before the agency commits to the property or capacity.
The Administrator keeps the zoning approval, notices and correspondence in the licensing binder for each home and gives APD a copy with the license application (GOV-02).

When the first resident is admitted, the Administrator sends written notice to the local zoning authority within [NUMBER] days and keeps a copy. The Administrator also records the first-admission date, which starts APD's 30-day on-site review period (GOV-02).

Before each admission, the admissions team checks the referral against the license: the home has an open licensed bed and the resident's characteristics match the license. A referral that does not match is declined, and the decision is documented (SDB-01, PCS-01).

The Home Manager keeps a daily census count and posts the licensed capacity in the home's administrative file. The Home Manager reports any situation that could place the census above the licensed capacity to the Administrator immediately. The agency does not admit a resident who would exceed capacity.

The Administrator reports census changes to APD in writing, using the method and timeframe in the APD instructions, and keeps a copy of each report and proof of delivery. Admissions, discharges, transfers and deaths are all census changes.

To increase or change licensed capacity, the Administrator first confirms that the new capacity fits the zoning rules above. The Administrator then obtains a passed fire inspection for the new capacity and sends APD a written request at least 30 days before the proposed effective date, with proof of the passed fire inspection and zoning compliance.
Capacity increases are not effective, and no additional resident is admitted, until APD approves the new capacity in writing and the revised license is received.

To change the resident characteristics on the license, the Administrator submits a written request to APD and waits for written approval before accepting a resident outside the current characteristics.

If APD or a local authority finds that the home is out of compliance with siting, zoning or capacity, the Administrator tells the governing body the same day, takes the corrective steps directed, and records the matter in the corrective action log (GOV-04).
The Administrator rechecks each home's zoning status, nearby APD facilities and capacity compliance at least annually, with the license renewal, and records the date and result.
During an emergency evacuation to a shelter, any over-capacity situation is reported as required under the CEMP (SDA-01, HES-02).

responsibilities.duty: Approves site selection and capacity, and does not authorize any admission or program that would conflict with zoning or the license.
Verifies zoning and siting, notifies local zoning, requests capacity changes, reports census changes, and keeps records.
Checks each referral against licensed capacity and resident characteristics before admission.
Keeps the daily census accurate and reports any capacity concerns at once.

documentation: Zoning designation and approval letters for each home, including any 60-day approval or denial records
1,000-foot facility check record
Notice to local zoning of first resident
License showing licensed capacity and resident characteristics
Daily census records and written census-change reports to APD with proof of delivery
Capacity-change requests with passed fire inspection and zoning proof, and APD's written approvals
Admission eligibility checks against license characteristics
Annual siting and capacity compliance check record

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
policies.applies_to: All residents, their guardians, guardian advocates and representatives, and all [AGENCY NAME] employees, contractors and volunteers at every licensed group home site
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident of a [AGENCY NAME] group home receives the rights guaranteed by the Bill of Rights of Persons with Developmental Disabilities and lives in a home that meets federal Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) settings requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] adheres to and protects resident rights and freedoms under s. 393.13, F.S., as required by Rule 65G-2.009(1)(b), F.A.C. This policy meets Rule 65G-2.009(1)(b)1.-10. Each item is addressed as follows. (1) Dignity, privacy, humane care and freedom from abuse, neglect and exploitation: residents are treated with dignity, bedroom and bathroom privacy is protected, and suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 (see BSP-03). (2) Freedom from harm, including unnecessary physical, chemical or mechanical restraint, isolation and excessive medication: restraint, seclusion and medication are never used for punishment, staff convenience or as a substitute for supports (see BSP-02 and HW-01). (3) Religious freedom: residents choose whether, where and how to worship, and staff help with access. (4) Services in the least restrictive conditions: supports are delivered in the least restrictive manner that meets the resident's needs. (5) Education and training: residents have access to education, training and skill development consistent with their Individual Plan. (6) Social interaction and community activities: residents are supported to take part in community life and to keep relationships (see PCS-05). (7) Exercise and recreation: residents have regular opportunities for exercise and recreation of their choice. (8) Consent to or refusal of treatment: residents may consent to or refuse treatment, subject to the authority of a guardian advocate under s. 393.12, F.S. or a guardian under ch. 744, F.S. (see IR-07). (9) Non-discrimination: residents are not discriminated against in publicly funded programs (see IR-08). (10) Voting: residents may register and vote, and staff provide information and transportation on request. As a provider-owned or controlled residential setting, [AGENCY NAME] also meets 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4). Each resident has a lease or equivalent residency agreement, a lockable bedroom door, roommate choice, access to food at any time, visitors at times the resident chooses, and freedom to decorate their own space. Any modification of these conditions requires documented person-centered justification and informed consent (see IR-03).

definitions.definition: The rights of persons with developmental disabilities set out in s. 393.13, F.S., which apply to every resident.
The federal conditions in 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4) that a provider-owned or controlled residential setting must meet under the iBudget Florida waiver.
A guardian, guardian advocate, or other person the resident has chosen or the law has designated to help the resident exercise rights.
Any change to an HCBS setting requirement (for example, limiting food access or visitors) that is based on an individual assessed need and documented in the Individual Plan.
Any physical, mechanical or chemical means that restricts a resident's freedom of movement, governed by BSP-02, s. 393.13, F.S. and ch. 65G-8, F.A.C.

procedures: At or before admission, the Facility Operator or designee gives each resident and the resident's guardian, guardian advocate or representative a copy of the Bill of Rights and explains it in plain language and the resident's preferred communication method. The signed acknowledgment goes in the resident record the same day.
The Bill of Rights is posted in a common area of each home in a readable, accessible format (large print, pictures or other formats as needed).

The Facility Operator ensures each resident has a signed lease or equivalent residency agreement before or on the day of move-in. The agreement is explained to the resident and representative and filed in the record.

Each resident's bedroom has a door that locks from the inside. The resident controls the lock and has a key. Staff may enter only with the resident's permission, except in an emergency. Any alternative arrangement must be an approved modification under IR-03.

At admission and at each Individual Plan review, staff ask each resident about roommate preferences. Roommates are assigned only with the resident's agreement, and a resident may request a change at any time.

Residents can get food and drinks at any time, including snacks and meals outside of regular hours. Staff do not lock the kitchen or food storage unless an approved modification under IR-03 exists for that resident.
Residents may have visitors at times of their choosing. House rules (IR-02) may set courtesy expectations but may not limit visiting hours without a documented modification.
Residents may decorate and furnish their own bedroom, within fire and safety rules, and may keep personal belongings. Staff help residents with decorating and record the resident's preferences.

Direct support staff protect privacy by knocking and waiting for a response before entering a bedroom or bathroom. Staff provide personal care in private and keep personal information confidential (IR-05).

Staff support residents to practice their religion, take part in community activities, exercise, recreation, education and training. Participation is offered, never required, and choices are recorded in daily documentation (PCS-03).
Staff offer voter registration assistance and transportation to vote in each election. Staff do not influence how a resident votes.

Staff ask for a resident's informed consent, or the consent of the guardian or guardian advocate where one has been appointed, before any treatment, service or support is started or changed (IR-07). A resident's refusal is respected and recorded, and the nurse or appropriate clinician is informed.

Any staff member who sees a possible rights violation reports it immediately to the Facility Operator. If it involves abuse, neglect or exploitation, the staff member calls the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 immediately.

The Facility Operator reviews rights compliance at least quarterly using resident interviews, observation and record review, and records findings and corrective actions for the Governing Body (GOV-04).
All staff complete rights training at orientation and at least annually (STF-04). Training is documented in the personnel record.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts this policy, provides resources to carry it out, and reviews rights compliance reports.
Delivers the Bill of Rights, ensures leases and HCBS conditions are in place, monitors compliance, and handles reports of violations.
Honor resident rights every shift, document choices and refusals, and report suspected violations immediately.
May exercise rights, request changes and file complaints under IR-04 without retaliation.

documentation: Signed acknowledgment of receipt of the Bill of Rights for each resident and representative
Lease or equivalent residency agreement
Rights training records for each staff member
Records of choices, refusals and consent in the resident record
Quarterly rights compliance review notes
Approved modifications and supporting justification (see IR-03)

policies.title: House Rules
policies.applies_to: All residents, representatives, employees and visitors at each [AGENCY NAME] group home
policies.purpose: To set clear, written house rules for the orderly operation of each home that are developed with residents and do not take away resident rights or HCBS setting protections.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 65G-2.009(1)(d), F.A.C. [AGENCY NAME] establishes, maintains and makes available to residents and employees written house rules and regulations, developed in consultation with residents, for the orderly operation of each group home facility. House rules are kept to what is needed for safety and shared living. House rules may not restrict rights under 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4) or the Bill of Rights, including visitors, access to food at any time, privacy and freedom to decorate. A rule cannot be applied to a resident in a way that limits one of these rights unless a documented, person-centered modification with informed consent is in place under IR-03.

definitions.definition: Written expectations for daily living in the home, such as quiet hours, shared-space courtesy, safety practices and use of shared items.
A documented, individually justified change to an HCBS setting right, approved with informed consent as described in IR-03.
A meeting or other process in which residents give input on the rules in a way each resident can understand and take part in.

procedures: Before a home opens and before any rule is adopted, the Facility Operator holds a house meeting, or individual discussions where needed, with residents to ask what rules they want and what matters to them. Staff use each resident's preferred communication method.
The Facility Operator drafts the written house rules in plain language, with pictures or other formats as needed, using resident input.

The Facility Operator checks each draft rule against the Bill of Rights (IR-01) and HCBS requirements. A rule that limits visitors, food access, privacy, decoration, bedroom access or movement is removed or rewritten.
The Governing Body or [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] approves the rules and records the date of approval and the version.
The Facility Operator gives a copy of the rules to each resident and representative at admission and reviews them in person. Acknowledgment is recorded in the resident record.
The rules are posted in a common area at each home and kept in a binder available to staff, residents and visitors.
Each employee receives the house rules at hire and signs an acknowledgment, which is filed in the personnel record. The Facility Operator reviews the rules at orientation (STF-04).
Staff apply the rules fairly and consistently. Staff do not use rules as punishment, to threaten a resident, or to take away personal items, food, outings or visitors.

If a resident does not follow a rule, staff first talk with the resident to understand the reason and offer support. A repeated problem is referred to the Facility Operator and the support team for review under PCS-02. Concerns about behavior are handled under BSP-01.
If a resident believes a rule is unfair or limits a right, staff help the resident to ask for a change, make a complaint under IR-04 or ask for help from a representative.
If a resident has an assessed need for a limit on a right, the Facility Operator and support team follow IR-03 and do not apply the limit through the house rules.

The Facility Operator reviews the house rules at least annually and whenever a resident, representative or staff member requests a change, or when a resident moves in or out. Residents are consulted on all revisions.
When rules change, the Facility Operator tells residents and representatives and posts the new version within 7 calendar days. Staff receive the updated rules and sign for them.
The previous version of the rules is retained in the document control file under GOV-03.

responsibilities.duty: Develops the rules with residents, checks them for rights conflicts, distributes and posts them, and reviews them at least annually.
Approves the rules and any changes.
Know and apply the rules fairly and report any rule that appears to limit a right.
Give input on the rules and may ask for changes or file a complaint under IR-04.

documentation: Current and prior versions of the written house rules with approval dates
Notes of resident consultation meetings or discussions
Resident and representative acknowledgment of receipt
Employee acknowledgment of receipt in the personnel record
Annual review record

policies.title: Rights Restrictions and Due Process
policies.applies_to: All residents, representatives, Facility Operator, support team members, behavior analysts and direct support staff
policies.purpose: To make sure any limit on a resident's rights or HCBS setting protections is individually justified, consented to, time-limited, reviewed and open to challenge, and that no behavioral program is used without review under APD rule.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not restrict a resident's rights except through a documented, person-centered process. Any modification of an HCBS setting requirement (for example, lockable door, roommate choice, access to food, visitors, or freedom of movement) requires documented person-centered justification and informed consent, as required by 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4). Under s. 393.13, F.S., no behavioral program may be implemented unless it has been reviewed under APD rule, and residents have the right to be free from unnecessary restraint and seclusion. Behavior analysis services that include restricted procedures are provided or supervised by a certified behavior analyst. Written plans are sent to the Local Review Committee (LRC) chair within 5 working days after implementation, and a plan the LRC disapproves is revised and resubmitted within 14 working days (Ch. 65G-4, F.A.C.). Restraint and seclusion are limited by s. 393.13, F.S. and Ch. 65G-8, F.A.C. Residents and representatives are told how to challenge a restriction, including the grievance process and the Florida Abuse Hotline. Restrictions are never used for punishment, for staff convenience or as a substitute for supports.

definitions.definition: Any limit on a right under s. 393.13, F.S. or on an HCBS setting requirement, whether by rule, practice or individual plan.
The APD committee that reviews, approves or disapproves behavior analysis plans that contain restricted procedures.

Voluntary agreement by the resident, or by the guardian or guardian advocate where one has authority, given after an explanation of the purpose, risks, less intrusive alternatives and the right to withdraw.
An emergency procedure used in response to behavior, regulated by Ch. 65G-8, F.A.C. and addressed in BSP-02.
A behavioral procedure that limits a resident's rights or freedom and requires review by the LRC.

procedures: Any staff member who thinks a limit on a resident's rights is needed raises it with the Facility Operator. No staff member may impose a restriction on their own.

The Facility Operator convenes the support team, which includes the resident, representative, nurse or other clinician as relevant, and behavior analyst where behavior is involved, to identify the assessed need that the restriction would address.
The team documents the specific need, the positive supports and less intrusive methods already tried and why they were not enough, and a description of the condition that the restriction responds to.

The team writes the proposed modification into the Individual Plan (PCS-02), including how it will be limited, a plan to collect and review data on its effectiveness, a time limit with dates for review (at least at each plan review and whenever the resident's needs change), and a statement that the modification will not cause harm.

The resident and the guardian or guardian advocate are given a plain-language explanation of the proposed restriction. Informed consent is obtained in writing before the restriction begins. If consent is refused or withdrawn, the restriction does not start or stops immediately.

If the proposal is a behavioral program with restricted procedures, a certified behavior analyst develops or supervises the written plan (BSP-01). The Facility Operator confirms that the plan is not implemented until it has been reviewed under APD rule.
The Facility Operator or behavior analyst sends the written plan to the LRC chair within 5 working days after implementation, and records the date of the submission.

If the LRC disapproves a plan, the behavior analyst and team revise it and resubmit within 14 working days. The Facility Operator tracks the date and stops any disapproved procedure until it is revised and approved.

Restraint and seclusion are used only as permitted by s. 393.13, F.S., Ch. 65G-8, F.A.C. and BSP-02, and only by staff who hold current certification in an APD-approved emergency procedure curriculum. Any prohibited procedure under Ch. 65G-8 is never used.

The resident and representative receive written notice of the restriction, the reason, the review date, and how to challenge it. The notice includes the grievance process (IR-04), the Florida Abuse Hotline number 1-800-962-2873, and the right to ask for the restriction to be reviewed at any time.
Staff carry out the restriction exactly as written, record each use and relevant data, and report any problem to the Facility Operator the same day.
The Facility Operator reviews data on every active restriction at least monthly and at each scheduled team review. The team removes the restriction when it is no longer needed and documents the date.
The Facility Operator tracks all active restrictions on a log, including consent dates, review dates and LRC dates, and reports to the Governing Body quarterly (GOV-04).

A resident or representative may challenge a restriction at any time by telling any staff member, the Facility Operator, the Support Coordinator or APD. The Facility Operator responds in writing within 10 business days, and the restriction is reviewed by the team without delay.

Any restriction implemented without the required consent, justification or review is reported to the Facility Operator as an incident (BSP-04). The restriction is stopped until the requirements are met.

responsibilities.duty: Convenes reviews, ensures consent and documentation, tracks LRC submission deadlines and keeps the restriction log.
Develops or supervises plans with restricted procedures and revises plans disapproved by the LRC.
Decide on the need for, consent to and review each modification.
Follow written plans exactly, record data and report concerns.
Reviews restriction data and corrective actions quarterly.

documentation: Assessed need, prior methods tried and justification for each modification
Signed informed consent from the resident and the guardian or guardian advocate
Individual Plan text describing the modification, time limit and review dates
Behavior analysis plan and LRC submission, approval or disapproval and resubmission dates
Data collected on each restriction and monthly review notes
Written notice to the resident and representative of how to challenge the restriction
Active restrictions log

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
policies.applies_to: All residents, representatives, family members, employees and advocates
policies.purpose: To give residents and their representatives an accessible, safe way to raise concerns and have them resolved, and to make sure allegations of abuse, neglect or exploitation go to the Florida Abuse Hotline and not into the internal grievance process.
policies.policy: Residents, representatives and others may make a complaint at any time, in any form, without fear of retaliation, consistent with the rights protected under s. 393.13, F.S. and Rule 65G-2.009, F.A.C. [AGENCY NAME] posts the grievance process in an accessible format and staff help residents to file. Every complaint, the response and the outcome are logged. Allegations of abuse, neglect or exploitation are not handled through the internal grievance process. They are reported immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873, as required by ss. 39.201 and 415.1034, F.S. as incorporated by Rule 65G-2.010(6)(a), F.A.C. (see BSP-03). Using the grievance process never limits a resident's right to contact APD, the Abuse Hotline, the Support Coordinator, Disability Rights Florida or any other advocate directly.

definitions.definition: Any complaint or expression of dissatisfaction about services, staff, other residents, house rules or conditions in the home, made orally or in writing.
Any adverse action or threat against a resident or other person because of a complaint, including loss of privileges, changes in staffing, treatment or tone.
Any known or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation of a resident, which must be reported immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline.

procedures: At admission, the Facility Operator explains the grievance process to each resident and representative in the resident's preferred communication method and gives a written copy. Receipt is recorded in the resident record.

The grievance process is posted in a common area of each home in large print and picture formats, and includes the Facility Operator's name and [PHONE], the Support Coordinator contact, the APD Regional Office contact and the Florida Abuse Hotline number 1-800-962-2873.

A resident or representative may complain orally, in writing, through an advocate, or by any communication method. Any staff member who hears a complaint accepts it respectfully, helps the person to put it in writing if wanted, and gives it to the Facility Operator by the end of the shift.

Staff screen every complaint at intake. If the complaint includes a known or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, the staff member immediately calls the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873, protects the resident, and informs the Facility Operator. The matter then follows BSP-03 and BSP-04 and not this process.
The Facility Operator enters each complaint on the grievance log the day it is received, noting the date, who complained, the issue and who received it.
The Facility Operator acknowledges the complaint to the resident or representative within 2 business days, in the resident's preferred communication method.
The Facility Operator reviews the complaint, talks with the resident and any staff involved, and tries to resolve it. Urgent concerns about health or safety are acted on the same day.
The Facility Operator gives a written or other accessible response within 10 business days stating what was found, what will be done and by when. The response is recorded in the log.

If the person is not satisfied, the Facility Operator refers the matter to [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] or the Governing Body for review within 10 further business days. The person is told that they may also contact APD or the Support Coordinator at any time.

Staff must not retaliate against, intimidate or treat any resident differently because of a complaint. The Facility Operator checks on the resident's experience in the weeks after a complaint. An allegation of retaliation is investigated as an incident under BSP-04 and may lead to discipline up to termination.
Staff help residents to file complaints, including writing, using communication devices or reaching an outside advocate. Staff must not discourage a complaint.
The Facility Operator records the outcome and the resident's satisfaction with it. Any change to services, house rules or staffing arising from a complaint is documented.
The Facility Operator reviews the grievance log at least quarterly for patterns and reports trends to the Governing Body as part of quality improvement (GOV-04).
Grievance records are kept in the resident record or a separate confidential file and retained for at least 6 years, in line with resident record retention (REC-01).

responsibilities.duty: Explains and posts the process, logs, investigates and answers complaints, and prevents retaliation.
Accept complaints, help residents file them, report to the Facility Operator and report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation to the Abuse Hotline immediately.
Reviews unresolved complaints and quarterly trends.
May complain at any time, in any form, without retaliation.

documentation: Grievance log with dates of receipt, acknowledgement, response and outcome
Written responses to complaints
Acknowledgment that the resident and representative received the process
Quarterly trend review reports
Incident reports for any retaliation allegations

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors, volunteers, residents, guardians and representatives
policies.purpose: To protect resident privacy and the confidentiality of resident information, and to make sure information is released only as permitted by law.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] protects resident privacy and the confidentiality of all resident information, as required by the right to privacy under s. 393.13, F.S., the record requirements of Rule 65G-2.009(5), F.A.C. and the HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164). Resident records are stored securely in the home's designated office area (Rule 65G-2.0072(4), F.A.C.). Information is released only as allowed by HIPAA and s. 393.13, F.S. and with the required consent. Copies of resident records are provided to APD within 2 calendar days on request (Rule 65G-2.009(5), F.A.C.). Residents have privacy in their bedrooms and bathrooms, and staff knock and wait before entering. Video monitoring follows the video monitoring policy (SDB-02), and any footage is restricted.

definitions.definition: Individually identifiable health information about a resident, in any form, held by [AGENCY NAME].
Using or disclosing only the least amount of information needed for the purpose.
A signed permission from the resident or the person with legal authority that allows release of specific information to a named person or entity.
An unauthorized acquisition, access, use or disclosure of PHI that compromises its privacy or security.

procedures: The Facility Operator is designated as [AGENCY NAME]'s privacy contact and is named in the notice of privacy practices. The contact details are [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] and [PHONE].
At admission, the Facility Operator gives each resident and representative the notice of privacy practices and explains it. Acknowledgment is signed and filed in the record.

Each employee, contractor and volunteer signs a confidentiality agreement at hire and completes privacy training at orientation and at least annually (STF-04). Records of this are filed in the personnel record.

Resident records are kept in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system in the home's designated office area, as required by Rule 65G-2.0072(4), F.A.C. Only staff who need the information for their duties have access.
Staff do not leave records, medication administration records, daily notes or screens with resident information open or visible in common areas, vehicles or public places.
Staff discuss resident information only in private and only with those who need to know. Staff do not discuss residents by name in public, on social media, or with other residents.
Before releasing information to any outside person, staff check with the Facility Operator that a valid signed authorization or a legal basis exists. The release is limited to the minimum necessary.

Information may be shared without authorization only where law allows, including for treatment and care coordination with the resident's health care providers, reports required by law (including to the Florida Abuse Hotline), and requests from APD or other regulators acting within their authority.
When APD requests copies of a resident's records, the Facility Operator provides them within 2 calendar days and logs the date and what was sent.

Staff protect resident privacy in daily care: knock and wait for a response before entering a bedroom or bathroom, close doors and curtains during personal care, and respect a resident's personal mail, calls and messages, except where a documented modification exists under IR-03.

Photographs, video and audio of residents are taken only with consent. Video monitoring is used only as set out in SDB-02. Footage is stored securely, viewed only by authorized staff for the stated purpose and not shared outside the home except as the law requires.
Residents and representatives may ask to see, copy and correct the resident's records. The Facility Operator responds within 30 calendar days and records the request and response.

A staff member who suspects a breach or improper disclosure reports it to the Facility Operator immediately. The Facility Operator investigates, takes steps to limit harm, notifies the resident and representative, and complies with any notification obligations under 45 CFR Part 164. The matter is logged as an incident (BSP-04).
Staff who violate this policy are subject to discipline up to termination.
When records are no longer needed, they are retained for the required period (REC-01) and then destroyed securely.

responsibilities.duty: Oversees privacy practices, authorizations, releases, breach response and records access.
Keep information confidential, share only on a need-to-know basis, and report suspected breaches.
Ensures resources for secure storage and reviews breach reports.
May request access to and correction of records and complain about privacy concerns.

documentation: Notice of privacy practices acknowledgment
Signed employee confidentiality agreements and privacy training records
Authorizations for release of information and a release log
Log of record copies provided to APD with dates
Breach and privacy incident reports
Requests for record access or amendment and responses

policies.title: Personal Funds and Property Management
policies.applies_to: All residents, guardians and representatives, and all staff with access to resident funds, account information or property
policies.purpose: To protect residents' money and belongings by setting written methods for managing and accounting for personal funds and benefits, ensuring the personal needs allowance, and keeping a property inventory.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 65G-2.009(4)(b), F.A.C. [AGENCY NAME] has written policies and procedures that set out the methods for management and accounting of any personal funds or benefits of residents. These procedures comply with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). Each staff member who has access to resident funds and account information is trained in these procedures before getting access and annually after that. Resident funds belong to the resident. They are never mixed with [AGENCY NAME] funds and are used only for the resident's benefit and according to the resident's wishes. A resident's personal needs allowance is at least 18% of the SSI federal benefit rate, which is $178.92 per month at the 2026 SSI rate of $994 (Rule 65G-2.018, F.A.C.). Separate accounting is kept for each resident. The APD room and board standard is $583.42 per month (Rule 65G-13.008, F.A.C.). A property inventory is kept for each resident as required by Rule 65G-2.009(3), F.A.C. Monthly reconciliations are signed by two staff and given to the resident and the representative.

definitions.definition: Any money or benefits belonging to a resident, including income, benefits, allowance and cash on hand.
The portion of a resident's income reserved for personal use, of at least 18% of the SSI federal benefit rate ($178.92 per month at the 2026 rate of $994).
The residential charge for housing and food, for which APD sets a standard of $583.42 per month and which is claimed on Form 65G-13.008A.
A dated written list of a resident's personal belongings of significant value or importance, completed at admission and kept up to date.
Generally accepted accounting principles, including separate accounts, documented transactions, supporting receipts and regular reconciliation.

procedures: At admission, the Facility Operator meets with the resident and the guardian, guardian advocate or representative to find out the resident's income and benefits, who manages the money, and the resident's wishes about spending and saving. This is recorded in the resident record.

Where [AGENCY NAME] manages any funds for a resident, the Facility Operator opens a separate account or ledger for that resident. Resident funds are never combined with [AGENCY NAME] operating funds or with another resident's funds.

[AGENCY NAME] makes sure each resident receives a monthly personal needs allowance of at least 18% of the SSI federal benefit rate, which is $178.92 at the 2026 rate of $994. The amount is updated when the SSI rate changes. The allowance is for the resident to spend as they choose.

Room and board charges are set consistent with the APD standard of $583.42 per month. No charge may reduce the resident's personal needs allowance below the minimum. The charge is explained to the resident and representative in writing at admission.

[AGENCY NAME] claims room and board on Form 65G-13.008A within 90 days after the end of the month. The Facility Operator or business office staff tracks the due date for each month and records the date submitted.
Staff record every deposit and withdrawal on the resident's ledger with date, amount, purpose and staff signature. A receipt or other supporting document is kept for every expenditure.

Cash held in the home for a resident is kept in a locked box accessible only to authorized staff. Cash is counted and signed by two staff at each handoff of the box and at least weekly, and the count is entered on the ledger.

Staff may not borrow from, lend to, accept gifts from or use a resident's money or property, and may not use a resident's debit card, accounts or personal identification. They may not co-sign or take financial benefits from a resident. A violation is reported to the Facility Operator immediately, and to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 if exploitation is suspected (BSP-03).

Residents choose how to spend their money. Staff support a resident's decisions and help with budgeting where asked. Any limit on a resident's access to their own money requires a person-centered modification under IR-03.

Within the first 30 days after admission, and each time a significant item is acquired or lost, staff complete or update a dated property inventory with the resident, and the resident and a staff member sign it. The inventory is kept in the resident record, as required by Rule 65G-2.009(3), F.A.C.

If a resident's property is lost, damaged or missing, staff report it to the Facility Operator the same day. The Facility Operator investigates, records the outcome, tells the resident and representative, and replaces or repays the item where [AGENCY NAME] is responsible. Suspected theft is handled under BSP-03 and BSP-04.
Each month, the Facility Operator or designated staff reconcile each resident's ledger against receipts, bank statements and cash on hand. Two staff members sign the reconciliation.
The signed monthly reconciliation is given to the resident and the guardian or representative within 10 days after month end in a format they can understand. Receipt is recorded.

[ADMINISTRATOR NAME] or a person outside of daily resident funds handling reviews each reconciliation at least quarterly and any discrepancy is investigated and recorded. Discrepancies that suggest theft or misuse are reported under BSP-03 and BSP-04.

Before getting access to resident funds or account information, each staff member is trained in these procedures, signs an acknowledgment, and repeats the training annually. The training is documented in the personnel record (STF-04, STF-06).

When a resident leaves, the Facility Operator returns all funds and belongings with a final accounting and a signed receipt from the resident or representative, using the property inventory to check, as set out in PCS-06.

responsibilities.duty: Keeps resident accounts and inventories, ensures the PNA is paid, makes reconciliations, trains staff and files the room and board claim on time.
Handle money only as trained, record every transaction, keep receipts and report discrepancies.
Reviews reconciliations quarterly and ensures independence from daily handling.
Direct how the resident's money is spent and review monthly statements.

Individual resident ledgers and receipts
Cash counts and signed handoff records
Monthly reconciliations signed by two staff and proof of delivery to resident and representative
Personal needs allowance records
Form 65G-13.008A room and board claim submission dates

policies.title: Informed Consent and Decision-Making Support
policies.applies_to: All residents, legal representatives, and all staff of the group home facility
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident decides for themselves wherever able, gets help understanding choices in plain language, and that consent is obtained from the right person and kept in the record before treatment, behavioral strategies, a Safety Plan or video monitoring.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] recognizes each resident's right under s. 393.13(3), F.S., to consent to or refuse treatment, subject to the authority of a guardian advocate (s. 393.12, F.S.) or a guardian (ch. 744, F.S.). A resident is presumed able to make their own decisions unless a court order or guardian advocate designation says otherwise. Staff support residents to understand their options in plain language and at their own pace. Where a legal representative holds decision-making authority, [AGENCY NAME] obtains that person's consent, still involves the resident, and respects the resident's expressed wishes. No behavioral program is implemented unless it has been reviewed as required by APD rule. Where [AGENCY NAME] uses reactive strategies, consent information is kept in the resident's record as required by Rule 65G-8.003, F.A.C. Consent to a Safety Plan and to video monitoring is obtained from the resident or legal representative before either is put in place. This policy supports the person-centered and rights-modification documentation requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c).

definitions.definition: Agreement to a treatment, intervention, plan or restriction given voluntarily after the person has received understandable information about its purpose, benefits, risks, alternatives and the right to refuse.
A court-appointed guardian (ch. 744, F.S.) or guardian advocate (s. 393.12, F.S.) with authority over the decision in question.
Help given to a resident to understand information, weigh choices and communicate a decision, without making the decision for them.
An emergency procedure used in response to behavior that poses imminent risk, governed by Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C. and BSP-02.

procedures: At admission, the Program Director asks the Waiver Support Coordinator and the resident's family for any guardianship, guardian advocate or other court documents and records who, if anyone, holds decision-making authority and over which decisions.

The Program Director files a copy of each court order or designation in the resident's record and flags the record with the legal representative's name and contact information. If no documents exist, the resident is treated as their own decision-maker.

Where decision-making authority is unclear or a resident appears to lack the ability to decide, the Program Director notifies the Waiver Support Coordinator and the APD Regional Office in writing so the proper process can be pursued. Staff do not decide for the resident in the meantime.

Before asking for any consent, the staff member explains the decision in plain language, using the resident's preferred communication method (words, pictures, devices, interpreter) and allowing time for questions. See IR-08.
The explanation covers what is proposed, why, expected benefits, risks, alternatives (including doing nothing), and that the resident may say no or change their mind.

Staff support the resident to take part in every decision, including those made by a legal representative, and record the resident's own views in the record even when they differ from the representative's.

Consent for medical treatment, medications and therapies is obtained by the nurse or Program Director from the resident or legal representative before the service begins and is documented on the consent form in the record.

If a resident with decision-making capacity refuses treatment, staff do not coerce, threaten or withhold privileges. The Program Director records the refusal, informs the prescriber or health care provider and the nurse, and offers alternatives or further explanation. See HW-02.

If a resident's legal representative refuses treatment that the health care provider believes is needed, the Program Director notifies the provider, the Waiver Support Coordinator and the APD Regional Office the same day and documents the contact.

Before any behavioral program is implemented, the Program Director confirms it has been reviewed as required by APD rule and that the resident or legal representative has consented in writing. See BSP-01.

Where reactive strategies may be used, the Program Director places the consent information required by Rule 65G-8.003, F.A.C. in the resident's record before any strategy is used and reviews it at least annually. See BSP-02.

Before a Safety Plan is put in place, the Program Director explains its safeguards to the resident and obtains consent from the resident or legal representative. The signed consent is filed in the record. See SDA-03.

Before video monitoring is started, the Administrator obtains written consent from the resident or legal representative, and affected roommates, as described in SDB-02. Monitoring does not begin without it.

Consent is revisited at each annual plan meeting and whenever the proposal changes materially, the resident withdraws agreement, or the legal representative changes. Updated consents are filed within 30 days of the change.

In a medical emergency where delay would endanger the resident, staff call 911 and follow HW-04. The Program Director notifies the resident's legal representative as soon as possible and documents what was done and why.
The Program Director trains all new staff on this policy during orientation and re-trains staff when a resident's decision-making status changes. Training is documented in the personnel record.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures this policy is carried out, obtains consent for video monitoring, and reviews rights concerns.
Verifies and records decision-making authority, obtains and files consents, and escalates unclear authority or refusals.
Explains treatment and medication choices and documents consent or refusal.
Support residents' understanding and decisions, never coerce, and report refusals or concerns to the Program Director.
Make decisions within their authority, with the resident's own wishes always considered.

Signed consent and refusal forms for treatment, medication and therapies

Notes on supported decision-making and the resident's expressed views
