Staff training sign-in sheets

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
policies.applies_to: All residents, applicants, family members, visitors and all staff of the group home facility
federal: Americans with Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.)
policies.purpose: To make sure no person is discriminated against in [AGENCY NAME]'s publicly funded program, and that every resident can communicate, understand information, vote and use the equipment they need.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not discriminate in admission, services or treatment on the basis of race, color, national origin, religion, sex, age, disability or any other protected characteristic, consistent with s. 393.13, F.S., the Americans with Disabilities Act and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act. [AGENCY NAME] provides interpreters, communication devices and accessible formats at no cost to residents and their representatives. Residents' voting rights are protected, and assistance is offered to those who want it. Specialized equipment required under Rule 65G-2.009(13), F.A.C. is kept in working order. Residents are never charged for language or communication access.

definitions.definition: Information presented so the person can use it, such as plain language, large print, Braille, audio, pictures, captioned video or an electronic format.
Equipment or an aid a person uses to understand or express themselves, such as a speech-generating device, picture board, hearing aid or amplifier.
A person able to interpret accurately and impartially between the resident and staff, including in sign language or a spoken language other than English.
Adaptive or medical equipment a resident uses, such as wheelchairs, lifts, communication devices or positioning supports.

procedures: The Administrator posts a nondiscrimination statement in the home and includes it in the admission packet, in plain language and in the languages and formats residents need.

At referral and admission, the Program Director asks the resident, family and Waiver Support Coordinator how the resident communicates, any language needs, hearing, vision and literacy needs, and any devices used. These are recorded in the resident record and the Individual Plan.

The Program Director arranges a qualified interpreter or alternate format at no cost when a resident or representative needs one. Family members and other residents are not used as interpreters unless the resident requests it and the choice is documented.
Staff learn each resident's communication methods during orientation and from a one-page communication profile kept in the resident record and shared at shift handoff. See PCS-04.

Staff give all rights notices, house rules, consent forms, grievance information and the Bill of Rights in a format the resident can understand, and confirm understanding by asking the resident to explain it back or show it in their own way.
Communication devices are kept charged, within the resident's reach and programmed. Staff do not remove or restrict a communication device except through the rights modification process in IR-03.

The Program Director inventories each resident's specialized equipment at admission and quarterly, records its condition, and checks it for working order. This covers equipment under Rule 65G-2.009(13), F.A.C.

Staff report broken, missing or ill-fitting equipment to the Program Director the same shift. The Program Director arranges repair or replacement through the supplier, the nurse or the Waiver Support Coordinator and documents the date requested and the date resolved.

While equipment is out of service, the Program Director puts a temporary alternative in place, such as a loaner or a manual back-up, and documents it, so the resident is not left without access or safe positioning.

Before each election, the Program Director asks every resident whether they wish to vote, helps with voter registration or address updates, and arranges mail ballot, early voting or election-day transportation. Staff do not tell residents how to vote or pressure them on any candidate or issue.

Residents who want help at the polls may choose the person who assists them. Staff help only when asked and only as the resident directs, and record that voting assistance was offered, not how the resident voted.

Any complaint that a resident was treated unfairly or denied communication access is handled under IR-04. The Administrator reviews the complaint within [NUMBER] business days and records the outcome.
The Administrator reviews admission and discharge decisions at least annually to check for patterns of discrimination, and reports the results to the governing body under GOV-04.
The Program Director trains all staff on nondiscrimination, communication access and equipment care at orientation and annually, and documents the training in personnel records.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the nondiscrimination statement, funds communication access at no cost to residents, and reviews complaints and annual patterns.
Identifies communication needs, arranges interpreters and formats, inventories equipment and organizes voting assistance.
Use each resident's communication method, keep equipment accessible and working, and report equipment problems the same shift.
Consults on positioning, adaptive and medical equipment needs and coordinates repairs.

documentation: Posted nondiscrimination statement and admission packet acknowledgement
Communication profile for each resident
Interpreter, device and accessible-format requests and how they were met
Specialized equipment inventory, condition checks, repair requests and resolution dates
Voting assistance offered and provided (not how the resident voted)
Complaint and review records
Staff training records

policies.title: Referral, Admission and Transition In
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Program Director, nurse and staff involved in referrals, admissions and new-resident transitions in the group home facility
policies.purpose: To make sure each person is admitted only after a referral, service authorization, review of history, and APD notification and approvals, so that the placement is safe for the person and for current residents and matches the facility's license.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] accepts referrals from Waiver Support Coordinators and APD Regional Offices. No services are provided and no one moves in before the service authorization is in place. [AGENCY NAME] applies the admission criteria in SDB-01, serves only residents whose characteristics match the license (Rule 65G-2.006(3), F.A.C.), notifies APD before accepting each new resident, and reports each census change in writing within 5 calendar days (Rule 65G-2.009(3) and Rule 65G-2.006(2), F.A.C.). This policy meets Rule 65G-2.009(3)(e)1-3, F.A.C.: (1) the facility ensures that a placement does not adversely affect the health, safety or welfare of current residents; (2) the facility obtains APD's approval before any placement that deviates from the criteria on the licensure application; and (3) the facility gives APD descriptive information on a prospective resident who is not an APD client, including intellectual or developmental disability documentation, medical needs, behavioral issues and known criminal history.

definitions.definition: APD's approval of Residential Habilitation for a named person under the iBudget waiver, issued before services begin.
Any admission, discharge, transfer or death that changes the number or identity of residents in the home.
A written plan of safeguards for a resident whose history or behavior creates a risk to others, including sexual-behavior risks. See SDA-03.
The resident characteristics (such as age, sex, support level and medical or behavioral needs) that APD approved for the home on its license.

procedures: The Administrator receives referrals only from Waiver Support Coordinators and APD Regional Offices (or, for a person not yet an APD client, from the referring party identified in Step 7) and logs each referral with the date, source and person's name.

The Program Director screens the referral against the license: licensed capacity and vacancy, approved resident characteristics, the home's physical accessibility, and the person's support level (Basic, Minimal, Moderate, Extensive 1 or Extensive 2) and any behavior-focus or intensive-behavior designation. If the person does not match the license, the referral is declined in writing with the reason (Rule 65G-2.006(3), F.A.C.).

The Program Director confirms [AGENCY NAME] can meet the minimum direct-care hours per resident per 24 hours for the person's support level (Basic 2, Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8, Extensive 2 11) and that staff are or will be trained for any behavior focus. See STF-01.

The Program Director requests and reviews the person's records: support plan, psychosocial and medical history, medications, behavior history, any Behavior Analyst or behavior support plan, any court orders on guardianship, and any Safety Plan. The nurse reviews health and medication information.

The Program Director and Waiver Support Coordinator arrange a visit and a meeting with the person and their family or representative so the person can see the home, meet staff and housemates, and voice preferences. See IR-07 for consent and decision-making.

Before acceptance, the Program Director assesses whether the placement would adversely affect the health, safety or welfare of current residents, including compatibility with housemates and the effect of the person's behavioral, medical or Safety Plan needs on the home (Rule 65G-2.009(3)(e)1, F.A.C.). The assessment and conclusion are written in the admission file.

If the person is not an APD client, the Administrator gives APD, before the placement, descriptive information on the person: documentation of the intellectual or developmental disability, medical needs, behavioral issues and any known criminal history (Rule 65G-2.009(3)(e)3, F.A.C.). A copy of what was sent and the date is kept in the admission file.

If the placement would deviate from the criteria on the licensure application, the Administrator submits a written request to the APD Regional Office and waits for written approval before accepting the person (Rule 65G-2.009(3)(e)2, F.A.C.). A copy of the approval is kept in the admission file.

Where a Safety Plan applies or there is a history of risk to others, the Administrator obtains APD approval of roommate matching before any room assignment, and the Program Director makes sure the Safety Plan safeguards are in place on the first day. See SDA-03.

The Administrator verifies in writing that the service authorization is in place and the Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement (AHCA Form 5000-3553) is in effect for [AGENCY NAME]. No services begin and no move-in date is set until then.

The Administrator notifies the APD Regional Office in writing before accepting the resident, using [AGENCY NAME]'s notice form, and records the date, method and APD's response (Rule 65G-2.009(3), F.A.C.).

On or before move-in, the Program Director completes the admission agreement or lease equivalent, an inventory of the person's personal property, the Bill of Rights, house rules and grievance information, each given in a form the person understands. See IR-01, IR-02, IR-04 and IR-06.

Staff prepare the person's room with the person's input and have medications, orders, dietary needs, equipment and the communication profile ready on day one. The nurse reconciles medications on the day of admission. See HW-01.

The Administrator reports the census change in writing to the APD Regional Office within 5 calendar days of the admission (Rule 65G-2.009(3) and Rule 65G-2.006(2), F.A.C.) and keeps the report in the admission file.

During the first 30 days, the Program Director checks in with the new resident and the Waiver Support Coordinator at least weekly, adjusts supports and schedules the person-centered planning meeting. See PCS-02.

responsibilities.duty: Decides acceptance, notifies APD before admission, obtains approvals for deviations and roommate matching, and files the 5-day census report.
Screens referrals, assesses effect on current residents, coordinates the transition and completes admission paperwork.
Reviews medical history, reconciles medications and plans health supports for admission.

responsibilities.role: Waiver Support Coordinator / APD Regional Office
responsibilities.duty: Make referrals, issue service authorization and approve exceptions.
Welcome the resident, follow the transition plan and report early concerns to the Program Director.

Declination letter, where applicable
Admission file with history review, written assessment of effect on current residents, and Safety Plan (if any)
Information sent to APD for non-APD clients
APD written approval for any deviation from licensure criteria and for roommate matching
Service authorization and Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement (AHCA Form 5000-3553) verification
Written pre-admission notice to APD

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning and the Individual Plan
policies.applies_to: Program Director, nurse, Behavior Analyst or clinician (where applicable), direct support staff and each resident in the group home facility
policies.purpose: To make sure each resident has an implementation plan developed with them that reflects their goals, preferences and choices, is tied to their support plan, and is reported on regularly to the support coordinator.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] writes an implementation plan for each resident, with the resident, tied to the goals in the resident's support plan, as required by the iBudget Waiver Services Coverage and Limitations Handbook (Rule 59G-13.070, F.A.C., p. 2-48). The plan records the resident's preferences and choices and any modification of rights. Any modification of a resident's rights in a provider-owned or controlled setting must have documented person-centered justification as required by 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4). [AGENCY NAME] files quarterly summaries and an annual report with the resident's Waiver Support Coordinator as the Handbook requires. For residents with a behavior focus or intensive behavioral designation, [AGENCY NAME] meets the Handbook's monitoring and staff training requirements.

definitions.definition: The plan developed by the resident and their Waiver Support Coordinator that sets the resident's goals and authorized services.
The provider's written plan describing how the residential habilitation supports will help the resident reach the support plan goals.
Any limit on a right or HCBS setting protection that is supported by a specific assessed need and documented person-centered justification. See IR-03.
APD designations for residential habilitation serving residents with significant behavioral needs, which carry added monitoring and training requirements.

procedures: Within [NUMBER] days of admission and before the first implementation plan is finalized, the Program Director obtains the resident's current support plan from the Waiver Support Coordinator and files it in the record.

The Program Director schedules the planning meeting at a time and place the resident chooses and invites the people the resident wants, including family, legal representative, Waiver Support Coordinator, nurse and key staff.

The Program Director prepares in advance a plain-language, accessible summary of the support plan goals, and uses the resident's preferred communication method during the meeting. See IR-07 and IR-08.

At the meeting, the resident states what is important to them (routines, relationships, interests, work, community, food, privacy, and what they want to change). The Program Director records the resident's own words wherever possible.
Together they write an implementation plan that ties each support plan goal to specific supports, who provides them, how often, how success will be measured and the resident's role.
The plan records the resident's preferences and choices, including daily schedule, bedroom and roommate choice, visitors, food, activities, and community and employment choices. See PCS-05.

If a proposed support would limit any right or HCBS setting protection, the Program Director does not include it in the plan until the rights modification steps in IR-03 are completed. The plan then records the specific assessed need, the positive interventions tried, less intrusive methods tried, the data collection plan, review schedule, consent and assurance of no harm, consistent with 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4).

For a resident with a behavior focus or intensive behavioral designation, the Program Director confirms that the monitoring required by the Handbook (a Board Certified Behavior Analyst or a Chapter 490/491 professional) is in place, that the behavior support plan is attached, and that staff are trained as the Handbook requires. See BSP-01 and STF-04.

The resident (or legal representative) signs the plan or documents their agreement in another way. The Program Director gives them a copy in an accessible format and sends a copy to the Waiver Support Coordinator.
The Program Director briefs all staff on the plan and posts a short summary of the resident's supports in the staff-only area of the home. Staff sign that they have read it. See PCS-04.

The Program Director prepares a quarterly summary for each resident from the daily documentation, covering progress, setbacks, health, incidents, community participation and any rights modifications, and sends it to the Waiver Support Coordinator by the due date set in the Handbook.
The Program Director prepares the annual report in time for the resident's annual plan meeting and sends it to the Waiver Support Coordinator. The report is filed in the resident record.
The plan is revised with the resident whenever goals change, a major event or change of condition occurs, or the resident asks for a change. Revisions are filed within 30 days of the new information.
The Administrator reviews a sample of plans, quarterly summaries and annual reports each quarter for timeliness and person-centered content and reports findings under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Leads planning meetings, writes and updates implementation plans, and prepares quarterly summaries and annual reports.
Directs the planning process to the extent they choose, states preferences and agrees to or changes the plan.
Provides the support plan, takes part in planning and receives quarterly and annual reports.
Monitors and trains staff on behavior supports for residents with behavior focus or intensive designations.
Deliver the supports as written and document progress.
Ensures timely reports and reviews plan quality.

documentation: Support plan from the Waiver Support Coordinator
Signed implementation plan and revisions
Planning meeting notes with resident's preferences in their own words
Rights modification documentation under 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)
Behavior support plan and monitoring records for behavior-focus residents
Quarterly summaries and annual reports with dates sent
Staff read-and-sign sheets

policies.title: Implementation of Supports and Daily Documentation
policies.applies_to: Direct support staff, Program Director, nurse and Administrator of the group home facility
policies.purpose: To make sure supports are delivered as planned, each day's supports are documented against the implementation plan, medical appointments are followed up, records stay current, and service and authorization information is entered in APD iConnect.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] delivers the supports in each resident's implementation plan and documents them every day against that plan, as the iBudget Waiver Services Coverage and Limitations Handbook (Rule 59G-13.070, F.A.C.) requires. [AGENCY NAME] follows up on resident medical appointments as required by Rule 65G-2.009(1), F.A.C., and updates resident records within 30 days of receiving new information as required by Rule 65G-2.009(5), F.A.C. Documentation and authorizations are entered in APD iConnect. At least one staff member is present at all times when residents are in the facility, consistent with Rule 65G-2.009(6), F.A.C. and STF-01. Documentation is accurate, timely, factual and respectful, and is never completed in advance or altered after the fact.

definitions.definition: The written or electronic record, completed each day, of the supports provided to a resident, the resident's response and notable events.
APD's online system used by waiver providers for service authorizations, documentation and related provider functions.
An entry made after the event, clearly labeled with the actual date and time written and the date and time of the event.

procedures: At the start of each shift, staff read the resident's current implementation plan summary, the shift communication log and any new orders, and sign that they have done so. See PCS-04.
Staff provide each resident's supports as written in the implementation plan, following the resident's own schedule and choices for the day, and offer alternatives when a resident declines.

Each day, the staff member who provides the support completes the daily note for the resident before leaving the shift. The note records the supports provided, which plan goals they relate to, the resident's participation and response, community activities, mood or behavior notes, and any refusals with the reason given.

Entries are factual, signed with full name or initials and the date and time, and written in ink or in the approved electronic system. Errors are corrected by a single line and initials, or an audit-tracked electronic edit, never by erasure or deletion.

Staff record every medical appointment in the resident's record when scheduled. After each visit, staff document the provider seen, findings, orders, medication changes and follow-up needed, and give the paperwork to the nurse the same day.

The nurse and Program Director track each follow-up (labs, referrals, return visits, treatments) on a follow-up log until it is completed. Overdue follow-ups are escalated to the Program Director within one business day. See HW-02.
Staff tell the Program Director the same shift of any significant change in the resident's condition, behavior or routine, and incident reporting is completed under HW-04 and BSP-04.

When new information arrives (new orders, evaluations, court orders, plan changes, contact changes), the Program Director updates the resident's record within 30 days of receiving it, and notes the date received and the date filed.

The Program Director reviews each resident's daily notes at least weekly against the implementation plan, and signs the review. Gaps, missing entries or supports not delivered are addressed with the staff member within two business days.

The Program Director keeps a monthly attendance record showing each resident's days in the home, so the correct billing rate (monthly rate for 24 or more days in the home, otherwise the daily rate) is used. See GOV-05.

The Administrator or designee enters the required service documentation and authorization information in APD iConnect, and confirms that service authorizations are current and match the services delivered. Entries are made by the due dates set by APD.
Late entries are allowed only when labeled as such and signed. Staff never document a support that was not provided or pre-chart.

The Program Director completes a monthly record audit of a sample of resident records, covering daily notes, appointment follow-up, 30-day updates and iConnect entries, and reports results to the Administrator for review under GOV-04.
The Program Director uses the daily documentation to prepare quarterly summaries and the annual report. See PCS-02.

responsibilities.duty: Deliver supports as written and complete accurate daily notes before the end of each shift.
Reviews daily notes weekly, keeps records updated within 30 days of new information and tracks follow-up.
Tracks medical appointment follow-up and communicates orders to staff.
Ensures iConnect entries and authorizations are current and that records audits are completed.

documentation: Daily notes for each resident
Shift communication log with staff sign-off
Medical appointment log and follow-up tracker
Record update log showing dates information was received and filed
Weekly daily-note review sign-offs
Monthly attendance record
APD iConnect entries and authorization verification
Monthly record audit results

policies.title: Shift Communication and Staff Handoff
policies.applies_to: All direct support staff, the Program Director, nurse and Administrator of the group home facility
policies.purpose: To make sure recent incidents and important resident information are passed in writing to staff on later shifts, and that every shift reviews the information.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written system to communicate recent incidents and resident information to staff on subsequent shifts. This policy meets Rule 65G-2.009(15)(a)1-2, F.A.C.: (1) a mechanism for documenting in writing the information staff should know, including medical or behavioral incidents and physician or therapist orders; and (2) a procedure to ensure the information is reviewed across all shifts, with staff sign-off. Verbal reports alone are not sufficient. No staff member starts work with residents until they have reviewed the communication log.

definitions.definition: The written (paper or electronic) record kept in the home where staff enter incidents, orders and resident information for later shifts.
The transfer of responsibility and information from outgoing to incoming staff at a shift change.
A signature or electronic acknowledgement, with date and time, that a staff member has read and understood the entries.

procedures: The Program Director sets up and maintains one shift communication log for the home, kept in a consistent, secure location (or approved electronic system) accessible to staff on all shifts and protected from access by visitors. See IR-05.

Throughout the shift, the staff on duty write in the log any medical or behavioral incident, injury, illness, medication change or refusal, physician or therapist order, new or changed procedure, appointment, family contact, equipment problem, safety concern and visitor or schedule change that later staff should know.

Each entry includes the date and time, the resident's name or initials as the home's system defines, a factual description, any action taken, any follow-up needed and who wrote it. Entries use objective language, not opinions or labels.

When a physician or therapist order is received, the nurse or staff who receives it enters it in the log on the same shift, and the nurse places the full written order in the resident record. See HW-02.

Incidents requiring a report are entered in the log with a note that a report is being completed under BSP-04 or HW-04. Details required to be kept confidential are not written in the log, and staff are directed to the incident report instead.

Before leaving, the outgoing staff member confirms the log is complete and gives a verbal handoff to the incoming staff member in person, covering each resident's condition, priority tasks and anything urgent. Staff do not leave residents without an on-duty staff member present. See STF-01.

When the incoming staff member arrives, before taking responsibility for residents, they read all log entries since their last shift on duty (and any entries marked as standing instructions), and sign and date the log to show they have reviewed them.
Staff returning after more than [NUMBER] days off read all entries made during their absence, and the Program Director summarizes significant changes for them at the start of the shift.
Staff who have a question about an entry ask the outgoing staff member, the nurse or the Program Director before acting, and record the clarification in the log.

The Program Director reviews the log at least [NUMBER] times per week, checks that every shift has signed off, confirms that orders in the log match the resident records and follows up on missed sign-offs with the staff member within one business day.
When an entry shows a change in a resident's needs, the Program Director updates the resident's implementation plan summary and tells all staff at the next shift change. See PCS-02 and PCS-03.
Completed log pages or electronic exports are kept and retained with the facility's records according to REC-01. Staff do not tear out, white out or delete entries.

The Administrator reviews the log system at least quarterly for completeness and timeliness of sign-off and addresses gaps through staff coaching or re-training. The review is documented under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Record information for later shifts, give a verbal handoff and read and sign the log before starting work.
Enters physician and therapist orders and health information on the same shift they are received.
Maintains the log, audits sign-offs and corrects missed reviews.
Reviews the system at least quarterly and ensures staff are trained on it.

documentation: Shift communication log with dated, timed and signed entries
Staff sign-off for each shift review
Program Director review notes and follow-up on missed sign-offs
Quarterly log review under GOV-04
Staff training record on the handoff procedure

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
policies.applies_to: All residents, direct support professionals, the Program Director, and the Administrator of [AGENCY NAME] group home(s)
policies.purpose: To ensure each resident has real and regular opportunities to take part in community life, social interaction, exercise, recreation and work, as the resident chooses. This also keeps the home operating as a community-based setting under the HCBS settings rule.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides opportunities for community activities as required by Rule 65G-2.009(2), F.A.C. Under s. 393.13(3), F.S., each resident may take part in social interaction, exercise, recreation, religious activity and community participation. Residents choose their daily activities, including whether to work and where. Staff support those choices and do not substitute their own. Under 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4), the home is not an isolating setting. Residents have access to visitors and food, and may make choices about their schedules and activities. Any limit on a resident's access to the community or to these choices is a rights modification. It may be used only with a documented person-centered justification and must follow IR-03 (Rights Restrictions and Due Process). Staffing shortages, convenience, group outings that suit staff, and house rules are never acceptable reasons to keep a resident home. Residents who want to work are supported to explore integrated, competitive employment in the community, and may also choose other options such as volunteering or day activities.

definitions.definition: A place in the community where people with and without disabilities take part together, such as a workplace, library, place of worship, store, park or club.
Work in the community for pay at or above minimum wage, alongside people without disabilities, with supports as needed.
Any outing or event outside the home that the resident chooses, including shopping, recreation, worship, classes, volunteering, visiting friends or family, and work.
Any limit on a right or setting condition under 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4). It requires a documented person-centered justification and is handled under IR-03.

procedures: At admission and at each annual plan meeting, the Program Director interviews the resident, and the legal representative and support coordinator where applicable. The interview asks about interests, routines, faith, friends, family, past and desired work, and places the resident wants to go. The answers are recorded in the person-centered plan (PCS-02).

The Program Director works with the resident to prepare a weekly activity schedule built on the resident's own choices. It includes community activities, exercise or recreation, social time and any work or volunteer activity. The schedule is written in plain language or a format the resident understands (IR-08), and the resident gets a copy.

Direct support professionals (DSPs) offer community activities every week to every resident. A resident may decline any activity. DSPs record offers and refusals, and report to the Program Director when a resident repeatedly declines so the team can look for the cause.

The Program Director reviews the staffing schedule each week against the activity schedule. Staff are assigned so that scheduled community activities can occur while the minimum staffing in STF-01 stays in place at the home. Activities are not cancelled because of staffing without Administrator approval and a documented make-up plan.
Residents who need a different activity, time or companion from housemates have that supported when possible. The home does not require group-only outings, and individual preferences are honored.

The Program Director asks each adult resident at intake and at every annual plan meeting whether he or she wants to work, volunteer, or look into integrated employment. The question and the answer, including 'no,' are documented. Employment is never required, and a decision not to work is respected and may be revisited at any time.

When a resident expresses interest in work, the Program Director notifies the support coordinator within 5 business days and asks for referral to employment supports available to the resident. The Program Director then helps the resident with logistics, including transportation (HES-05), a schedule that allows the work, and any adaptations the resident needs.

DSPs provide the day-to-day supports the resident needs to attend work, school or volunteer activities, as written in the plan. These include transportation, reminders, personal care, meals and medications at the workplace as ordered (HW-01).

Staff support residents to keep and build relationships with family and friends, and to take part in faith or cultural activities they choose. Visitors are welcome under IR-02 (House Rules) and IR-01.
Residents have access to exercise and recreation as their health allows. DSPs follow any limits set by the resident's practitioner (HW-03).

Any proposed limit on community access, visitors, schedules or other setting conditions is sent to the Program Director before it takes effect. It is allowed only after the process in IR-03 is complete, including documentation of the assessed need, less intrusive methods tried, and the resident's or representative's informed consent. Without that, the limit is not applied.

Safety concerns about a specific outing or workplace are handled through individualized supports written into the plan and not through blanket restrictions. If a safety risk requires a plan change, the team meets under PCS-02.

The Program Director reviews each resident's activity log monthly. If a resident has had fewer community activities than the schedule provides, or has not left the home for an extended time, the Program Director identifies the cause and records a corrective action within 5 business days.

The Administrator reviews a summary of community participation and employment interest quarterly, as part of the quality review in GOV-04. The review is also used to find residents whose participation has dropped and to guide changes to staffing, transportation and activity options.

Staff who see a resident being kept from the community without the proper process, or being pressured about work, report it to the Program Director or Administrator. A resident or representative who feels choices are not honored may file a grievance under IR-04.

responsibilities.duty: Ensure staffing, transportation and budgets support community participation and employment choice. Review quarterly participation data. Approve any modification only after IR-03 is complete.
Interview residents, build activity schedules, document employment interest, coordinate with support coordinators, review activity logs monthly, and take corrective action.
Offer and support community activities every week, honor residents' choices, record offers, refusals and participation, and report barriers or restrictions.
Share preferences and choose activities, work and visitors. Raise concerns about access.
Help arrange employment supports and community resources and take part in plan meetings.

documentation: Person-centered plan sections on interests, community activities and employment preference
Weekly activity schedule for each resident
Daily activity log showing offers, refusals and participation (PCS-03)
Employment interest record and referral notification to the support coordinator
Monthly Program Director activity review and corrective actions
Rights modification documentation under IR-03, if any
Quarterly community participation summary (GOV-04)

policies.title: Transition, Discharge and Termination of Services
policies.applies_to: All residents, the Administrator, Program Director, support staff, and business office staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure that when a resident moves, is transferred, is discharged or has services terminated, or when the home closes, the change is safe and orderly. It must follow the written termination procedures, Chapter 65G-3, F.A.C., and APD notice requirements, and the resident's property and funds must be returned.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 65G-2.009(3)(a), F.A.C.: [AGENCY NAME] has written criteria and procedures for the admission and termination of residential services, and its termination procedures are consistent with Chapter 65G-3, F.A.C. The admission criteria are in SDB-01 and PCS-01. This policy and SDB-01 together form the written termination criteria and procedures. Services are ended only for a reason stated in SDB-01, such as a change in the resident's needs or characteristics that no longer matches the home's license (Rule 65G-2.006(3)), a resident's or representative's request, or a health or safety need that the home cannot meet. A transfer to another home or provider requires approval as provided in Rule 65G-2.009(3). The census change is reported to APD in writing before it occurs and updated within 5 calendar days. The resident's property is returned according to the property inventory, and personal funds are accounted for and returned under Rule 65G-2.009(4) and IR-06. [AGENCY NAME] gives APD 30 days' written notice before closing a home (Rule 65G-2.002(13)). The resident's rights, dignity and continuity of care are protected throughout.

definitions.definition: The end of residential services at the home, whether the resident chooses to leave or the home ends services.
A move of a resident from one APD-licensed residence or provider to another.
Any change in the number or identity of residents living in the home, including admission, discharge, transfer or death.
The written list of a resident's belongings made at admission and updated as items are added or removed.
A written plan, made with the resident, representative and support coordinator, for the move and the continuation of supports.

procedures: When any person raises the possibility of a move, discharge or termination, including the resident, the legal representative, the support coordinator, a physician or staff, the Program Director notifies the Administrator the same business day and documents the reason in the resident's record.

The Administrator and Program Director first review whether added supports, plan changes (PCS-02), behavioral supports (BSP-01), or health supports can resolve the concern, and document that review. The resident, representative and support coordinator take part in it.

If services will end at the home's initiative, the Administrator confirms that the reason fits the written criteria in SDB-01. Written notice is then given to the resident, the legal representative and the support coordinator, in a format the resident can understand (IR-08), stating the reason and the proposed date. Notice is given in the manner and within the time required by Chapter 65G-3, F.A.C., including any rights to appeal or review it provides.

The Program Director invites the resident, the representative, the support coordinator and, where relevant, the behavior analyst and nurse to a transition meeting. The meeting covers the resident's choice of destination, supports needed, medications, diet, equipment, communication needs, transport and who will do what.

If the move is a transfer, the Administrator seeks approval under Rule 65G-2.009(3) before the move takes place and records the approval in the resident's record. A transfer does not occur until approval is documented.

The Administrator reports the census change to the APD Regional Office in writing before it occurs. Within 5 calendar days of the change, the Administrator sends the written update confirming the date and outcome. Copies are kept in the resident's record and the census file.
The Administrator confirms that the move keeps the home's population within the licensed capacity and resident characteristics (Rule 65G-2.006) and updates the census tracking sheet (GOV-07).

Before the move, the Program Director prepares a transition packet for the receiving provider or family, consistent with consent in IR-05 and IR-07. It includes the current plan, support needs, medication list and last 30 days of the medication administration record, health information and appointments, protocols (seizure, choking, behavior), emergency contacts, legal documents, and the resident's preferences and routines.

The nurse or designated staff reconcile medications with the prescriber's orders. Medications, supplies and specialized equipment that belong to the resident go with the resident, with a signed list of what was sent (HW-01).

Staff and the resident, with the representative if applicable, go through the property inventory together. Each item is checked off and returned. Missing or damaged items are documented, and the Administrator investigates and resolves them in writing. The resident or representative signs for the items received.

The business office completes a final account of the resident's personal funds under IR-06 and Rule 65G-2.009(4). The balance is returned by the move date, or as soon after as possible when a check must be issued, to the resident or representative. A signed receipt is obtained.

Staff help the resident say goodbye to housemates and staff in the way the resident prefers, and arrange transport. The Program Director or a designee makes a follow-up contact within 7 days after the move to confirm the transition is going well and records the result.

If the resident is discharged in an emergency, such as a hospitalization or an imminent safety risk, the Administrator notifies the support coordinator, the representative and the APD Regional Office as soon as possible. The Administrator then completes the written census report within 5 calendar days and follows the remaining steps in this policy.
The Program Director closes the record in accordance with REC-01, retains it for the required period, and sends the required copies to APD on request.

If [AGENCY NAME] decides to close a home, the Administrator gives APD written notice at least 30 days before closing (Rule 65G-2.002(13)). The Administrator also notifies each resident, representative and support coordinator in writing at the same time and prepares transition plans for each resident under this policy.
The Administrator reviews each termination or transfer at the next quality review (GOV-04) to find patterns and prevent avoidable moves.

responsibilities.duty: Decide on terminations consistent with criteria and Chapter 65G-3, obtain transfer approval, send census reports to APD, give 30-day closure notice, and sign off on property and funds return.
Lead the transition meeting, prepare the transition packet, coordinate with the support coordinator, complete the property inventory check and follow-up.
Reconcile medications and send medications, supplies and equipment with the resident.
Prepare the final accounting of personal funds and return the balance.
Help identify the new setting and coordinate services across providers.
Take part in decisions, receive notice, and sign for property and funds.

documentation: Written reason for discharge, transfer or termination, and notice to the resident, representative and support coordinator
Record of review of alternatives
Transition meeting notes and transition plan
APD transfer approval
Written census change reports and the 5-calendar-day update
Transition packet contents list and medication transfer list
Signed property inventory return
Final personal funds accounting and receipt
Follow-up contact note
APD 30-day written closure notice and resident notices, when a home closes

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Certification
policies.applies_to: All direct support professionals who assist with or administer medication, the Program Director, nursing consultant and Administrator of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To ensure residents get the right medication safely and as ordered, and that only trained, validated staff give or supervise medication, as required by Rule 65G-2.009(12), s. 393.506, F.S., and Chapter 65G-7, F.A.C.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 65G-2.009(12)(a)-(g), F.A.C. (Medication). [AGENCY NAME] (1) administers medication only according to the health care practitioner's written order; (2) keeps medication in its original labeled container; (3) stores medication locked, accessible only to staff; (4) keeps a daily medication administration record (MAR) as required by Chapter 65G-7; (5) administers, documents, stores and reports errors according to ss. 393.13 and 393.506, F.S., and Chapter 65G-7; (6) retrains staff on an ongoing basis when medication errors occur; and (7) conveys adverse reactions immediately to the prescriber or other medical professional. Unlicensed staff may supervise self-administration or administer medication only after completing the APD Basic Medication Administration course (exam score of at least 85%, and 100% on the MAR section), and validation by an approved validator. They must complete an annual update and be revalidated, and revalidate within the 60 days before their validation expires. Under s. 393.506, F.S., they must also complete an annual 2-hour in-service on medication administration and error prevention. A staff member whose certification, revalidation or in-service lapses does not give medication until the requirement is met. Under s. 393.506, a provider who misses revalidation or the in-service must repeat the initial course.

definitions.definition: Medication Administration Record. The daily record of each medication given, refused or missed, with the staff member's initials.

An approved validator's onsite observation of a staff member administering medication to an actual resident with an actual medication. It is done initially and annually for oral, enteral, ophthalmic, rectal and inhaled routes. Otic, transdermal and topical routes are validated by simulation in the initial course.
Any deviation from the practitioner's order, including wrong resident, drug, dose, route or time, an omitted dose, or a failure to document.
An unwanted or harmful response to a medication.
A resident taking his or her own medication, with staff supervising as the plan allows.

procedures: Before staff give any medication, the Program Director confirms and records that the staff member holds current APD Basic Medication Administration certification, current validation for each route they will use, and a completed annual in-service. A roster of certified and validated staff, with expiration dates, is kept at the home and updated by the Program Director.

Staff complete the initial course of at least 6 hours by an agency-approved trainer under s. 393.506, F.S., and the APD Basic Medication Administration course. The passing score is at least 85% on the exam and 100% on the MAR section. A staff member who does not pass does not give medication.

An approved validator then validates the staff member onsite, with an actual resident and actual medication, for oral, enteral, ophthalmic, rectal and inhaled routes. Otic, transdermal and topical routes are validated by simulation in the initial course. The validation record is placed in the personnel file (STF-06).

The Program Director tracks every expiration date. The staff member must be revalidated within the 60 days before the validation expires and must complete the annual update. The Program Director sends a reminder 90 days before each date and removes a staff member from medication duty on the day any certification expires.

Each staff member completes the annual 2-hour in-service on medication administration and error prevention. If a staff member misses revalidation or the in-service, he or she stops giving medication and repeats the initial course before returning to medication duty.

Medication is given only on the written order of a health care practitioner. Staff do not accept verbal orders or change a dose, time or route on their own. Each new or changed order is written, entered on the MAR, and checked against the pharmacy label by two staff members when possible, or by the nurse consultant (HW-02).
Medication is kept in the original labeled container from the pharmacy or manufacturer. Staff never transfer, mix or pre-pour medications into other containers for later use.

All medications are stored locked, and only staff can open the storage. Keys are held by the staff member on duty. Medications requiring refrigeration are kept in a locked container or refrigerator. Residents may not access others' medications. Controlled substances are counted and signed for at each shift change (PCS-04).

Before each administration, the staff member checks the resident's identity, the MAR, the label, and the written order: the right resident, medication, dose, route, time, and documentation. The staff member observes the resident taking the medication.

Staff initial the MAR immediately after giving each dose, not before and not at the end of the shift. If a dose is refused, held, or missed, the staff member records the reason on the MAR and notifies the Program Director and the prescriber as the order or protocol directs.

When a resident self-administers, staff supervise according to the plan and the practitioner's order, record on the MAR that the resident took the medication, and report concerns to the Program Director.

Staff convey any suspected adverse reaction immediately to the prescriber or another medical professional, and call 911 for any life-threatening symptoms (HW-04). They record the reaction, the time of the call and the instruction received, and inform the Program Director, the legal representative and the support coordinator.

When a medication error occurs, staff immediately check on the resident, contact the prescriber or poison control as needed and follow instructions, record the error, and notify the Program Director the same shift. Errors are reported as required by Chapter 65G-7, F.A.C., and, if the error is a reportable incident, under BSP-04 and REC-02.

Within 3 business days after each error, the Program Director reviews it with the staff member to find the cause. The staff member is retrained and, as needed, reobserved by the validator or trainer. The retraining is documented. Repeated errors lead to removal from medication duty until the staff member is revalidated.
The Program Director reviews each MAR weekly for gaps or errors, and the nurse consultant reviews them as scheduled under HW-02. Medication errors and trends are reviewed quarterly in GOV-04.

Expired, discontinued or unused medication is disposed of or returned according to Chapter 65G-7 and pharmacy guidance, with two staff members documenting it. The Program Director keeps the disposal record.

responsibilities.duty: Ensure only certified and validated staff give medication, provide for training and validation resources, and review error trends.
Maintain the certification roster and expiration tracking, audit MARs weekly, review and document errors and retraining.
Follow orders and the five checks, document each dose immediately, store medication locked, report errors and reactions at once.
Review orders and MARs, advise on medication questions, and support staff retraining (HW-02).
Provide written orders and labeled medication, and respond to questions and reports of reactions.

documentation: Staff medication certification, exam scores, validation records and in-service records (personnel file)
Certification and expiration roster
Practitioner written orders
Daily MAR for each resident
Controlled substance counts
Medication error reports, follow-up review and retraining records
Adverse reaction notes and prescriber contact record
Medication disposal records

policies.title: Nursing Oversight and Health Care Coordination
policies.applies_to: All residents, direct support professionals, Program Director, nurse consultant and Administrator of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To coordinate each resident's health care. This includes routine and specialty appointments, follow-up of recommendations, communication of health changes, use of licensed nurses for skilled needs, and maintenance of specialized equipment.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] makes sure residents get routine and specialty health care and that appointment recommendations are followed up (Rule 65G-2.009(1), F.A.C.). Residential Habilitation under the iBudget waiver is a non-nursing service. Direct support professionals do not perform nursing tasks. When a resident has a skilled need, [AGENCY NAME] uses a licensed nurse or other licensed provider, arranged through the resident's practitioner and support coordinator. Health changes are shared promptly with the resident's support coordinator, legal representative and prescribers. Specialized equipment is maintained so it works safely (Rule 65G-2.009(13)). Residents and representatives make health decisions as set out in IR-07, and the home supports their choices.

definitions.definition: A service delivered by trained staff that does not require a licensed nurse, such as personal care, supervision, and medication administration by validated staff.

A health task that, by law or practitioner order, must be done by a licensed nurse or other licensed professional, for example injections or wound care beyond basic first aid, unless a practitioner delegates it as the law allows.
Scheduling appointments, providing transport and information, carrying out orders, and communicating results and changes to the team.
Resident-specific items such as wheelchairs, lifts, feeding pumps, oxygen, communication devices, and orthotics.

procedures: At admission, the Program Director gathers each resident's health information, including diagnoses, practitioners, allergies, medications, diet, protocols, equipment, and immunizations. The information is placed in the record and shared with the nurse consultant.

The Administrator engages a licensed nurse (RN or LPN, as appropriate) as a consultant. The nurse reviews each resident's health needs at admission and at least quarterly, and advises on training, protocols and any change of condition.

The Program Director keeps a health calendar for each resident listing routine checkups, dental, vision, hearing, specialty and follow-up appointments, and scheduled labs. The calendar is reviewed weekly.

The Program Director schedules appointments, arranges transport (HES-05), and assigns a staff member who knows the resident to attend, unless the resident or representative prefers otherwise. The staff member brings the medication list, protocols and the resident's current health information.
At each appointment, staff ask the practitioner for written instructions, orders, and follow-up dates, and record them in the resident's record on the same day.

Within 1 business day after each appointment, the Program Director reviews the instructions. New orders are entered on the MAR (HW-01) or into protocols. Referrals and follow-up visits are scheduled and added to the health calendar. Staff are briefed at the next shift handoff (PCS-04).

The Program Director tracks every recommendation until it is completed, declined by the resident or representative with a documented reason, or closed by the practitioner. Open items are reviewed weekly.

When staff observe a change in a resident's health, they follow HW-04 and notify the Program Director. The Program Director notifies the support coordinator and legal representative, and the nurse consultant when relevant, and informs prescribers as needed.

If a resident has a skilled need, the Program Director asks the practitioner and the support coordinator how it will be met, and arranges a licensed nurse or other licensed provider. Direct support professionals do not carry out the skilled task unless the law and a practitioner's written delegation allow it and they have been trained and validated for it. The arrangement is recorded in the plan.

The nurse consultant provides or arranges resident-specific training for staff on health protocols and equipment, and documents who was trained and when. The Program Director verifies competence before staff work independently with that resident.

For each item of specialized equipment, the Program Director records the vendor, maintenance requirements and cleaning schedule. Staff check the equipment each shift or as directed, and report any problem the same day. Broken or unsafe equipment is taken out of service and repaired or replaced, and the practitioner or vendor is contacted for interim supports.
Staff support residents to take part in decisions about their health care, with the information in a form they understand and with legal representative consent where needed (IR-07).
Health information is shared only as allowed by IR-05. Staff obtain valid authorizations before releasing information beyond treatment and coordination.

The nurse consultant reviews MARs, health records and protocols according to the schedule set by the Administrator. The nurse documents findings and recommendations, and the Program Director acts on them within 14 days.
Health coordination outcomes, such as missed appointments, overdue follow-ups, and equipment issues, are reported to the Administrator and reviewed quarterly in GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Engage the nurse consultant, ensure resources for care coordination, and review outcomes.
Schedule and track appointments and recommendations, update orders and protocols, arrange skilled services, and communicate changes.
Review health needs and records, train staff on protocols and equipment, and advise on health concerns.
Attend appointments, follow orders and protocols, report changes, and maintain equipment.
Receive health updates, arrange needed services, and make or consent to decisions as authorized.

documentation: Resident health profile and practitioner list
Health calendar and appointment log
Appointment summaries, orders and recommendation tracking log
Nurse consultant review notes and staff training records
Skilled service arrangements
Equipment maintenance and repair log
Notices to support coordinators and representatives about health changes

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
policies.applies_to: All residents, direct support professionals, Program Director, nurse consultant and Administrator of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To protect residents with seizure disorders, choking or aspiration risks and other health risks through individual protocols, trained staff, CPR and first aid readiness, and the use of ordered diets and equipment.
policies.policy: Each resident with a seizure, choking, aspiration or similar health risk has an individual health protocol that is part of the resident's plan. Staff follow those protocols exactly. At least one staff member who is CPR-certified is on site whenever residents are present, and all direct support professionals complete classroom CPR and first aid training within 90 days of hire (Rule 65G-2.008(7), F.A.C.). First aid is provided according to Rule 65G-2.009(11). Modified diets and adaptive equipment are used as ordered by the practitioner. Protocols do not authorize restraint or restrictions on rights. Any such restriction goes through BSP-02 and IR-03.

definitions.definition: A written, resident-specific set of instructions from a practitioner or the nurse consultant describing what to watch for and what staff must do for a health risk.
Food, liquid or other material entering the airway or lungs.
A resident's higher risk of airway blockage due to swallowing difficulty, eating habits, medications or other factors.
A diet with ordered texture, liquid consistency, or content, such as pureed, mechanical soft or thickened liquids.

procedures: At admission and at each annual plan review, the Program Director and nurse consultant identify each resident's health risks, including seizures, choking, aspiration, dehydration, falls and other conditions, using records, practitioner information and resident or representative input.

For each identified risk, the nurse consultant or practitioner supplies a written protocol. The Program Director places it in the resident's record and in the quick-reference location at the home. Protocols include warning signs, steps to take, when to call 911, whom to notify, and any resident-specific equipment or medications.

Before working alone with a resident, each staff member is trained on that resident's protocols. The nurse consultant or other qualified trainer provides the training, and the Program Director verifies and records it. Staff review the protocols again when they change and at least annually.

Each staff member completes classroom CPR and first aid within 90 days of hire, and renews the certification before it expires. The Program Director maintains a roster of certification dates. The schedule is built so that at least one CPR-certified staff member is on site whenever residents are present, including overnight (STF-01).

For seizures, staff follow the individual protocol. In general, they stay with the resident, note the time the seizure starts and ends, protect the resident from injury, do not put anything in the mouth, turn the resident on one side when the protocol directs, and call 911 when the protocol requires or when the resident is injured or has trouble breathing afterward. Staff record a seizure log entry with time, duration, description and recovery. If the resident's protocol sets a different threshold, the protocol controls.

For choking, staff follow the protocol and their first aid training. They call 911 if the resident cannot breathe, cough or speak, and provide the first aid they are trained in. They notify the Program Director immediately afterward and document the incident (HW-04, BSP-04).

For mealtimes, staff provide the diet texture and liquid consistency exactly as ordered, use the adaptive equipment as ordered, position the resident as the protocol states, and stay near and attentive for residents with choking or aspiration risk. Staff do not leave these residents alone with food. HES-04 covers the food and diet process.

Staff observe residents daily for changes in alertness, breathing, eating and drinking, skin, mobility, mood, pain and sleep. They record observations in the daily notes (PCS-03) and report any concerns to the Program Director the same shift.
When a staff member sees a possible change of condition, they follow HW-04. The nurse consultant is contacted for guidance. The practitioner is contacted for orders as needed.
Staff check adaptive and safety equipment, such as suction, positioning devices, and bed or chair features, at the frequency in the protocol. They report problems the same day (HW-02).

The Program Director reviews seizure logs and choking or aspiration events monthly and sends them to the nurse consultant. Trends, such as increased seizure frequency or repeated coughing at meals, are reported to the practitioner and the support coordinator within 2 business days.

Protocols are updated whenever the resident's practitioner changes orders or the resident's condition changes. The Program Director replaces the old copies, and retrains staff before the next shift when possible and in all cases before the staff member works with that resident.
Health events are reviewed quarterly in the quality review (GOV-04) for corrective actions.

responsibilities.duty: Ensure CPR-certified staffing at all times residents are present, and provide for protocols, training and equipment.
Maintain protocols, verify staff training, keep the CPR roster, review logs monthly, and communicate trends.
Develop or review protocols, train staff, and respond to questions on health events.
Follow protocols, keep CPR and first aid current, monitor residents, document and report events.
Provide orders for seizure, diet, and equipment and respond to reports of changes.

documentation: Individual health protocols in each resident's plan and record
Staff protocol training records
CPR and first aid certificates and tracking roster
Seizure logs and choking or aspiration event reports
Daily notes and health observations
Diet orders and equipment checks
Monthly Program Director and nurse reviews, and quarterly quality review summaries

policies.title: Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
policies.applies_to: All residents, direct support professionals, Program Director and Administrator of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To ensure staff recognize and respond immediately to a change in a resident's condition or a medical emergency. It also ensures emergency telephone access and numbers are always available, and that the people responsible for the resident and APD are notified as required.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 65G-2.010(1)(b), F.A.C.: at least one telephone is accessible to direct service providers and residents for emergency use at all times, and the required emergency telephone numbers, including each resident's doctors and each resident's support coordinator, are readily accessible at each telephone extension. [AGENCY NAME] responds immediately to any emergency. Staff call 911 first for any life-threatening condition. Adverse medication reactions are conveyed immediately to the prescriber or another medical professional. The legal representative and support coordinator are told of significant changes in condition. Incidents are reported under Rule 65G-2.010(6) and BSP-04.

definitions.definition: A noticeable shift in a resident's physical, mental, behavioral or functional status, such as new illness, injury, pain, loss of function, confusion, or refusal to eat or drink.
A condition that may cause death or serious harm without immediate care, such as trouble breathing, unresponsiveness, chest pain, stroke signs, severe bleeding, a prolonged seizure, or choking.
An incident of the type APD requires to be reported to the Regional Office within 4 hours, as described in BSP-04 and on APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006.
The posted list of emergency numbers kept at each telephone extension.

procedures: The Administrator makes sure the home has at least one working telephone that is accessible to staff and residents for emergency use at all times. A charged cell phone is kept with staff on outings and during transport. The Program Director tests the phone service monthly and records the test.

The Program Director posts an emergency telephone list at each telephone extension and keeps a copy in the staff area. The list includes 911, poison control, the Florida Abuse Hotline (1-800-962-2873), the APD Regional Office, the Administrator at [PHONE], the Program Director at [PHONE], the home address [ADDRESS], each resident's doctors and each resident's support coordinator, and the nurse consultant. Residents' doctors and support coordinators are listed by resident.
The Program Director updates the list within 2 business days of any change of doctor, support coordinator or number, and checks every extension against the list monthly. The check is recorded.

Staff who notice a change of condition check the resident right away, follow the resident's protocol if one applies (HW-03), take vital signs if trained, and record what they saw, including the time. They notify the Program Director the same shift.

In any medical emergency, staff call 911 immediately, give first aid or CPR as trained (Rule 65G-2.009(11)), and stay with the resident. A second staff member, if available, unlocks the door, gathers the medication list, the face sheet, the plan and protocols, and meets emergency personnel. Staff do not delay a 911 call to contact a supervisor.

When a resident is taken to the hospital, a staff member goes with the resident or follows as soon as staffing allows, unless the resident or representative prefers otherwise. Staff bring the medication list, insurance and Medicaid information, legal documents, protocols and emergency contacts, and provide a written summary to the treating team. Required staffing at the home is maintained at all times (STF-01).

For a non-emergency change of condition, staff call the resident's doctor or the nurse consultant the same day, report the change and symptoms, and follow the instructions. Staff record the instructions and carry them out. If the doctor cannot be reached and symptoms get worse, staff call 911 or arrange urgent care.

If a resident has a suspected adverse reaction to a medication, staff convey it immediately to the prescriber or another medical professional, call 911 for severe symptoms, hold further doses only as instructed, and record the reaction, time of call, and instruction on the MAR and in the notes (HW-01).

The Program Director notifies the legal representative or guardian and the support coordinator of every emergency, hospital visit and significant change in condition, as soon as possible and within the same day. Notice is documented with the time, the person notified, and the information shared. If the resident prefers that a family member or friend be told, that person is also notified with consent (IR-05).
If the event may involve abuse, neglect or exploitation, staff call the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 immediately, as required in BSP-03.

If the event is a critical incident, the Administrator or designee gives initial notice to the APD Regional Office within 4 hours and submits the completed APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day. If the event is a reportable incident, the form is submitted within 1 calendar day. Follow-up information is submitted within 5 days (Rule 65G-2.010(6); BSP-04).

The staff member who responded completes an incident report before the end of the shift. The Program Director reviews it within 1 business day and decides whether any additional report or action is required.

After an emergency, the Program Director meets with the resident, staff and, as needed, the nurse consultant to review what happened. The plan, protocols and orders are updated (PCS-02, HW-03), and staff are briefed at the next handoff (PCS-04).

Staff are trained on emergency response, telephone use and the emergency list at orientation and annually (STF-04). The Administrator reviews emergency responses and notifications quarterly in GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Ensure telephone access and posted numbers, make required APD reports, and review emergency events for improvement.
Maintain and check the emergency lists, notify representatives and support coordinators, review incident reports, and update plans.
Recognize changes, call 911 when needed, give first aid, report promptly and document accurately.
Advise staff on changes of condition and review follow-up needs.
Receive notice and take part in decisions about care after the event.

documentation: Emergency telephone list for each extension and monthly check log
Telephone test record
Change of condition notes and daily notes
Hospital or urgent care transfer summaries
Record of notifications to representative, support coordinator and prescriber
Adverse reaction record and MAR entries
Incident reports and APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006, with follow-up submissions
Post-event review notes and updated plans

policies.title: Death of an Individual
policies.applies_to: All staff, the Administrator, and the contracted or consulting nurse at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure that when a resident dies, staff respond with dignity and urgency, call emergency services, report to APD within the required time frames, notify the resident's legal representative and support coordinator, protect the resident's property and funds, and keep the census and records accurate.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] treats every death of a resident, whether sudden, expected, or in the home, a hospital or in the community, as a critical incident under Rule 65G-2.010(6). Staff call 911 and follow the resident's directives. The Administrator gives initial notice to the APD Regional Office within 4 hours and submits APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day. The Administrator confirms the death category under Rule 65G-2.010(6)(f)3. The legal representative and support coordinator are notified. The resident's property and personal funds are secured under the inventory and funds policies. The census change is reported to APD within 5 calendar days under Rule 65G-2.009(3). If abuse, neglect or exploitation is known or suspected, staff also report immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 under BSP-03.

definitions.definition: An incident that Rule 65G-2.010(6)(f) classifies as critical, which includes the death of a resident. It requires initial notice to the APD Regional Office within 4 hours and Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day.

Any advance directive, Do Not Resuscitate Order, health care surrogate designation, or other written wishes about emergency treatment that are in the resident's record and have been shared with staff.
The resident's guardian, guardian advocate, or other person legally authorized to make decisions for the resident, as recorded in the resident record.
The report to APD, due within 5 calendar days, that a resident is no longer residing in the facility (Rule 65G-2.009(3)).

procedures: The first staff member who finds a resident unresponsive, not breathing, or without a pulse calls 911 immediately and gives the address, the resident's name, and the condition found.

While waiting for responders, staff check the resident's record for an advance directive or Do Not Resuscitate Order. Staff follow the resident's directives and the 911 dispatcher's instructions, and give CPR or first aid only as the directives and staff training permit. Staff give the directive to the responders when they arrive.

Staff keep the other residents safe and supervised, and offer comfort and privacy to housemates. Staff do not move the resident's body or disturb the area unless emergency responders direct it or it is needed to give care.

Staff call the on-call Administrator at [PHONE] as soon as the 911 call is made and give the time, the circumstances, and what responders are doing. If the resident is taken to a hospital, a staff member goes along when possible or follows, and carries the face sheet, medication list and directives.

If anything about the death suggests abuse, neglect, exploitation or a serious injury, staff report immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 and tell the Administrator. Staff cooperate with law enforcement and any investigator, and they protect the scene and records as directed.

The Administrator gives initial notice of the death to the APD Regional Office at [REGIONAL OFFICE PHONE] within 4 hours of the death or of learning of it, and records the time, the person spoken to, and the details given.

The Administrator confirms the death category under Rule 65G-2.010(6)(f)3 and completes APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day. The form includes the circumstances, the response, the persons notified, and the follow-up measures.

The Administrator, or a designee for the Administrator, promptly notifies the resident's legal representative, and asks about any funeral, religious or cultural wishes. Notice is given by telephone in a respectful and private way, never by voicemail or text message alone. If the legal representative cannot be reached, the Administrator keeps trying and documents each attempt. Staff do not release information to anyone else except as IR-05 allows.

The Administrator notifies the resident's support coordinator the same day and confirms by email. The Administrator also notifies the nurse under HW-02 and the resident's primary care provider, and tells the Behavior Analyst if one is involved.

The Administrator secures the resident's room, personal belongings, valuables and records. Two staff, one of whom is the Administrator or designee, complete a written count of the property against the admission inventory and the resident's funds ledger. Both sign and date it. Funds, valuables and medications are locked up and are released only to the legal representative or to the person legally entitled to receive them, with a signed receipt, as IR-06 requires.
Staff do not discard, share out or give away any belongings. Medications for the resident are counted, secured, and disposed of or returned only as HW-01 permits and with documentation.
The Administrator reports the census change to APD within 5 calendar days of the death under Rule 65G-2.009(3) and updates the internal census and daily attendance records.

The Administrator records the death in the resident record, including a dated summary of events, the notifications made and their times, and what was done with property and funds. The resident record is updated within 30 days of any new information, such as the cause of death, and is kept for 6 years. The Administrator provides copies to APD within 2 calendar days of a request.
The Administrator tells billing staff of the date of death so that service documentation and claims are accurate under GOV-05.

The Administrator holds a debrief with staff and housemates within [NUMBER] days, offers information on grief support resources, and arranges for housemates to take part in memorial or remembrance activities if they wish.

The Administrator refers the death to the quality improvement and mortality review process in GOV-04 and reports on any follow-up measures needed to prevent similar events. Follow-up measures are recorded on Form OP 3-0006 within 5 days.

responsibilities.duty: Call 911, follow the resident's directives, keep other residents safe, call the on-call Administrator, and document what was seen and done.

Make the 4-hour notice and file Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day, notify the legal representative and support coordinator, secure property and funds, report the census change within 5 calendar days, and complete the record and follow-up.
Provide clinical information for the report, help secure and account for medications, and take part in the mortality review.
Review the death and the findings under GOV-04 and approve corrective actions.

documentation: APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 with follow-up measures
