Log of notifications with dates, times, names and means of contact (APD Regional Office, legal representative, support coordinator, nurse)
Staff incident statements
Property inventory reconciliation and funds ledger closing entry, signed and dated by two staff
Receipt for release of property, funds and medications
Census change report to APD
Mortality review notes (GOV-04)

policies.title: Positive Behavior Support
policies.applies_to: All direct support staff, the Administrator, the Behavior Analyst and all persons who support residents with behavior needs
policies.purpose: To set out how [AGENCY NAME] helps prevent and respond to problematic behaviors through positive, person-centered supports, led by a certified behavior analyst, with review of plans by the Local Review Committee and trained staff.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 65G-2.009(8)(a), F.A.C., the written statement of policies and procedures governing actions that direct service providers may take to help prevent or respond to problematic behaviors exhibited by residents, including emergency procedures and reporting requirements, consistent with s. 393.13, F.S., and Chapters 65G-4 and 65G-8, F.A.C. [AGENCY NAME] uses positive, proactive supports first: understanding why a behavior occurs, teaching new skills, changing the environment and honoring the resident's choices. Behavior analysis services that include restricted procedures are provided or supervised by a certified behavior analyst. Written plans go to the Local Review Committee (LRC) chair within 5 working days after implementation. Staff are trained on each resident's behavior plan by a certified behavior analyst, and the training is recorded in the personnel record. Emergency procedures are in BSP-02, and reporting is in BSP-04 and BSP-03. Where [AGENCY NAME] operates a behavior focus home, it has the APD designation, BCBA or Chapter 490/491 licensee monitoring, and staff with 20 contact hours or RBT status.

definitions.definition: A behavior analyst who is certified as required by APD rule and who provides or supervises behavior analysis services.
A behavior procedure that limits a resident's rights or freedom and so requires review under Chapter 65G-4, F.A.C., including LRC review.
The written plan that describes the behavior, its function, the proactive and teaching strategies, the response strategies, and the data to be collected.
The committee that reviews behavior plans and approves or disapproves them under Chapter 65G-4, F.A.C.
A home with an APD behavior-focus or intensive-behavioral designation that serves residents who need behavior supports under the iBudget handbook.
Board Certified Behavior Analyst and Registered Behavior Technician, certified by the national certifying board.

procedures: Before or at admission, the Administrator asks the support coordinator and the legal representative for any existing behavior plan, functional assessment and the Individual Plan, and records any behavior needs on the resident's face sheet.

When a resident shows a behavior that may harm the resident or others, or limit the resident's life, the Administrator asks the support coordinator to refer the resident for behavior analysis services and engages a certified behavior analyst.

The certified behavior analyst completes an assessment of the function of the behavior, using information from the resident, family, staff and records. The resident takes part to the extent possible, and the resident's preferences guide the strategies.

The behavior plan puts proactive strategies first: environmental changes, skills teaching, choice-making, and reinforcing alternative behaviors. Any restricted procedure must be justified in the plan and must be provided or supervised by the certified behavior analyst.
The Administrator obtains informed consent from the resident or legal representative under IR-07 before any plan is put into effect. Any rights restriction in the plan is also handled under IR-03.
The written plan is submitted to the LRC chair within 5 working days after implementation, and the Administrator records the date sent and the date of LRC receipt.

If the LRC disapproves a plan, the certified behavior analyst and Administrator revise it and resubmit it within 14 working days, and record the dates. Any procedure the LRC has not approved is not used.

The certified behavior analyst trains each direct support staff member who works with the resident on the resident's behavior plan before the staff member supports the resident alone. The training covers the strategies, data collection and emergency steps. The trainer, date, content and staff signatures are recorded in the personnel record.

Staff must also hold current certification under Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C., before using any reactive strategy, as BSP-02 requires. Training on Chapter 65G-8 compliance is part of the staff's required training under STF-04.

Staff carry out the plan as written, collect behavior data on the plan's data sheets each shift, and record them in the daily documentation (PCS-03). Staff do not add, change or skip any strategy without the written approval of the certified behavior analyst.

Where [AGENCY NAME] has a behavior-focus or intensive-behavioral designation, the Administrator keeps the APD designation, makes sure monitoring is provided by a BCBA or a Chapter 490/491 licensee, and makes sure staff providing the service have 20 contact hours of training or hold RBT status. Documentation is kept in each staff member's personnel record.

The certified behavior analyst reviews the data at least [FREQUENCY] and meets with the team. If a behavior plan is not working, is no longer needed, or has restricted procedures that can be reduced, the plan is revised and sent again to the LRC as needed.
The Administrator makes sure the implementation plan, the quarterly summary and the annual report that the iBudget handbook requires are completed and kept in the resident record.
When a behavior incident occurs, staff use the response in the behavior plan first. Staff use emergency procedures only as BSP-02 permits, and report incidents under BSP-04 and BSP-03 as applicable.
The Administrator reviews behavior data and incident trends monthly with the certified behavior analyst and brings the results to the quality improvement review in GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Assess behavior, write and supervise the plan, train staff on the plan, monitor data, and revise the plan.
Make sure plans are obtained, consented to and sent to the LRC within 5 working days, keep training records, and keep any APD designation.
Use the plan as written, collect data, complete training, and report problems or incidents.
Review plans and approve or disapprove them.
Take part in planning and give informed consent.

documentation: Behavior assessment and written behavior plan
LRC submission date, decision, and any revisions with resubmission dates
Informed consent documentation
Staff training record on each resident's behavior plan, signed by the certified behavior analyst, in the personnel record
Behavior data sheets and the certified behavior analyst's data review notes
Implementation plan, quarterly summary and annual report
Evidence of APD designation, BCBA or Chapter 490/491 monitoring, and staff 20-hour or RBT proof (behavior focus homes)

policies.title: Restrictive Interventions, Restraint and Seclusion
policies.applies_to: All direct support staff, the Administrator, the Behavior Analyst and the nurse
policies.purpose: To protect residents from unnecessary restraint, seclusion and punishment, and to limit any reactive strategy to staff who are certified under Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C., with the approvals, documentation and notification that the rules require.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 65G-2.009(8)(b)-(d), F.A.C. Direct service providers must be trained to respond appropriately to serious and spontaneous behavioral incidents requiring emergency intervention. Restraint, seclusion or physical-discomfort procedures are used only by staff who are certified under Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C., and only with Local Review Committee (LRC) approval. The following responses are forbidden: (1) physical or corporal punishment; (2) any other response forbidden by Rule 65G-2.009(8)(d); (3) verbal abuse; (4) humiliation, including dark or locked time-out rooms; and (5) any reactive strategy prohibited under Rule 65G-8.009. Each resident has the right under s. 393.13, F.S., to be free from unnecessary restraint or seclusion. Chemical restraint is governed by Rule 65G-8.008. Use of any reactive strategy is documented and reported as Rule 65G-8.010 requires. Any rights modification must also meet 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4) and IR-03. [AGENCY NAME] performs an annual internal review under Rule 65G-8.003. Because APD has revisions to Chapter 65G-8 in development, the Administrator confirms the current text each year.

definitions.definition: A response used after a behavior has begun to protect the resident or others from harm, such as physical restraint or seclusion, regulated under Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C.
A physical, mechanical or chemical means that restricts a resident's freedom of movement.
Placing a resident alone in a place from which the resident is prevented from leaving.
A drug used to control behavior or restrict freedom of movement that is not a standard treatment for the resident's medical or psychiatric condition, regulated by Rule 65G-8.008.
Staff who have completed an APD-approved emergency procedure curriculum with at least 12 direct training hours, passed a written test with at least 80%, and hold a certification valid for one year.
Any act that demeans or degrades a resident, including use of a dark or locked time-out room.

procedures: The Administrator uses only an emergency procedure curriculum approved by APD under Rule 65G-8.002. Certification requires at least 12 direct training hours and a written test with a minimum 80% score, and is valid for one year.

Before any direct support staff member uses any physical technique, the Administrator confirms that the staff member holds current certification. Staff who are not certified, or whose certification has lapsed, never use restraint, seclusion or physical-discomfort procedures, and they call for help instead. The expiration dates are kept in a tracking log.

All direct support staff are trained in non-physical responses, such as de-escalation and calm communication, so they can respond to serious and spontaneous behavioral incidents. Training is documented in the personnel record.

Restraint, seclusion and physical-discomfort procedures are not part of any routine plan. A procedure that is part of a behavior plan must be reviewed and approved by the LRC under Chapter 65G-4, F.A.C., and the resident or legal representative must consent first under IR-07. Consent information is kept in the resident record as Rule 65G-8.003 requires.

Staff use a reactive strategy only as a last resort when a resident is a danger to self or others and less restrictive responses have not worked. Staff use the least force for the shortest time, watch the resident's breathing and physical condition at all times, and end the procedure as soon as the danger has passed.

Staff never use any of the following: physical or corporal punishment; verbal abuse; humiliation, including dark or locked time-out rooms; any other response forbidden under Rule 65G-2.009(8)(d); or any procedure prohibited under Rule 65G-8.009. Staff never use restraint as punishment, for staff convenience, or because of too few staff.

Chemical restraint is used only as Rule 65G-8.008 allows. Only a licensed prescriber may order medication, and staff never give extra or different medication on their own to control behavior. Any such order is reviewed by the nurse and the Administrator under HW-01 and HW-02.

If a reactive strategy is used, staff immediately check the resident and others for injury and call 911 or arrange medical care if needed under HW-04. The resident is given a chance to calm and to talk about what happened.

The staff member completes the incident documentation by the end of the shift and gives it to the Administrator. The record includes what led up to the incident, the less restrictive responses tried, the technique used, its duration, who took part, any injuries, and the resident's condition afterwards.

The Administrator notifies the resident's legal representative and support coordinator and reports the incident as Rule 65G-8.010 and BSP-04 require. The Administrator reports to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 if there is any suspicion of abuse, neglect or exploitation (BSP-03).

The Administrator and the certified behavior analyst review each use of a reactive strategy within [NUMBER] working days, interview staff and the resident, decide whether the response was appropriate, and decide whether the behavior plan, training or supports should change. Staff who misused a technique are retrained or disciplined, and may be removed from direct care.

The Administrator completes an annual internal review of all uses of reactive strategies, as Rule 65G-8.003 requires, covering frequency, trends, injuries, certifications and policy compliance, and takes the results to the quality improvement review in GOV-04.
The Administrator checks the current text of Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C., each year, because APD has revisions in development, and updates this policy and staff training when the rule changes (GOV-03).

Any rights restriction that applies to a resident is handled under IR-03, which requires an assessed need, a record in the Individual Plan, informed consent and regular review, consistent with 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4).

responsibilities.duty: Make sure only APD-approved curricula are used, track certifications, review each incident, report as required, and complete the annual internal review.
Use techniques only as trained and only as a last resort, monitor the resident throughout, and document fully.
Include any approved procedure in the plan, seek LRC approval, and review incidents and revise the plan.
Assess the resident after any use of a reactive strategy and review any medication orders used to manage behavior.
Approve or disapprove behavior plans that include restricted procedures.

documentation: Staff certification records, with expiration dates, in the personnel record
LRC approval for any plan that includes restraint, seclusion or physical-discomfort procedures
Consent information in the resident record
Incident documentation for each use of a reactive strategy, with notifications under Rule 65G-8.010
Post-incident review notes
Annual internal review under Rule 65G-8.003
Rights restriction documentation (IR-03)

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers, contractors and the Administrator at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To protect residents from abuse, neglect and exploitation, to make sure every known or suspected case is reported immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline, and to set out the steps for investigating employees and submitting a Corrective Action Plan when an employee with a verified finding stays employed.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] has zero tolerance for abuse, neglect, exploitation and abandonment of residents, who have the right under s. 393.13, F.S., to be free from them. Any person who knows of or suspects abuse, neglect or exploitation reports it immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873, as Rule 65G-2.010(6)(a) requires under ss. 39.201 and 415.1034, F.S. Every staff member completes Zero Tolerance training before providing services, with a refresher every 3 years. Staff named as alleged perpetrators are handled under Rule 65G-2.008(5). This policy meets Rule 65G-2.008(5)(c): if an employee has a verified finding of abuse, neglect, exploitation or abandonment and remains employed, the Administrator submits a Corrective Action Plan to the Regional Office within 15 days that states (1) why the employment is not terminated; (2) the disciplinary action taken; (3) any training and dates; and (4) how residents will be protected. No one is punished for making a report in good faith.

definitions.definition: Any willful act or threatened act that causes or is likely to cause significant impairment to a resident's physical, mental or emotional health, including physical, verbal and sexual abuse.
Failure to provide the care, supervision or services needed to maintain a resident's physical and mental health.
Improper use of a resident's funds, property or resources for another person's profit or advantage.
Leaving a resident without the care and supervision the resident needs.
A determination by the investigating agency that the allegation of abuse, neglect, exploitation or abandonment is verified.
The written plan submitted to the Regional Office within 15 days under Rule 65G-2.008(5)(c) when an employee with a verified finding remains employed.

procedures: Before an employee provides services, the Administrator gives the employee Zero Tolerance training and records the date, trainer and signature in the personnel record. The employee repeats the training every 3 years, and the Administrator tracks due dates (STF-04).

At orientation and each year, the Administrator reviews this policy with all staff and gives each staff member the Abuse Hotline number, 1-800-962-2873. The number is posted at each phone and in the staff area along with the other emergency numbers.

Any person who witnesses or suspects abuse, neglect or exploitation calls the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 immediately. The person does not wait for approval from a supervisor, and does not investigate first. Staff record the date, time and the intake number given by the Hotline.

Staff immediately protect the resident from further harm. They get medical care if needed (HW-04), keep the resident away from the alleged perpetrator, and preserve evidence, such as clothing and the scene.

Staff tell the Administrator, or the on-call Administrator at [PHONE], as soon as the report is made. If the Administrator is the person suspected, staff report to the Hotline and to the APD Regional Office at [REGIONAL OFFICE PHONE] and tell the Governing Body representative, [GOVERNING BODY CONTACT].

The Administrator makes the required incident report under BSP-04: initial notice to the Regional Office within 4 hours for a critical incident, and Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day. The Administrator also notifies the resident's legal representative and support coordinator.

When an employee is named as an alleged perpetrator, the Administrator immediately puts protective measures in place. These may include removing the employee from contact with residents, as directed by the Hotline, law enforcement or APD. The Administrator follows Rule 65G-2.008(5) for the investigation, takes no action that interferes with an outside investigation, and does not tell the alleged perpetrator who made the report.

The Administrator cooperates fully with the Hotline, law enforcement, APD and other investigators, and gives records and access to staff and residents promptly. The Administrator carries out any internal review under BSP-04 and does not treat that review as a substitute for the outside investigation.

When the investigating agency issues a finding, the Administrator records it, notifies the legal representative and support coordinator as appropriate, and puts the finding in the personnel file and incident file. The Administrator checks the employee's status in the screening and registry checks under STF-02.

If an employee has a verified finding of abuse, neglect, exploitation or abandonment and the Administrator decides to keep the employee, the Administrator prepares a Corrective Action Plan and sends it to the Regional Office within 15 days.

The Corrective Action Plan states: (1) why the employment is not terminated; (2) the disciplinary action taken; (3) any training provided and the dates; and (4) how residents will be protected, including supervision and any changes to the employee's duties. The Administrator keeps a copy in the personnel record and the Governing Body reviews it.
The Administrator makes sure no retaliation takes place against anyone who reports in good faith. Retaliation is grounds for discipline up to and including termination.

The Administrator discusses with the resident, in a way the resident can understand, what happened and what supports are available, and offers counseling or other help through the support coordinator. The Individual Plan is updated if the resident's needs change (PCS-02).

The Administrator reviews each report and its outcome at the quality improvement review in GOV-04, looks for patterns and risks, and makes changes to staffing, training, supervision or the home environment.

responsibilities.duty: Report known or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873, protect the resident, and cooperate with investigations.
Train staff, make incident reports, protect residents during investigations, and submit any Corrective Action Plan to the Regional Office within 15 days.
Review serious findings and Corrective Action Plans and make sure residents are protected.
Receive notice, take part in follow-up, and help the resident get support.

documentation: Zero Tolerance training record before services and every 3 years
Hotline report details, date, time and intake number
APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 and notification log
Protective measures taken and investigation records
Corrective Action Plan and proof it was sent to the Regional Office within 15 days
Personnel file entries for findings, discipline and retraining
Quality improvement review notes (GOV-04)

policies.title: Reportable Incidents and Investigations
policies.applies_to: All staff and the Administrator at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure all critical and reportable incidents are reported to the Florida Abuse Hotline and the APD Regional Office on time, that the legal representative and support coordinator are told, that follow-up is documented, and that incidents are investigated and used to improve care.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 65G-2.010(6)(a)-(h), F.A.C. Known or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 (ss. 39.201 and 415.1034, F.S.). A critical incident is reported with initial notice to the APD Regional Office within 4 hours and a complete APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day. A reportable incident is reported within 1 calendar day. The Administrator notifies the legal representative and support coordinator. Follow-up measures are recorded on the form within 5 days. The incident types are those listed in Rule 65G-2.010(6)(f)3 and (g), and the Administrator keeps a current copy of those lists for staff. [AGENCY NAME] cooperates with investigations and provides records promptly.

definitions.definition: An incident of a type listed in Rule 65G-2.010(6)(f)3, such as the death of a resident. It requires initial notice within 4 hours and Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day.
An incident of a type listed in Rule 65G-2.010(6)(g). It requires a report within 1 calendar day.
The APD Incident Reporting Form (Dec. 2025) used to report incidents and record follow-up.
The first notice to the APD Regional Office, given within 4 hours of a critical incident, before the form is complete.
Actions taken to protect the resident, address the cause, and prevent a repeat, recorded on the form within 5 days.

procedures: Any staff member who sees or learns of an incident protects the resident, gets medical help if needed (HW-04), and tells the Administrator or on-call Administrator at [PHONE] right away.

If abuse, neglect or exploitation is known or suspected, the staff member calls the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 immediately and records the intake number (BSP-03). Staff do not delay this call to complete other reports.

The Administrator decides whether the incident is a critical incident or a reportable incident by checking the lists in Rule 65G-2.010(6)(f)3 and (g). If there is doubt, the Administrator treats it as the more serious category and calls the Regional Office at [REGIONAL OFFICE PHONE] to confirm.
For a critical incident, the Administrator gives initial notice to the Regional Office within 4 hours and records the time, person spoken to and details given.

The Administrator completes APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 for a critical incident within 1 calendar day, and for a reportable incident within 1 calendar day, and submits it to the Regional Office. The form is complete, factual and signed, and states what happened, when, where, who was involved and what was done.
The Administrator notifies the resident's legal representative and support coordinator as soon as possible, and records the time, person and method of each notification.

Staff involved or present write a statement before the end of the shift. Statements are factual and include only what the person saw, heard or did. Staff do not discuss the incident with each other in a way that changes the account.

The Administrator records follow-up measures on the form within 5 days. These include changes in supervision, staffing, plan or environment, further medical care, staff retraining and any other steps taken to protect the resident and prevent a repeat.
The Administrator keeps a copy of the Form OP 3-0006 and all related documents in the incident file and the resident's record, as REC-01 requires. Copies are provided to APD within the time required.
If the incident involves a staff member, the Administrator follows BSP-03 and Rule 65G-2.008(5), including protective measures and any Corrective Action Plan.
The Administrator cooperates with APD, the Abuse Hotline, law enforcement and other investigators. The Administrator gives records, makes staff available, and does not destroy or change any records.
If the incident was a death, missing resident, use of a reactive strategy or other event with its own procedure, the Administrator also follows HW-05, BSP-05 or BSP-02.

The Administrator reviews incidents monthly for type, time, place, people involved and trends. The Administrator takes the data to the quality improvement review under GOV-04 and reports any needed policy changes under GOV-03.

The Administrator keeps the incident type lists from Rule 65G-2.010(6)(f)3 and (g) and this policy at the staff desk or in the staff binder. All staff are trained on this policy at orientation and each year.

responsibilities.duty: Protect residents, report abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately to the Hotline, tell the Administrator, and write accurate statements.
Classify incidents, give 4-hour initial notice, submit Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day, notify the legal representative and support coordinator, and record follow-up within 5 days.
Review incident trends and require corrective action under GOV-04.
Provide clinical or behavioral input to the follow-up measures.

documentation: APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 with follow-up measures
Notification log (APD Regional Office, Hotline intake number, legal representative, support coordinator)
Staff written statements
Incident log and monthly trend review
Copies of the Rule 65G-2.010(6)(f)3 and (g) incident lists
Investigation correspondence and records provided to investigators

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
policies.applies_to: All direct support staff and the Administrator at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure that when a resident is missing, staff act at once, involve law enforcement, document the response, report as a critical incident, and reduce the risk of a repeat by keeping current identifying information and elopement risk in the plan.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 65G-2.010(5), F.A.C., the missing residents procedure. After determining that a resident is missing, staff immediately call local law enforcement, ask the officer to assign a case number, and, if the officer refuses to take a report, document the officer's name and contact the Watch Commander. The Administrator makes a critical incident report under Rule 65G-2.010(6)(f): initial notice to the APD Regional Office within 4 hours and APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day. [AGENCY NAME] keeps a current photo and identifying information in each resident's record, and records elopement risk in the resident's plan.

definitions.definition: A resident whose whereabouts are unknown and who is not where the plan or supervision requires, once staff have checked the places the resident is likely to be.
A resident leaving the home or a supervised setting without staff knowledge or without the supervision the plan requires.
The supervising officer on duty at the law enforcement agency, who is contacted if an officer declines to take a report.
A resident's known tendency to leave or wander, assessed and recorded in the resident's plan with the supports to reduce it.

procedures: At admission and at each plan review, the Administrator and the support team assess each resident's elopement risk. The risk, triggers, and prevention supports are recorded in the Individual Plan (PCS-02) and, where needed, the behavior plan (BSP-01).

The Administrator keeps in each resident's record a current photograph, description (height, weight, hair, eye color, distinguishing marks), clothing sizes, medical needs, communication needs, and places the resident likes to go. The Administrator reviews and updates these at least [FREQUENCY] and after any change in appearance.
Staff do regular headcounts and checks as the resident's supervision level requires. At each shift change, staff confirm where every resident is and record it (PCS-04).

When a staff member cannot find a resident, the staff member quickly checks the house, yard, vehicles and nearby places the resident likes. A second staff member is told at once. If the resident has not been found after the quick check, staff declare the resident missing without waiting.

As soon as the resident is determined to be missing, staff immediately call local law enforcement at 911 or [LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT NON-EMERGENCY NUMBER] and give the resident's name, description, photo, clothing, health needs, last time and place seen, and the likely direction.
Staff ask the officer to assign a case number and record it, along with the officer's name, agency and the time of the call.
If the officer refuses to take a report, staff document the officer's name and contact the Watch Commander. Staff record the Watch Commander's name and the outcome.

Staff call the on-call Administrator at [PHONE] immediately. The Administrator sends additional staff to help search, while making sure the other residents continue to be supervised. Staff do not leave other residents unsupervised to search.

The Administrator makes a critical incident report under Rule 65G-2.010(6)(f): initial notice to the APD Regional Office within 4 hours and APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day (BSP-04). The Administrator also notifies the legal representative and support coordinator.
If anything suggests abuse, neglect or exploitation, the Administrator or any staff member also reports immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 (BSP-03).
Staff keep a time-stamped log of search actions, calls and contacts, and keep a phone line open for law enforcement.

When the resident is found, staff tell law enforcement, the Regional Office, the legal representative and the support coordinator. The resident is checked for injury and illness, given medical care if needed (HW-04), and treated with respect and without blame.

Within 5 days, the Administrator records follow-up measures on Form OP 3-0006, and reviews with the team why the resident left. The Individual Plan, behavior plan, supervision, alarms or door supports, and the environment are reviewed and revised, with any rights concerns handled under IR-03.
The Administrator reviews each missing person event at the quality improvement review under GOV-04 and retrains staff as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Do checks and headcounts, call law enforcement immediately when a resident is missing, get the case number, and document the search.
Send the 4-hour notice and Form OP 3-0006, notify the legal representative and support coordinator, keep resident photos and identifying information current, and update plans after an event.
Assess elopement risk and agree on prevention supports for the plan.
Take the report, assign a case number, and assist with the search.

documentation: Current photo and identifying information in each resident record
Elopement risk assessment and supports in the Individual Plan
Law enforcement case number, officer's name and agency, and Watch Commander contact if used
Search log with times and actions
APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 and the 4-hour notice record
Notification log and follow-up measures recorded within 5 days

policies.title: Residential Environment and Accessibility
policies.applies_to: Facility operator, direct support staff, maintenance personnel and all residents of [AGENCY NAME] group homes
federal: Americans with Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.)
policies.purpose: To make sure every [AGENCY NAME] group home is safe, sanitary, accessible and homelike. The home must meet the physical plant standards for APD-licensed facilities before residents move in and stay compliant for as long as the license is held.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates only homes that meet the General Residential Facility Standards in Rule 65G-2.007, F.A.C., and the Group Home Facility Standards in Rule 65G-2.0072, F.A.C. No home is a mobile or manufactured home. No bedroom holds more than 2 residents for a home first licensed on or after 7/1/2014. A single bedroom has at least 80 sq ft. A shared bedroom has at least 60 sq ft per person. The home has at least one toilet, one sink and one tub or shower for every 3 residents. It has at least 35 sq ft of living and dining space per household member. Hot water at fixtures residents can reach does not exceed 120°F. Working smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are installed and maintained. Access to water hazards is restricted. Hazardous chemicals are stored securely. The home has a designated office area with secure records storage. The home is accessible to the residents who live there, consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Physical adaptations are made to meet each resident's needs as identified in the individual plan, and they do not reduce other residents' access to the home. This policy has no items on the state's official checklist. It is adopted to meet the physical plant standards cited above.

definitions.definition: Any person living in the home, including residents and any live-in staff or operator's family, counted when calculating living and dining space.
Any pool, spa, pond, canal, retention area or other body of water that could present a drowning risk to residents.
Cleaning agents, pesticides, solvents, fuels and similar products that are poisonous or dangerous if ingested, inhaled or touched.
Usable by each resident, including residents who use wheelchairs, walkers or other mobility or sensory aids, without avoidable barriers.

procedures: Before leasing or purchasing a property, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] confirms it is a site-built or otherwise permitted dwelling and not a mobile or manufactured home. The finding is recorded on the Home Site Review Checklist.

Before applying for licensure, the operator measures every bedroom, bathroom and common room. The operator records the measurements on a floor plan that shows square footage and the number of residents assigned to each bedroom.
The operator confirms each bedroom is at least 80 sq ft for one person or 60 sq ft per person for two. The operator confirms no bedroom is assigned more than 2 residents.
The operator confirms the home has at least one toilet, one sink and one tub or shower for every 3 residents. Licensed capacity is never set above what the bathroom count supports.
The operator confirms living and dining space is at least 35 sq ft per household member. The operator recalculates when any household member is added.

The operator sets the water heater so water at resident-accessible fixtures does not exceed 120°F. Staff test and log water temperature at least monthly, and at each move-in, after any plumbing or heater repair, and after any report of hot water.

Staff install smoke and carbon monoxide detectors per the manufacturer's instructions and local fire authority requirements. Staff test each detector monthly and record the test date, location and result. Batteries are replaced as needed, and failed units are replaced the same day.

Staff identify every water hazard on and next to the property. The operator installs barriers such as fencing, locked gates or door alarms that restrict resident access. The operator documents any supervision requirements in the individual plan (see PCS-02).
Staff keep hazardous chemicals in a locked or otherwise secured location, in original containers. The operator keeps current safety data sheets for products used in the home.
The operator sets up a designated office area in the home with lockable storage for resident records and confidential personnel files. Only authorized staff have keys. See REC-01 and IR-05.

At admission and whenever a resident's needs change, the operator and the support coordinator review whether the home meets the resident's accessibility needs, such as ramps, grab bars, doorway width, bathroom access and visual or auditory alarms.

The operator promptly arranges needed modifications and documents the request, the approvals needed and the completion date. If the home cannot be made accessible, the operator notifies the support coordinator and follows PCS-06.

The operator or a designee completes a monthly environmental inspection of the entire home. The inspection covers bedrooms, bathrooms, common areas, exits, detectors, water temperature, chemical storage, water hazard barriers, sanitation and repairs. Findings are recorded and corrected, with the correction date noted.
Staff report hazards or needed repairs to the operator immediately. Urgent safety hazards are corrected or isolated the same day, and residents are protected until the repair is complete.
[ADMINISTRATOR NAME] reviews a summary of inspection findings quarterly through the quality improvement process in GOV-04 and updates this policy when Rule 65G-2.007 or 65G-2.0072 changes.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the home meets all physical plant standards, completes or assigns monthly inspections, and approves repairs and modifications.
Perform daily safety checks, test detectors and water temperature as assigned, secure chemicals, and report hazards immediately.
Complete repairs and modifications promptly and document the work performed.
Is notified of accessibility needs and works with the operator on modifications or alternate placement.

documentation: Home Site Review Checklist and floor plan with room measurements
Monthly environmental inspection reports and corrective action records
Smoke and carbon monoxide detector test log
Water temperature log
Accessibility assessment and modification records
Repair and maintenance work orders

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Fire Drills
policies.applies_to: Facility operator, all direct support staff and all residents of [AGENCY NAME] group homes
policies.purpose: To prepare staff and residents to evacuate and respond safely in a fire or other emergency. Fire drills are conducted and documented as the rule requires. Residents who need medically essential service are protected during a power outage or service interruption.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 65G-2.010(3)(a)-(c), F.A.C. (Emergency preparedness drills) and Rule 65G-2.007(3)(e), F.A.C. (Backup equipment or power supply). [AGENCY NAME] holds a fire drill every month in every home. Each drill record shows the date, the time of day, the points of exit used, the evacuation time and the signature of the person conducting the drill. Drill records are kept for one year. No fire drill is held between midnight and 5:00 a.m. APD Regional Office staff may observe any drill, and staff cooperate fully. Each home has an annual fire inspection under Chapter 69A-38, F.A.C., and an approved inspection is on file before initial licensure and each renewal (Rule 65G-2.010(2)). Where a resident requires a medically essential service, such as oxygen or other electrically powered medical equipment, [AGENCY NAME] is solely responsible for backup equipment or power and a written plan of action for a power outage or service interruption, under s. 366.15, F.S. Emergency numbers are posted at every phone extension. The Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP) required by s. 393.067, F.S., is maintained and followed as set out in SDA-01.

definitions.definition: A practiced evacuation of all residents and staff on duty from the home to a designated safe meeting place, with the evacuation timed and recorded.
Any utility-dependent service, such as electricity for oxygen concentrators, suction, feeding pumps or powered lifts, whose interruption could endanger a resident's health or life.
The Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan described in SDA-01.
The APD Regional Office that licenses and monitors the home.

procedures: The operator schedules one fire drill per home each calendar month and varies the day of the week and time of day. The operator records the planned date on the drill calendar.

Drills are held only between 5:00 a.m. and midnight. A drill is never started between midnight and 5:00 a.m., even if overnight evacuation practice is needed. Overnight readiness is addressed through staff training and the CEMP.

Before a drill, the staff member conducting it checks that exits are clear and that the evacuation route and meeting place are accessible for every resident. The staff member notes any resident who needs assistance.

The staff member conducting the drill sounds the alarm or uses the actual alarm system and starts a timer. Staff help each resident leave by the closest safe exit, using individualized supports from the resident's plan.
Staff count residents at the meeting place and confirm that everyone who was in the home is accounted for. Staff check rooms and bathrooms as part of the sweep.

The staff member stops the timer when everyone is outside and accounted for. The staff member records the date, the time of day, the exits used, the total evacuation time, the residents and staff who took part, and any problems.
The person conducting the drill signs the drill record the same day. The operator reviews and initials the record within 7 days.

If a drill reveals a problem, such as a blocked exit, slow evacuation, a resident who did not respond or a non-working alarm, the operator corrects it and records the correction. The operator may repeat the drill to confirm the fix.
Staff keep drill records in the home's office for at least one year and make them available to APD on request. The operator permits Regional Office staff to observe drills and notes the observation.

The operator arranges the annual fire inspection under Chapter 69A-38, F.A.C., with the local fire authority before the current inspection expires. The operator keeps the approved inspection on file for initial licensure and every renewal and corrects any cited deficiency promptly.

At admission, and again whenever a resident's needs change, the nurse or operator identifies each resident who depends on a medically essential service. The operator documents the resident's device, power needs and vendor contact.

For each such resident, the operator maintains and tests backup equipment or power, such as battery backup, portable oxygen supply or a generator. The operator writes a power outage plan with the vendor, utility and emergency contacts, and shelter or relocation steps. Staff are trained on the plan, and it is stored with the CEMP.

The operator posts emergency numbers at every phone extension. These include 911, the Florida Abuse Hotline (1-800-962-2873), the Regional Office, the operator and the backup operator at [PHONE]. Staff verify the postings monthly.

During any emergency or evacuation, staff follow SDA-01, protect residents first, and report as required to the Regional Office. Evacuations are reported within 6 hours and every 6 hours after. Emergency shelter over capacity is reported within 48 hours.
Staff are trained on the CEMP and drill procedures within 30 days of hire and annually. The operator documents attendance.

responsibilities.duty: Schedules drills, reviews records, arranges annual fire inspection, ensures backup power plans exist and are tested, and corrects problems.
Conduct and take part in drills, assist residents to evacuate, complete and sign drill records, and report equipment or exit problems.
Identifies residents who depend on medically essential services and helps develop outage plans (see HW-02).
Conducts the annual fire inspection under Chapter 69A-38, F.A.C.

documentation: Monthly fire drill records (date, time of day, exits used, evacuation time, signature of person conducting), kept 1 year
Drill calendar and corrective action notes
Approved annual fire inspection report
Power outage and backup equipment plan for each resident with a medically essential service, and equipment test records
Emergency number posting verification
CEMP training attendance records

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
policies.applies_to: All direct support staff, nurses, the facility operator and residents of [AGENCY NAME] group homes
policies.purpose: To reduce the risk of infection and the spread of communicable disease for residents and staff. This includes protection from bloodborne pathogens, safe sanitation and waste handling, and required training.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps each home clean and sanitary, as required by the General Residential Facility Standards in Rule 65G-2.007, F.A.C. All staff complete HIV/AIDS training within 90 days of hire as required by Rule 65G-2.008, F.A.C. The agency maintains a written bloodborne pathogen exposure control plan under the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030. The plan includes personal protective equipment (PPE) and an offer of the hepatitis B vaccine to staff with occupational exposure risk. The Florida Department of Health does not inspect APD-licensed group homes. APD monitors compliance with sanitation and health standards, and [AGENCY NAME] keeps the home ready for monitoring at all times. Sanitation, laundry, linens and waste handling are part of the home's standards and are managed as set out below. This policy has no items on the state's official checklist. It is adopted to meet the standards cited above.

definitions.definition: Microorganisms in human blood that can cause disease, including HIV, hepatitis B and hepatitis C.
Infection control practices applied to all residents at all times, including hand hygiene, PPE and safe handling of blood, body fluids and sharps.
Personal protective equipment such as gloves, gowns, masks and eye protection.
A specific eye, mouth, other mucous membrane, non-intact skin or parenteral contact with blood or other potentially infectious material during staff duties.

procedures: The operator maintains a written Exposure Control Plan that identifies tasks with exposure risk. The plan covers PPE, hand hygiene, cleanup, sharps handling, waste disposal and post-exposure follow-up. The operator reviews it at least annually and updates it as needed.
Within 90 days of hire, every staff member completes HIV/AIDS training. The operator records the completion date and the trainer in the personnel file (see STF-04 and STF-06).

Before a staff member has potential exposure, the operator offers the hepatitis B vaccine at no cost to the employee. Staff who decline sign a written declination and may accept later. Records are kept in a confidential file.
Staff practice standard precautions with every resident. They wash hands before and after care, before preparing or serving food, after toileting assistance and after removing gloves.
The operator keeps gloves, other PPE, hand soap, paper towels, hand sanitizer and disinfectant available in sufficient quantity in each home. Staff check supplies weekly and reorder when low.
Staff clean and disinfect bathrooms, kitchen surfaces, door handles, shared equipment and other high-touch areas daily. They follow a written cleaning schedule and initial the cleaning log.

Staff wash laundry soiled with blood or body fluids separately, wearing gloves. They launder linens and clothing at settings that clean effectively and handle soiled items minimally. Resident linens are changed at least weekly and whenever soiled.

Staff place sharps, such as lancets and needles, in labeled puncture-resistant containers and dispose of them as regulated medical waste. Staff bag soiled dressings, briefs and other waste and remove it from the home regularly.
After any spill of blood or body fluid, staff put on PPE, contain and clean the spill, and disinfect the area with an approved disinfectant. They dispose of materials safely and wash their hands.

Staff who have an exposure incident wash the area immediately, notify the operator and seek medical evaluation without delay. The operator completes an exposure incident report, documents the follow-up offered and keeps it in a confidential file.

Staff who are ill with symptoms of a communicable disease, such as fever, vomiting, diarrhea or a rash of unknown cause, do not work until cleared under STF-05. Staff notify the operator before the shift begins.

When a resident has signs of infection or a communicable disease, staff notify the nurse and follow the nurse's or physician's direction. Staff document the symptoms and follow HW-04. The operator takes reasonable steps to protect other residents while protecting the ill resident's dignity and privacy.

Staff teach and support residents in hand washing and personal hygiene, in line with each resident's plan. Staff encourage the preventive care ordered by the resident's physician, such as vaccines, with the resident's consent (see IR-07).
The operator reviews infection-related incidents and trends during quality improvement under GOV-04 and updates practices as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the Exposure Control Plan, supplies, training, vaccine offers and exposure incident follow-up, and ensures the home is clean and ready for APD monitoring.
Advises on infection concerns, guides response to resident illness and supports staff training.
Follow standard precautions, complete cleaning tasks, use PPE correctly, and report illness and exposure incidents.
Are supported and encouraged, according to their plans, to practice good hygiene and take part in a clean home.

documentation: Written Bloodborne Pathogen Exposure Control Plan with annual review date
HIV/AIDS training completion records
Hepatitis B vaccine offer, acceptance or declination forms
Exposure incident reports and follow-up records (confidential)
Cleaning schedule and logs
Supply inventory checks

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
policies.applies_to: Facility operator, direct support staff, nurse or dietitian consultants and residents of [AGENCY NAME] group homes
policies.purpose: To make sure residents receive safe, nutritious meals that meet their medical, behavioral and dietary needs and personal preferences, and that adequate food and water are always on hand.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 65G-2.007(13)(f), F.A.C. (Menus). Menus are planned, written and dated at least two days before the food is consumed. Resident participation in meal planning is recommended, and [AGENCY NAME] invites and supports it. Meals are developed in accordance with each resident's individual medical, behavioral and dietary requirements, consistent with Rule 65G-2.007(13)(e). The home keeps at least two days of fresh food and five days of staple food and drinking water on hand, in accordance with the menu, consistent with Rule 65G-2.007(13)(g). Residents have access to food at any time, consistent with HCBS setting requirements. Any limit on that access is a rights restriction and is handled only under IR-03. Modified diets, such as texture-modified, thickened liquid, diabetic or allergy diets, are provided only as ordered by a licensed practitioner and recorded in the resident's plan.

definitions.definition: A diet changed in texture, consistency, content or amount as ordered by a licensed health care practitioner or required by a documented medical need.
Perishable foods such as fruit, vegetables, milk, eggs, meat and bread that require prompt use or refrigeration.
Shelf-stable foods such as canned goods, rice, pasta, cereal and dried or long-life items.
A written, dated plan of meals and snacks to be served.

procedures: At admission, the nurse or operator records each resident's dietary orders, allergies, swallowing or choking concerns, preferences, and cultural or religious food practices. These are entered in the individual plan and posted in the kitchen in a way that protects privacy.

Each week, staff and residents together plan menus and write and date them at least two days before the food is served. Residents choose meals and snacks to the extent possible, and staff record the choices made.

Before finalizing the menu, a staff member compares it to every resident's ordered diet. Meals that conflict are adjusted. Modified versions of meals are listed on the menu for each affected resident.
Staff post the current menu in a place residents can see it. Staff note any substitution and the reason on the menu. Staff keep menus on file for at least [MENU RETENTION PERIOD] for review.
Staff shop for groceries based on the menu and resident preferences. They check dates on perishables and rotate stock.

Staff maintain at least two days of fresh food and five days of staple food and drinking water per the menu. Staff check supplies weekly and record the date, the person checking and the restock actions.
Staff store perishables in a refrigerator and freezer kept at safe temperatures. Staff check the temperature of each and record it at least weekly. They discard food that has expired or is spoiled.

Staff prepare, cook, cool and store food under safe food-handling practices, including hand washing, clean surfaces, separation of raw and ready-to-eat foods, and cooking to safe temperatures (see HES-03).

Staff serve modified diets exactly as ordered. They follow texture, liquid thickness, portion and supervision requirements, including choking-risk precautions in HW-03. Staff do not change a diet order without a written order from the practitioner.
Staff support residents at mealtimes in the ways written in their plans, including adaptive utensils and positioning. Staff encourage independence and a dignified dining experience.

Residents have access to food and drink at any time of day or night, including snacks and water. If a medical need such as a documented condition requires a limit, the limit is reviewed and approved only through the process in IR-03.
Staff record unusual intake, refusal of meals, weight changes, swallowing difficulty or signs of dehydration. They report these concerns to the nurse and follow HW-04 when the concern is urgent.
The nurse reviews weights and nutrition-related concerns with the operator at least quarterly, and the operator refers residents to a physician or registered dietitian when indicated.
The operator keeps emergency food and water supplies and instructions in the CEMP (SDA-01) and rotates them regularly.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures menus, food supplies and diet orders meet this policy and reviews weekly records.
Plan menus with residents, prepare and serve meals safely, follow diet orders and record findings.
Reviews diet orders, assists with modified diets and monitors weight and nutrition concerns.
Take part in meal planning and choose foods according to their preferences and plans.

documentation: Written, dated weekly menus
Diet orders and dietary information in the individual plan
Weekly food and water supply check log
Refrigerator and freezer temperature logs
Meal intake, weight and nutrition concern notes
Rights restriction documentation, if any (IR-03)

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
policies.applies_to: Facility operator, direct support staff who drive or assist with transportation, and residents of [AGENCY NAME] group homes
policies.purpose: To make sure residents travel safely in the community and that staff who transport residents are qualified and meet safety standards.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 65G-2.008(4)(b)-(c), F.A.C. (Safety standards). [AGENCY NAME] allows only staff who hold a valid driver license and have no qualifying violation within the previous 3 years to transport residents. The operator updates each such staff member's driving history at least annually. At least annually, the operator accesses the FDLE Sexual Offender/Predator Database for registrants within a one-mile radius of each home, notifies staff of the results and documents the notification. Transportation is provided in line with Rule 65G-2.009(14), F.A.C. Residents are transported in vehicles that are safe, maintained and equipped for their needs. Seat belts are used, and wheelchair securement is used for residents who ride in wheelchairs. The agency carries automobile liability coverage for any vehicle used to transport residents and keeps vehicle maintenance records. Transportation access supports community integration under PCS-05.

definitions.definition: A driving violation or record that disqualifies a staff member from transporting residents under the rule and agency policy, such as a license suspension or serious moving violations within the previous 3 years.
The staff member's official motor vehicle record from the Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles or the issuing state.
The Florida Department of Law Enforcement Sexual Offender/Predator database.
Equipment that safely secures a wheelchair or mobility device and its occupant in a vehicle.

procedures: At hire, the operator confirms that each staff member who will drive residents has a valid driver license. The operator obtains the driving history and verifies no qualifying violation within the past 3 years. Staff with a qualifying violation do not transport residents.

The operator obtains an updated driving history for every staff member who transports residents at least once every 12 months. The operator records the date, the result and the reviewer's initials in the personnel file (see STF-06).

Staff must tell the operator within 1 business day of any license suspension, revocation or traffic citation that could affect driving eligibility. The operator removes the staff member from driving duties until the matter is reviewed.
At least annually, the operator accesses the FDLE Sexual Offender/Predator Database and checks for registrants within a one-mile radius of each home.
The operator notifies all staff in writing of the results of the FDLE check. The operator records the date of the check, the names of those notified and the results in the facility file.
Before each trip, the driver checks that the vehicle is in safe working order: tires, lights, brakes, fuel, doors and seat belts. The driver does not use a vehicle with a safety defect.

The driver makes sure every resident is seated with a seat belt fastened. The driver loads residents who use wheelchairs by using the vehicle lift or ramp, and secures both the chair and the resident according to the manufacturer's instructions.

Staff who transport residents follow each resident's individual plan, including any seating, supervision, behavior support or medical needs. They carry emergency contact information and any needed medication, supplies or equipment.
Staff do not leave a resident unattended in a vehicle. Staff do not use a handheld phone or otherwise drive while distracted.
In an accident, breakdown or emergency, staff call 911 if anyone may be injured, move residents to safety, call the operator and follow HW-04 and BSP-04. Staff document the event the same day.
The operator maintains automobile liability coverage on every vehicle used to transport residents and keeps proof of coverage on file (see GOV-06).

The operator keeps a maintenance schedule and records for each vehicle, including oil changes, tire and brake checks, inspections and repairs. The operator corrects defects promptly and removes unsafe vehicles from service.
Staff keep a trip log for agency vehicles that records date, driver, destination and any incident. The operator reviews the logs monthly.
The operator reviews transportation incidents and vehicle issues during quality improvement under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Verifies driver eligibility, updates driving histories annually, completes the annual FDLE check and staff notification, and maintains vehicles and insurance.
Maintain a valid license, report violations, check vehicles, use seat belts and securement, and follow each resident's transportation supports.
Use seat belts and the supports in their plans, and give feedback on transportation needs and preferences.

documentation: Driver license verification and annual driving history updates in personnel files
Annual FDLE Sexual Offender/Predator Database check and documented staff notification
Vehicle maintenance and inspection records
Proof of automobile liability coverage
Trip logs and accident or incident reports
Driver reports of violations and the operator's decisions

policies.title: Staffing Ratios, Supervision and Awake Overnight Staff
policies.applies_to: Facility operator, scheduling staff and all direct support staff of [AGENCY NAME] group homes
policies.purpose: To make sure each home has enough qualified staff at all times to meet residents' needs, to meet the minimum direct-care hours required for Residential Habilitation, and to keep the staffing schedules the rules require.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 65G-2.009(6)(b), F.A.C. (Resident left alone for limited periods, written plan) and Rule 65G-2.008(6)(a)4, F.A.C. (Weekly staff schedules). [AGENCY NAME] employs adequate staff for the number and characteristics of the residents, even above the minimum, as required by Rule 65G-2.008(1). At least one staff member is present at all times residents are in the facility, under Rule 65G-2.009(6). A resident is left alone for limited periods only under a written plan prepared by [AGENCY NAME] that proposes it for a specified resident, either day or night, and the Regional Office approves the plan before it is implemented. The agency meets the iBudget Residential Habilitation minimum direct-care hours per resident per 24 hours: Basic 2, Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8 and Extensive 2 11. The agency posts a weekly written schedule showing staff coverage at least one week in advance. Weekly schedules of actual staff coverage are kept for six months and provided to the Regional Office within three calendar days on request. Overnight staffing follows each resident's individual plan and risk assessment. The rule requires staff presence at all times, and the operator confirms any awake-overnight requirement in the individual plan or APD approval.

definitions.definition: Hours that qualified direct support staff spend providing care, supervision and support to residents, counted toward the minimum for Residential Habilitation.
The iBudget level assigned to each resident (Basic, Minimal, Moderate, Extensive 1 or Extensive 2) that sets the minimum direct-care hours.
A staff member who is on duty and awake throughout the overnight hours, as required by a resident's plan or APD approval.
A resident remaining in the home without staff for a defined, short time under a written plan approved in advance by the Regional Office.

procedures: For each home, the operator lists every resident, the resident's current support level and any behavior focus or other designation. The operator updates the list when a level changes, someone is admitted or someone leaves.

The operator multiplies the number of residents at each level by the minimum daily direct-care hours (Basic 2, Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8, Extensive 2 11) and adds the results. For example, 2 Minimal, 3 Moderate and 1 Extensive 1 residents require at least 8 + 18 + 8 = 34 direct-care hours per day.

The operator builds the weekly schedule so the daily or weekly total of scheduled direct-care hours meets or exceeds that minimum. The operator adds staff above the minimum when residents' needs, behavior supports, medical needs or the CEMP require it.

The operator reviews each resident's individual plan, behavior plan, health needs, risk assessments and APD approvals to decide what supervision is needed, including awake overnight coverage. The operator documents the decision and the source for each home.
The operator makes sure at least one staff member is in the home at all times that any resident is present. No shift is left uncovered, and a staff member does not leave until relieved (see PCS-04).

The operator posts a written weekly schedule showing staff names, shifts and coverage, in a place staff can see, at least one week in advance. The operator identifies the operator and backup on-call person on the schedule.
If the schedule changes, the operator records the change, the reason and the staff members involved. The posted schedule is updated, and the operator keeps the original version.

When a call-out or emergency leaves a shift short, the staff member on duty stays until relieved and calls the operator or backup at [PHONE]. The operator brings in a qualified replacement as quickly as possible and documents the gap and the response.

Only staff who meet screening and training requirements (see STF-02, STF-03 and STF-04) count toward coverage. Staff in the supervised 90-day period are scheduled in line with the supervision rules in STF-03.

If [AGENCY NAME] proposes that a resident be left alone for limited periods, the operator prepares a written plan naming the resident. The plan states the day or night periods, the length, the resident's skills and risks, emergency steps and how staff will check in.

The operator submits the plan to the Regional Office and does not implement it until written approval is received. The operator keeps the plan and approval in the resident's record and the facility file, and reviews it when the resident's condition or the home changes.

The operator keeps the actual schedule of staff coverage for each week, showing who actually worked and when, for six months. The operator provides copies to the Regional Office within three calendar days of a request.
Each week, the operator compares the actual hours worked to the required minimum direct-care hours. The operator investigates any shortfall, corrects it and records the action.

The operator reviews staffing levels at least quarterly in the quality improvement process (GOV-04), including overtime, call-outs, turnover and incident trends. The operator adjusts staffing as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Calculates required hours, builds and posts schedules, ensures coverage at all times, prepares any request to leave a resident alone, and keeps and produces schedules.
Is available by phone, arranges replacement coverage in emergencies and supports staff on duty.
Report to work as scheduled, remain until relieved, notify the operator of absences as early as possible and record the hours worked.
Approves any written plan to leave a resident alone for limited periods and may request schedules.

documentation: Resident support level list and minimum direct-care hour calculation
Posted weekly staff schedules
Actual staff coverage schedules kept six months
Schedule change and coverage-gap records
Written plan to leave a resident alone for limited periods and Regional Office approval, if applicable
Individual plan or APD approval documenting awake-overnight requirements
Quarterly staffing review in the quality improvement records

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
policies.applies_to: Licensee/applicant, facility operator, managers, supervisors, all direct support staff (full-time, part-time, relief), and any other person with access to residents' living areas, funds or property
policies.purpose: To make sure that no one works in [AGENCY NAME] until Level 2 screening shows they are eligible, that eligibility is tracked for as long as they work here, and that safety checks required of licensed group homes (driving history of staff who transport residents, and the annual sexual offender/predator database check) are completed and documented.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires Level 2 background screening under chapter 435, F.S., as required by s. 393.067(5) and s. 393.0655, F.S., for the applicant/licensee, the facility operator, managers, supervisors and every direct service staff member before that person works. Screening also applies to anyone, whether employee, relief worker, volunteer or contractor, who has access to residents' living areas, funds or property. Screening results are managed through the AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse (s. 435.12, F.S.), where [AGENCY NAME] registers, tracks each person's eligibility and monitors rescreening. A person who is not eligible does not work. An exemption from disqualification is accepted only as provided in s. 435.07, F.S., and only after the exemption is granted in writing. This policy meets Rule 65G-2.008(4)(b)-(c) (checklist cite 65G-2.008(4)(b)2., (4)(c)): (1) the driving history of every staff member who transports residents is updated at least annually, and (2) at least annually the Administrator accesses the FDLE Sexual Offender/Predator Database for registrants within a one-mile radius of the home, notifies staff, and documents the notification.

definitions.definition: Fingerprint-based state and national criminal history screening under chapter 435, F.S., required for direct service providers, managers and supervisors of licensed residential facilities.
The AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse, where screening results are stored and where employers register and track employee eligibility.
Any person who has direct contact with residents, or access to their living areas, funds or property, including paid staff, relief staff and contractors.
A status in the Clearinghouse showing the person has no disqualifying offense, or has been granted an exemption under s. 435.07, F.S.
The Florida Department of Law Enforcement public registry of registered sexual offenders and predators, searchable by address and radius.

procedures: Before recruiting for any position, the Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) confirms the role is covered by screening: licensee/applicant, operator, manager, supervisor, DSP, relief staff, and any person with access to living areas, funds or property (including maintenance workers, housekeepers, volunteers and contractors who are not escorted at all times).

The Administrator registers [AGENCY NAME] in the Clearinghouse, names a Screening Coordinator and a backup, and keeps the account current. The Screening Coordinator is the only person who may view or record screening results.

The Screening Coordinator gives each candidate written notice that employment is contingent on Level 2 screening, and sends the candidate for electronic fingerprinting at an approved vendor, with the agency's Clearinghouse information, before the first day of work.

The Screening Coordinator links the candidate to [AGENCY NAME] in the Clearinghouse and checks the result. No one is scheduled, shadowed, left alone with residents, or given access to funds, property or living areas until the Clearinghouse shows 'eligible.'

If the result shows a disqualifying offense, the person is not hired or is removed from duty the same day. The Administrator decides whether to support an exemption request. An exemption is requested only under s. 435.07, F.S., and the person does not work until the exemption is granted in writing.
The Screening Coordinator prints or saves the eligibility confirmation and files it in the person's personnel record (STF-06), with the date checked and the initials of the person who checked it.

The Screening Coordinator reviews the Clearinghouse employer list monthly and records upcoming rescreening or expiration dates on the screening tracking log. Anyone whose status changes to ineligible or who is not rescreened by the due date is removed from duty until eligibility is restored.

Every employee must tell the Administrator within one business day if they are arrested for, charged with or convicted of any offense. The Administrator reviews the matter with the Screening Coordinator the same day and removes the person from duty if eligibility is in doubt.
When an employee separates, the Screening Coordinator removes the person from the agency's Clearinghouse employment list within five business days and records the date on the tracking log.

Contract and volunteer access: no contractor or volunteer is given unescorted access to living areas, funds or property unless screened and eligible. Unscreened visitors are escorted at all times by a screened staff member and are never left alone with residents.

FDLE database check: at least once every 12 months, and before each license renewal, the Administrator searches the FDLE Sexual Offender/Predator Database for registrants whose addresses are within a one-mile radius of the home, and prints or saves the results with the search date.

Within five business days of each search, the Administrator notifies all staff in writing of the results (including a statement of 'none found' if applicable). Each staff member signs an acknowledgement. New staff receive the most recent notification during orientation. If the Administrator learns of a new registrant within one mile between searches, staff are notified within two business days.
The Administrator shares relevant results with each resident's support team through PCS-02 so that community and safety planning reflects them, while respecting IR-05.

Annual driving history: at least once every 12 months, the Administrator obtains an updated driving record for every staff member who transports residents, and also obtains a driving record before the person first transports residents.

The Administrator reviews each record against the driver standard in Rule 65G-2.008(4) (no qualifying violation in the previous three years). Anyone who does not meet the standard stops transporting residents immediately, and the Administrator documents the reassignment. HES-05 governs vehicle use.

The Administrator files the FDLE search results, staff notification and signature sheet, and the driving history updates in the screening and safety file and in each individual's personnel record. Copies are given to the Regional Office within 3 calendar days if requested (STF-06).
The Quality Improvement Committee audits the screening tracking log, the FDLE annual check and the driving-history updates at least annually and reports gaps to the governing body (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures no one works before eligibility is confirmed; completes the annual FDLE database check, staff notification and driving history reviews; decides on removal from duty.
Maintains the Clearinghouse account, confirms eligibility, tracks rescreening dates, and files confirmations in personnel records.

Complete fingerprinting before working, report any arrest within one business day, review and sign the annual FDLE notification, and tell the Administrator about any change affecting their driving record.
Reviews screening compliance audits at least annually.

documentation: Clearinghouse eligibility confirmation for each person, with date checked, in the personnel record
Screening tracking log (rescreening dates, status changes, removals)
Exemption decision letters, if any
Annual FDLE database search results with date and name of searcher
Staff notification of FDLE results and signed acknowledgements
Annual driving history for each transporting staff member and the Administrator's review note
Record of any removal from duty or reassignment for screening or driving reasons

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Qualifications and Hiring
policies.applies_to: Administrator, hiring managers and all applicants and employees in direct support professional (DSP) positions
policies.purpose: To ensure every direct support professional meets the minimum qualifications of Rule 65G-2.008 before working alone with residents, that staff without prior experience are supervised and evaluated as the rule requires, and that the facility operator meets the standards of Rule 65G-2.0072.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] hires as a direct support professional only a person who is at least 18 years old; has cleared screening under chapter 435 and s. 393.0655, F.S. (STF-02); holds a high school diploma or equivalent; and has either one year of relevant experience or 30 semester hours, 45 quarter hours or 720 classroom hours of related training (Rule 65G-2.008(2)). A person who lacks the experience or training may be hired only under the supervised 90-day alternative in Rule 65G-2.008(2)(f)-(h): the person works under supervision for 90 days, [AGENCY NAME] sends written notice to the Regional Office within 5 days of hire, and a performance evaluation is completed within 120 days. Each DSP must have the skills required by Rule 65G-2.008(3) and meet fitness-for-duty standards under Rule 65G-2.008(4) (STF-05). [AGENCY NAME] employs enough staff for the number and characteristics of the residents, even if that is above the minimum (Rule 65G-2.008(1); STF-01). The facility operator meets Rule 65G-2.0072: 90 college credits in a related field, or a high school diploma plus 3 years of disability-related experience, and is on site or on call at all times with a designated backup.

definitions.definition: An employee who provides residential habilitation, care and supervision directly to residents.

The option in Rule 65G-2.008(2)(f)-(h) to hire a person who lacks the required experience or training, provided the person works under supervision for 90 days, the Regional Office is notified in writing within 5 days of hire, and a performance evaluation is done within 120 days.
30 semester hours, 45 quarter hours or 720 classroom hours of coursework or training relevant to supporting persons with developmental disabilities.
The person named in writing to act for the facility operator when the operator is not on site or reachable.

procedures: The Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) maintains a written DSP job description (see STF-06) that lists the minimum qualifications and the skills required by Rule 65G-2.008(3), and posts openings using it.
Each applicant completes a written application listing education, work history, relevant training and references, and signs a statement that the information is true.
The hiring manager verifies age with government-issued photo identification and copies it for the personnel file.
