The hiring manager verifies the diploma or equivalent (copy, transcript or the issuing institution's confirmation) and files it.

The hiring manager verifies one year of relevant experience through previous employer contact or written reference, or verifies 30 semester / 45 quarter / 720 classroom hours of related training through transcripts or certificates. Verification is documented with date, source and initials.
At least two references are checked, and notes are filed. Concerns about prior abuse, neglect or exploitation of vulnerable persons stop the hiring process until reviewed by the Administrator.
The Screening Coordinator completes Level 2 screening through the Clearinghouse (STF-02). No offer becomes effective and no work starts until the person is shown as eligible.
The hiring manager assesses the skills in Rule 65G-2.008(3) through interview and a documented skills check against the job description, and records the results.
The hiring manager confirms fitness for duty under STF-05 and, for any position that includes driving residents, completes the driving history review in STF-02.

If the applicant lacks the required experience or training, the Administrator may use the supervised 90-day alternative. The Administrator names a qualified supervising staff member in writing, and the new DSP is never counted alone in the ratio or left alone with residents during the 90 days.

The Administrator sends written notice of the hire under the supervised alternative to the [REGION] Regional Office within 5 days of the hire date and files a copy with proof of delivery in the personnel record.
The supervising staff member documents supervision at least weekly during the 90 days, covering observed tasks, coaching and concerns.

The Administrator completes a written performance evaluation within 120 days of hire, shares it with the employee, and files it. Continued employment under the alternative requires a satisfactory evaluation. The employee must also complete the required training in STF-04 in the times stated there.

Before the start date, the Administrator gives the new hire the job description, resident rights and house rules materials, and the reporting duty for abuse, neglect and exploitation, and obtains signed acknowledgements.
The Administrator reviews staffing each month against resident needs, and adds staff above the minimum when resident characteristics require it (STF-01).

Operator qualifications: the Administrator keeps proof of the education or experience required by Rule 65G-2.0072, and keeps a written designation of a backup operator with current contact information, posted in the office area and given to all staff. [AGENCY NAME] confirms that the operator or backup can be reached at all times, including nights and weekends, at [PHONE].

responsibilities.duty: Approves all hires, ensures qualifications are verified, sends Regional Office notice for supervised-alternative hires within 5 days, and completes 120-day evaluations.
Verifies age, education, experience/training and references, and assesses required skills.
Supervises the new DSP during the 90-day alternative and documents supervision weekly.
Confirms Level 2 eligibility before any work (STF-02).

documentation: Application, identification copy and diploma/equivalent verification
Experience or related-training verification with date and verifier
Reference check notes
Clearinghouse eligibility confirmation
Skills assessment against Rule 65G-2.008(3)
Supervised-alternative supervisor designation and weekly supervision notes
Written notice to the Regional Office (within 5 days of hire) with proof of delivery
120-day performance evaluation
Signed acknowledgements and job description
Operator qualification proof and backup designation

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Orientation and Training
policies.applies_to: All direct support professionals, relief staff, managers and supervisors who provide or oversee direct care
policies.purpose: To make sure every staff member is trained in the topics required by Rule 65G-2.008(7) and related rules within required timeframes, and that training is documented and retained.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] trains all direct care staff before they are counted in staffing ratios or work without supervision, and keeps written documentation of all required training for at least three years. This policy meets Rule 65G-2.008(7)(c)-(g) (checklist cite 65G-2.008(7)(b)-(g)): (c) Zero Tolerance training on detection, prevention and reporting of abuse, neglect and exploitation is completed before any direct services are provided, with a refresher at least every three years; (d) basic first aid and CPR certification is completed within 90 days of hire in a classroom setting (online-only training is not accepted), and at least one CPR-certified staff member is on site whenever residents are present; (e) staff are trained on each resident's current behavior plan by a certified behavior analyst, with documentation in the personnel record; (f) [AGENCY NAME] complies with chapter 65G-8, F.A.C.; and (g) written documentation of required training is retained for at least three years. Staff must also complete the Direct Care Core Competencies and HIV/AIDS training within 90 days of hire, and training on the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan within 30 days of hire and annually (Rule 65G-2.010(4)). Unlicensed staff do not administer medication until they have completed the APD Basic Medication Administration course and been validated (Rule 65G-7.004).

definitions.definition: Training on detection, prevention and reporting of abuse, neglect and exploitation, required before providing direct services and refreshed every three years.
The APD-required core training for direct care staff, to be completed within 90 days of hire.
A behavior analyst certified as required by APD who trains staff on residents' behavior plans.
CPR and first aid training with in-person instruction and skills demonstration. Online-only courses do not satisfy the requirement.
Observation and approval of an unlicensed staff member's medication administration skills by an APD-approved validator after the Basic Medication Administration course.
Emergency procedures used in response to dangerous behavior, which may only be used by staff certified in an APD-approved curriculum.

procedures: The Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) designates a Training Coordinator and keeps a training matrix for each employee showing every required course, due date, completion date and expiration date.

On the first day, before any direct service, the Training Coordinator enrolls the new hire in Zero Tolerance training and completes it. The staff member does not provide direct services or work alone until the certificate is filed. The refresher is scheduled in the matrix for no later than three years after completion.
Within 30 days of hire, the Training Coordinator trains the new hire on the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan and fire/evacuation procedures (SDA-01, HES-02), and repeats this annually.

Within 90 days of hire, the staff member completes the Direct Care Core Competencies and HIV/AIDS training. The Training Coordinator reviews progress at 30 and 60 days and informs the Administrator of any risk of missing the deadline.

Within 90 days of hire, the staff member completes classroom basic first aid and CPR with an accredited provider. Online-only certificates are rejected and the course repeated in a classroom. Renewal is scheduled before the certificate expires.

The Administrator builds the schedule so that at least one CPR-certified staff member is on site at all times when residents are present, and documents this on the weekly schedule (STF-01). New hires still within the 90-day period do not count as the CPR-certified person unless already certified.

Before working with any resident, and whenever a plan is changed, a certified behavior analyst trains the staff member on that resident's current behavior plan (BSP-01). The Training Coordinator records the date, trainer, plan version and attendees, and places the record in the staff member's personnel record.

[AGENCY NAME] checks whether it uses reactive strategies. If so, only staff who have completed the APD-approved emergency procedure curriculum (at least 12 direct hours, written test with a minimum 80% score, certification valid for one year) may use any technique, and certification is renewed annually before it expires. If not, staff are told that no reactive technique is authorized and are trained on the prohibition in BSP-02. The Administrator confirms the current text of chapter 65G-8 at least annually, because APD revisions are in development.

Unlicensed staff may not administer medication until they pass the APD Basic Medication Administration course (at least 85% on the exam and 100% on the MAR section) and are validated by an approved validator (HW-01). The Training Coordinator tracks the annual update and revalidates each person within the 60 days before expiry. Anyone whose certification lapses stops administering medication immediately.

New hires complete orientation on resident rights, house rules, confidentiality, resident-specific supports in each Individual Plan, incident reporting procedures and the Abuse Hotline (1-800-962-2873), before working alone.
Each training session is recorded on a sign-in sheet with date, content, trainer name and credentials, and staff in attendance. Certificates are copied and filed.
The Training Coordinator updates the matrix within 2 business days of every course and gives the Administrator a monthly report of upcoming and overdue training.

Staff who miss a due date are removed from duties that depend on the training (for example, unsupervised care, driving or medication) until completed, and the Administrator documents the corrective action.
Training records are kept in each staff member's personnel record (STF-06) and retained for at least three years, longer if the agency's records schedule (GOV-03) requires.
On request, training records are given to the Regional Office within 3 calendar days (STF-06).
The QI Committee reviews training completion rates at least annually and the governing body acts on gaps (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures all required training is completed on time, removes untrained staff from affected duties, and confirms the schedule has a CPR-certified person on site.
Maintains the training matrix, schedules courses, collects documentation and reports overdue items.
Trains staff on each resident's current behavior plan and documents attendance.
Complete required training on time, bring certificates and report any lapse.

documentation: Training matrix per employee
Zero Tolerance certificate (before direct services) and refresher record
Direct Care Core Competencies and HIV/AIDS completion records
Classroom CPR/first aid certificate
Behavior plan training record (date, trainer, plan version, attendees)
Chapter 65G-8 certification records, if reactive strategies are used, or written statement that none are authorized
CEMP training record (within 30 days of hire and annually)
Medication course certificate, validation and annual update/revalidation records
Sign-in sheets and certificates retained at least 3 years

policies.title: Employee Health, Fitness for Duty and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief staff and applicants for direct support and supervisory positions
federal: Americans with Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.)
policies.purpose: To ensure staff are fit to carry out their duties safely, that employee health information is protected, and that infection control practices, including tuberculosis (TB) screening and bloodborne pathogen protections, are applied consistently.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires every staff member to meet the fitness-for-duty standards of Rule 65G-2.008(4), including the driver standards for anyone who transports residents (no qualifying violation in the previous three years and an annual driving-history update, STF-02). Fitness-for-duty requirements are applied consistently and in line with the Americans with Disabilities Act: the agency asks only job-related questions and provides reasonable accommodation where possible. No TB testing requirement was found in chapter 65G-2, F.A.C.; [AGENCY NAME] therefore follows its own health screening standard and the guidance of the Florida Department of Health. Health information is kept in a confidential file separate from the personnel file. In line with the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030), the hepatitis B vaccine is offered to staff with occupational exposure risk, at no cost to the employee.

definitions.definition: The ability of a staff member to perform the essential functions of the job safely, with or without reasonable accommodation, and without risk to residents, themselves or others.
A change in the job, schedule or work setting that allows a qualified person with a disability to perform essential job functions, as required by the ADA.
A locked file kept apart from the personnel record that contains employee medical and health screening information.
Reasonably anticipated contact with blood or other potentially infectious materials while performing job duties.

procedures: The job description lists the essential functions of the DSP role, including lifting and transfer, supervision, emergency evacuation, driving, and medication tasks where applicable. Applicants receive it before a conditional offer.

After a conditional offer, the Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) asks each candidate to confirm in writing that they can perform the essential functions with or without reasonable accommodation, and applies the same process to all candidates in the same job.

The Administrator may require a health screening after the conditional offer only if it is job-related and applied to all entering employees in that job. Results go only into the confidential health file.
The Administrator checks that the person meets the fitness-for-duty standards in Rule 65G-2.008(4), including applying the driver standards under STF-02 to every person who will transport residents.

TB screening: because chapter 65G-2 has no TB testing requirement, [AGENCY NAME] follows its own written standard. Before starting work, each new hire completes a TB symptom screening and, if the agency's health advisor or the Department of Health guidance recommends, a TB test. Results are filed in the confidential health file.

Positive symptom screens or test results are referred to the employee's health care provider and the county health department. The employee does not return to work until cleared in writing by a health care provider.
The Administrator offers the hepatitis B vaccine, at no cost, to staff with occupational exposure risk, and records acceptance or a signed declination.
Staff receive training on bloodborne pathogens and standard precautions, and the exposure control plan is explained, consistent with HES-03.

Staff exposed to blood or body fluids report the incident to the supervisor immediately, receive first aid, and are referred for medical evaluation the same day. The incident is documented, with confidentiality kept in the health file.

Employees must tell the Administrator before working if they have a contagious illness, symptoms (such as fever, vomiting, diarrhea or respiratory illness) or any condition that could affect the safe care of residents. The Administrator decides on exclusion from work or adjusted duties according to HES-03 and health authority guidance.

Staff must not work while impaired by alcohol, drugs, medication or fatigue. A supervisor who has a reasonable concern removes the person from duty, arranges a safe ride home, and documents objective observations.

Employees who need an accommodation may ask the Administrator at any time. The Administrator meets with the employee, documents the interactive process and the decision, and files it in the confidential health file.

All health and medical information is stored in a locked file separate from the personnel record, and is shared only with those who need it to apply restrictions or accommodations, or as the law requires.
The Administrator reviews fitness-for-duty and health screening practices annually, with the QI Committee, to make sure they are applied consistently (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Applies fitness-for-duty standards, handles accommodations, keeps the confidential health file and decides on work restrictions.
Observe for fitness-for-duty concerns, remove staff from duty when needed, and document observations.
Report contagious illness, exposures and conditions affecting safe work; complete required screening and vaccination decisions.

documentation: Job description with essential functions and signed fitness-for-duty confirmation
Confidential health file: TB symptom screen/test result, return-to-work clearances, accommodation records
Hepatitis B vaccine acceptance or signed declination
Bloodborne pathogen training record
Exposure incident and follow-up records
Records of removal from duty and reasons

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: Administrator, personnel record custodian and all paid staff (full-time and part-time)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] develops and maintains the personnel policies, procedures and records required by Rule 65G-2.008(6) and can produce them promptly for the Regional Office.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains the following personnel policies, procedures and records as required by Rule 65G-2.008(6)(a): (1) Rule 65G-2.008(6)(a)1 — a written job description for every paid staff position; (2) Rule 65G-2.008(6)(a)2 — documentation of all facility staff training, including a record of training dates, training content and trainers, and staff in attendance; and (3) Rule 65G-2.008(6)(a)3 — a separate personnel record for each full-time and part-time employee that contains written documentation of the employee's education, qualifications, experience, references, background screening, staff training participation, and any disciplinary action taken against the employee. Training documentation is retained at least three years. The weekly work schedule is posted one week ahead, actual schedules are kept for six months, and copies of personnel records and schedules are provided to APD within 3 calendar days of a request.

definitions.definition: A separate file for each full-time and part-time employee holding employment, qualification, screening, training and disciplinary documentation.
A written statement of the duties, qualifications and reporting relationship for each paid staff position.
The record of who actually worked each shift, which may differ from the posted schedule.
A separate locked file for employee medical information (STF-05); not part of the personnel record.

procedures: The Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) writes and approves a job description for every paid position (including DSP, house manager, relief staff and any administrative role), stating duties, qualifications, required skills, reporting line and supervisory responsibilities. Descriptions are reviewed at least annually and dated.
Each employee receives their job description at hire and signs an acknowledgement, which is filed in the personnel record.
The Administrator designates a personnel record custodian, who opens a separate personnel record for each full-time and part-time employee on or before the first day of work.

Each personnel record contains, at minimum: application; education verification; qualifications and experience verification; references; Clearinghouse eligibility confirmation and screening documentation (STF-02); driving history if the person transports residents; training participation records; job description acknowledgement; performance evaluation(s); and any disciplinary actions.
The record also contains notice to the Regional Office and the 120-day evaluation for any supervised-alternative hire (STF-03), and the behavior plan training documentation (STF-04).

The custodian keeps a checklist on the inside of each personnel record showing each required item, the date it was filed and the initials of the filer. The Administrator reviews each new record within 7 days of hire for completeness.

All staff training documentation is recorded on a training form or sign-in sheet that lists the training date, content, trainer and staff in attendance. Training records are filed in each attendee's personnel record and in a facility-wide training binder or file.
Training documentation is retained for at least three years. The custodian never removes training records before that date.

Disciplinary actions are written, dated, signed by the supervisor and the employee (or noted as refused), and filed in the personnel record on the day issued. Investigations of staff conduct are documented under BSP-04.
Medical information, TB results, accommodation requests and similar documents are not placed in the personnel record. They are stored in the separate confidential health file (STF-05).

Personnel records are stored in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system in the facility's designated office area, available only to the Administrator, the custodian and authorized licensing or monitoring personnel.

The Administrator posts the weekly work schedule at least one week ahead of the week it covers, and keeps the actual schedules (recording any change) for six months. Schedules show names and shift times (STF-01).

When the Regional Office or APD requests personnel records, schedules or training records, the custodian copies and delivers the requested records within 3 calendar days and logs the date and the person who received them.

Records of separated employees are kept for at least 5 years after separation (agency standard), and training records for at least three years, per the document control schedule in GOV-03. Records are destroyed only on the Administrator's written authorization.

The Administrator audits at least ten percent of personnel records each quarter (or all records if there are fewer than ten employees) for completeness and reports findings to the QI Committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Approves job descriptions, reviews each new personnel record, audits records, and authorizes release and destruction.
Opens and maintains records, files training and discipline documents, keeps the checklist, and responds to records requests within 3 calendar days.
Document discipline and evaluations promptly and give them to the custodian.
Provide accurate information and copies of certifications; sign acknowledgements.

documentation: Job descriptions with approval and review dates; signed employee acknowledgements
Separate personnel record for each full-time and part-time employee with completeness checklist
Training records: dates, content, trainers and attendees (retained at least 3 years)
Disciplinary action documentation
Posted weekly schedules and actual schedules retained 6 months
Records request log showing delivery within 3 calendar days
Quarterly personnel record audit results

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief staff, volunteers, interns and contractors who have contact with residents
policies.purpose: To set clear standards of conduct and professional boundaries so that residents are treated with dignity and are protected from abuse, neglect, exploitation and misuse of their funds or property.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] expects all staff to treat residents with respect and to maintain professional relationships. Staff follow the boundary standards in the Sexual Activity Policy (SDA-03), which implements Rule 65G-2.009(9). Solicitation of residents is governed by Rule 65G-2.009(10) and is prohibited. Staff must not use physical or corporal punishment, verbal abuse, threats, ridicule or humiliation. Staff may not borrow money or property from residents, accept gifts from residents, or use resident funds or property for their own benefit. Violations lead to discipline up to termination, and conduct that may constitute abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 (BSP-03). Staff receive training on this policy before working with residents (Rule 65G-2.008(7); STF-04).

definitions.definition: The limit that separates a staff member's professional role from personal, financial, romantic or sexual relationships with a resident.
Any physical act intended to cause pain or discomfort as discipline, such as hitting, slapping, pinching or forced physical exercise.
Yelling, name-calling, threats, sarcasm, ridicule, or any language or action meant to demean, frighten or embarrass a resident.
Taking or using a resident's money, property or services for the benefit of another person, including borrowing, gifts and misuse of funds.
Asking residents, or their representatives, for money, gifts, business, services or other benefits, as governed by Rule 65G-2.009(10).

procedures: At hire and annually, each staff member receives this policy and the Code of Conduct, completes training on boundaries and dignity (STF-04), and signs an acknowledgement that is filed in the personnel record (STF-06).

Staff address residents by their preferred names, offer choices, speak in age-appropriate language, and respect privacy, including knocking before entering bedrooms and bathrooms, consistent with IR-01 and IR-05.

Staff do not use physical or corporal punishment, verbal abuse, threats, ridicule, humiliation, withholding of food, or forced isolation. Behavior supports are limited to those in an approved plan (BSP-01, BSP-02).

Staff follow the sexual activity and boundary standards in SDA-03: no sexual contact, romantic relationships or sexualized communication between staff and residents, ever, regardless of resident consent. Staff who are concerned about a resident's sexual health or safety speak to the supervisor, and supports are put in place per SDA-03.

Staff do not solicit residents, families or representatives for money, gifts, loans, donations, business, votes or personal favors. [AGENCY NAME] applies this as a flat ban, in line with Rule 65G-2.009(10).

Staff do not borrow money or property from residents, accept gifts of value from residents, or sell items to residents. Staff do not use resident funds, food, vehicles or property for personal use. Residents' funds are handled only as stated in IR-06.

A staff member offered a gift by a resident or family declines politely. A token item of little value (such as a card or homemade craft) may be accepted if reported to the Administrator the same day and recorded in the gift log.

Staff do not give residents personal financial, legal or medical advice, share personal social media contacts, or conduct personal business with residents. Staff do not bring friends or family into the home to visit with residents without the Administrator's prior approval.
Staff do not take photos or videos of residents on personal devices, or post any information about residents on social media or messaging apps (IR-05).

Off-duty social, financial or romantic relationships with a resident or a resident's family member are not permitted. Any pre-existing relationship (such as a relative) is disclosed to the Administrator at hire so that safeguards can be set.

Any staff member who witnesses or suspects abuse, neglect, exploitation or a boundary violation reports it immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline (1-800-962-2873) and to the Administrator, as set out in BSP-03. Staff may not delay a report for a supervisor to review, and no one may retaliate against anyone who reports.

The Administrator removes the staff member from contact with residents pending review where there is a reasonable concern for resident safety, completes the incident report and notifications in BSP-04, and begins an internal investigation.
The Administrator documents the findings, decides on discipline (counseling, written warning, suspension or termination), and places the written disciplinary action in the personnel record (STF-06).

If a substantiated violation involves abuse, neglect or exploitation, or a staff member leaves while under investigation, the Administrator takes the steps in STF-02 regarding Clearinghouse status and fulfills reporting duties in REC-02.
The Administrator reviews boundary and conduct complaints and findings with the QI Committee at least quarterly, without identifying residents unnecessarily, and updates training as needed (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Enforces the policy, investigates concerns, imposes discipline, and ensures reports are made and documented.
Model professional conduct, observe staff-resident interaction, and report concerns immediately.
Maintain boundaries, avoid solicitation and personal gain, report violations, and sign acknowledgements.

documentation: Signed acknowledgement of Code of Conduct and boundary training in the personnel record
Gift log and disclosure of pre-existing relationships
Abuse Hotline report confirmation and incident report (BSP-03, BSP-04)
Investigation file and disciplinary action documentation in the personnel record
QI Committee review of conduct complaints and trends

policies.title: Wage and Hour Compliance and Workers' Compensation
policies.applies_to: All employees of [AGENCY NAME], including direct support professionals (DSPs), awake overnight staff, relief and on-call staff, the facility operator, and administrative staff.
policies.purpose: To make sure every employee of [AGENCY NAME] is paid correctly for all hours worked, and that employees are protected by workers' compensation insurance if they are hurt on the job. This protects staff, supports stable staffing for the people we serve, and keeps the agency in compliance with Florida and federal wage law.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] pays every employee at least the Florida minimum wage in effect on the date the work is performed, which is $15.00 per hour from September 30, 2026 (s. 448.110, F.S.; Fla. Const. art. X, s. 24). It also pays at least the federal minimum wage where that is higher. The agency pays overtime as required by the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA). It records and pays for all hours worked, including on-call time and overnight time that counts as hours worked. Direct support staff are treated as employees, not independent contractors, unless counsel has reviewed and approved a different classification in writing. [AGENCY NAME] maintains workers' compensation insurance as required by ch. 440, F.S. (s. 440.02, F.S., requires coverage for employers with four or more employees). The agency secures coverage before the first employee begins work. No employee may be asked or allowed to work off the clock, to waive pay, or to waive workers' compensation coverage.

definitions.definition: All time an employee is required or permitted to work, including time spent on duty in the home, supervising residents, in required training, in required meetings, driving residents, and completing documentation. It also includes on-call or overnight time during which the employee cannot freely use the time for personal purposes.
A fixed, recurring period of 168 hours (seven consecutive 24-hour days) set by [AGENCY NAME] at [WORKWEEK START DAY AND TIME]. Overtime is calculated per workweek and workweeks are not averaged.
Hours worked over 40 in a workweek, paid at one and one-half times the employee's regular rate of pay unless an FLSA exemption has been confirmed in writing.
The employee's hourly rate plus other pay required by the FLSA to be included, such as shift differentials and non-discretionary bonuses.
Time an employee is available to respond to the home or a resident. It is hours worked if the employee's freedom to use the time for personal purposes is significantly restricted.
Insurance required under ch. 440, F.S., that pays for medical care and wage-loss benefits when an employee is injured or becomes ill because of work.

procedures: The Administrator sets and documents the pay rate for each position. Before the hire date, the Administrator confirms the rate is at least the Florida minimum wage in effect, and at least $15.00 per hour for all work on or after September 30, 2026.

Before September 30, 2026, the Administrator reviews all pay rates and updates any rate below $15.00 per hour effective that date. The Administrator records the review and the date in the payroll file.

At hire, the Administrator or designee gives each employee a written statement of the hourly rate, the workweek definition, the pay schedule, and how to report time and pay problems. The employee signs and a copy is placed in the personnel record (STF-06).

Each employee records actual start and stop times for every shift and for any other work, including training, meetings, and transport. Employees record time on [TIME SYSTEM] on the day worked, not afterward from memory.
Employees must not perform work off the clock. A supervisor who learns that an employee is working unrecorded time must record and pay it and then correct the cause.

On-call and overnight time is reviewed by the Administrator. If the employee must remain in the home, stay awake, or respond to residents (see STF-01 for awake overnight requirements), all of the time is recorded and paid as hours worked. No time is deducted for sleep or meals unless the Administrator has confirmed in writing, after review by [WAGE-HOUR ADVISOR OR COUNSEL], that the requirements for a deduction are met and the employee has agreed in writing.
Unpaid meal periods are allowed only if the employee is completely relieved of duty. If an employee must stay with residents or respond during a meal period, the meal period is paid time.

Payroll staff totals hours for each workweek by employee, combining hours from all homes and positions of [AGENCY NAME]. Overtime is paid at one and one-half times the regular rate for hours over 40 in the workweek.
The Administrator plans schedules to limit unplanned overtime while keeping the staffing required by STF-01. Overtime may be required to maintain required supervision, and it is always paid.

The Administrator does not classify any DSP or other direct care position as exempt from overtime, and does not treat any DSP as an independent contractor, without written review by [WAGE-HOUR ADVISOR OR COUNSEL]. The review is kept in the payroll file.

Payroll is paid on [PAY SCHEDULE]. The employee receives a pay statement showing hours, rate, overtime, and deductions. Deductions are made only when required by law or authorized by the employee in writing, and never in a way that reduces pay below minimum wage or overtime due.

The Administrator verifies workers' compensation coverage in force with [INSURANCE CARRIER], policy number [POLICY NUMBER], before the first employee starts work. The Administrator reviews headcount at least quarterly, including part-time, relief, and seasonal staff, and keeps the certificate of coverage on file. Coverage is kept in force regardless of headcount once it is purchased.
The workers' compensation notice is posted at [LOCATION IN OFFICE] where employees can see it. New employees are told at orientation how to report a work injury (STF-04).

An employee who is hurt or becomes ill because of work reports it to the supervisor on duty immediately, or as soon as able. The supervisor arranges emergency care if needed, notifies the Administrator the same day, and completes the injury report on [FORM NAME] the same shift.

The Administrator reports the injury to the carrier promptly and within all time frames required by law and the policy, and gives the employee the claim information and the choice of authorized providers the carrier specifies. Employees are not disciplined or retaliated against for reporting an injury or filing a claim.
Return-to-work and fitness for duty after an injury follow STF-05. Staff who cannot safely perform duties are not scheduled to work alone with residents until cleared.

An employee who believes they were not paid correctly reports it to the Administrator, or to [OWNER OR GOVERNING BODY CONTACT] if the concern involves the Administrator. The Administrator reviews it within 5 business days, pays any amount owed on the next payroll or sooner, and documents the outcome. Retaliation is prohibited.

Once a year, and whenever the minimum wage changes, the Administrator performs a wage-and-hour self-audit. It compares a sample of timesheets to pay records, checks on-call and overnight pay, overtime, rates, and worker classification. Findings and corrections are reported to the governing body (GOV-01) and reviewed under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Provides funding to pay lawful wages and carry workers' compensation, reviews the annual self-audit, and acts on findings.
Sets compliant pay rates, enforces timekeeping, confirms workers' compensation coverage, handles injury reports and claims, investigates pay complaints, and completes the annual audit.
Calculates hours and overtime by workweek, issues pay statements, applies minimum wage updates, and keeps payroll records.
Make sure staff record all time, do not allow off-the-clock work, and report work injuries the same shift.

responsibilities.role: Direct Support Professionals and other employees
responsibilities.duty: Record time accurately, report pay errors and injuries promptly, and do not work unrecorded time.

documentation: Pay rate schedule and written pay statement signed at hire
Time records for each shift and workweek
Payroll registers and employee pay statements
Overtime calculations and any written wage-hour exemption or classification reviews
On-call and overnight pay determinations
Workers' compensation certificate of coverage and quarterly headcount review
Work injury reports, carrier claim records and return-to-work records
Pay complaint log and resolutions
Annual wage-and-hour self-audit report
Records kept in the personnel and payroll files for the period required by law, and not less than the period set in STF-06

policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All staff who create, use, store, or release records for individuals residing in [AGENCY NAME] facilities. This includes the Administrator, DSPs, nurses and delegated health staff, and administrative staff.
policies.purpose: To make sure a complete, current, and secure record is kept for each person we serve, that it is retained for the required period, and that it can be given to the Agency for Persons with Disabilities (APD) quickly when requested.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps an individual record for every resident with the contents required by Rule 65G-2.009(5), F.A.C. The record is updated within 30 days of receiving new information. Records are retained for 6 years. Copies of a resident's record are provided to APD within 2 calendar days of APD's request. Records are stored securely in the home's designated office area (Rule 65G-2.0072(4), F.A.C.), or in an access-controlled electronic system, and are protected under HIPAA (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164) and IR-05. Daily service documentation and billing support are handled under PCS-03 and GOV-05.

definitions.definition: The complete set of paper and electronic documents about one resident that [AGENCY NAME] must maintain under Rule 65G-2.009(5), F.A.C. It includes admission, plan, health, medication, incident, rights, funds, and property information.

Any information that changes or adds to what is in the record, such as a new diagnosis, medication order, assessment, plan, guardian or representative contact, rights restriction, incident, or hospital or clinic visit summary.
The area of the home set aside for administrative functions and record storage, as required by Rule 65G-2.0072(4), F.A.C.
Individually identifiable health information protected by 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164.
Every day of the week, including weekends and holidays.

procedures: Within 1 business day after the admission decision, the Administrator opens an individual record for the resident in [RECORD SYSTEM / FILE LOCATION], using the standard table of contents on [RECORD INDEX FORM], which lists every item required by Rule 65G-2.009(5), F.A.C.

The record contains, at a minimum: identification and face sheet; guardian, health care surrogate, or representative information; admission and referral documents and APD authorizations; the individual plan and support documents; health information, physician orders and medication administration records; incident reports and follow-up; rights restriction documentation and any due process records; funds and property inventory records; and discharge or transfer documents. The Administrator confirms each required item is present at 30 days after admission and at each annual review.

Any staff member who receives new information about a resident gives it to the Administrator or designee the same business day. The designee files it in the record within 30 days at the latest. The target is within 5 business days, and urgent health or safety information is filed and shared with the team immediately (PCS-04).

Each entry is dated and signed or initialed with the author's printed name and title. Electronic entries are time-stamped and show the author. Errors are corrected by a single line, date, and initials in paper records, or by an addendum in electronic records. Information is never erased or obscured.

Original records are kept in the designated office area in a locked cabinet or in a password-protected system. Only the Administrator and staff designated in writing on [ACCESS LIST] have access. Daily-use records, such as medication records, are kept in a locked area in the home, and the Administrator ensures they move to the record on the schedule set by this policy.

Residents' records are not left unattended in common areas, vehicles, or on unlocked screens. Records are not taken out of the home except to an appointment or transfer, in which case staff carry only what is needed and return it the same day.

Each person with access signs a confidentiality acknowledgement at hire (STF-06, IR-05). The Administrator reviews the access list at least quarterly and removes access immediately when employment ends or duties change.

Records are released only as allowed by IR-05, with a valid authorization from the resident or legal representative, or as permitted or required by law. Release to APD for oversight does not require a separate authorization. Every release is entered in the record disclosure log with date, recipient, purpose, and what was released.

When APD requests copies of a resident's record, the staff member receiving the request notifies the Administrator immediately. The Administrator copies the complete requested record and sends it by [SECURE METHOD] within 2 calendar days of the request, counting weekends and holidays. If the Administrator is unavailable, the designated backup performs this step.

The Administrator logs each APD records request on the Reports Calendar (REC-02) showing the date requested, date sent, method, and staff who sent it. If the requested information cannot be sent within 2 calendar days, the Administrator tells APD before the deadline passes and sends all available documents.

Electronic records are backed up at least [BACKUP FREQUENCY]. The Administrator confirms the backup can be restored, tests it at least annually, and stores copies in a secure location. Scanned paper documents are checked for legibility before the paper original is moved to inactive storage.

Records are retained for 6 years, per Rule 65G-2.009(5), F.A.C. As a conservative agency practice, [AGENCY NAME] counts the 6 years from the later of the date of the record or the resident's discharge or transfer. If another law or payer requires a longer period (GOV-05), the longer period applies.

When a resident is discharged, transferred, or dies, the Administrator closes the record within 30 days. The record is labeled with the discharge date and the earliest destruction date, and is moved to secure inactive storage. A copy of the discharge and transfer documents goes to the receiving provider as required by PCS-06.

Records subject to an open investigation, incident review, audit, claim, or legal hold are not destroyed, even if the retention period has passed. The Administrator places the hold in writing and releases it only after all matters are resolved.

After the retention period, the Administrator approves destruction in writing. Paper records are shredded and electronic records are permanently deleted, with the date, method, and staff recorded in the destruction log. The log itself is kept permanently.

If a record is lost, stolen, or accessed without authorization, the staff member who finds it tells the Administrator immediately. The Administrator follows the breach process in IR-05, attempts to reconstruct the record, documents what happened, and reports to APD as required by REC-02 and BSP-04 if applicable.

At least twice a year, the Administrator or designee audits a sample of resident records for completeness, timeliness of the 30-day updates, signatures, and secure storage. Findings and corrections are documented and summarized for the governing body under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Opens and maintains each record, makes sure it is complete and updated within 30 days, controls access and release, sends copies to APD within 2 calendar days, approves retention and destruction, and runs record audits.
Carries out record release to APD and other records duties when the Administrator is unavailable.
Document accurately and on time, give new information to the Administrator the same business day, and keep records secure.
Provides health documents, orders, and assessments for the record and reviews health portions for accuracy (HW-02).
Oversees HIPAA compliance, access controls, and breach response (IR-05).

documentation: Individual record for each resident with a table of contents confirming required items
Record access list and signed confidentiality acknowledgements
Record disclosure log
APD records request log showing date requested and date sent
Backup and restore test records
Record audit reports and corrective actions
Retention schedule, legal hold notices, and destruction log
Discharge or closure record showing earliest destruction date

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, designated backup, shift supervisors, and all staff who identify events that must be reported to the Agency for Persons with Disabilities (APD) or other state authorities.
policies.purpose: To make sure every notice, report, and filing that [AGENCY NAME] owes to APD and other state authorities is identified, assigned, submitted on time, and documented, so that residents are protected and the license stays in good standing.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] meets each state reporting deadline listed in this policy. It reports census changes in writing to APD, with notice before the change and an updated census within 5 calendar days (Rule 65G-2.006(2) and Rule 65G-2.009(3), F.A.C.). It reports critical incidents to APD within 4 hours of the initial notice and submits APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day (Rule 65G-2.010(6), F.A.C.). It reports evacuations within 6 hours and every 6 hours after, and shelter use over capacity within 48 hours (Rule 65G-2.010(4), F.A.C.). It files the annual sworn cost statement (s. 393.067(10), F.S.) and submits renewal at least 45 days before the license expires (Rule 65G-2.002(4), F.A.C.). It requests capacity changes 30 days ahead (Rule 65G-2.006(1)(d), F.A.C.), gives 30 days' written notice before closing a home (Rule 65G-2.002(13), F.A.C.), and gives the DSP supervised-hire notice within 5 days of hire. Reports to the Florida Abuse Hotline are made immediately by anyone who suspects abuse, neglect, or exploitation, and are not delayed to complete any other report. A deadline is counted from the time of the event or the time staff first learn of it, whichever the rule requires, and the shorter reading is used whenever there is doubt.

definitions.definition: The APD Regional Office that licenses and monitors the home, at [REGIONAL OFFICE NAME], [REGIONAL OFFICE PHONE] and [REGIONAL OFFICE EMAIL].

An incident that APD classifies as critical on Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 and its instructions in effect at the time, and which requires initial notice within 4 hours. The Administrator keeps the current form and instructions in the Reports Binder.
An incident listed as reportable on form OP 3-0006 that is not critical, which must be reported within 1 calendar day. Incident handling is covered in BSP-04.
The current list of residents living in the home, which may not exceed licensed capacity, and which must match the resident characteristics approved on the license (Rule 65G-2.006(3), F.A.C.).
The maximum number of residents APD has approved for the home. Each home has its own license (Rule 65G-2.002(8), F.A.C.).
The annual sworn statement of costs for APD-funded clients required by s. 393.067(10), F.S.
Every day of the week, including weekends and holidays.
The agency's tracking calendar and log of all recurring and event-based reports, kept by the Administrator.

procedures: The Administrator keeps a Reports Calendar for each licensed home listing every recurring due date. These include the license renewal date, the date 45 days before expiration, the annual fire inspection, the annual sworn cost statement, the annual CEMP review, and the monthly fire drills. Each entry shows the responsible person and a backup. The calendar is reviewed at the start of each month.

Abuse, neglect, or exploitation: any staff member who suspects it calls the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 immediately, before doing any other report. They tell the Administrator or backup right after, and the call is documented under BSP-03. A report to the Hotline is never delayed for internal review.

Critical incidents: the staff member on duty first protects the resident and obtains medical or emergency help if needed (HW-04). They then notify the Administrator or backup immediately. The Administrator or backup gives the Regional Office the initial notice within 4 hours, by phone and [OTHER METHOD], and records the time, person contacted, and what was said.

Critical incident form: the Administrator completes APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 (Dec. 2025, or the version current at the time) and submits it to the Regional Office within 1 calendar day of the incident. If facts are not yet known, the form is submitted with what is known and updated later.
Reportable incidents that are not critical: the Administrator submits form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day of the incident.

Follow-up: the Administrator sends follow-up information on each reported incident within 5 days, covering the outcome, injuries, medical follow-up, actions taken to protect the resident, and any change to the plan. Follow-up is documented and added to the incident file (BSP-04).

Missing resident: if a resident is missing, staff follow BSP-05 immediately. The Administrator also makes the reports required by Rule 65G-2.010(5) and (6), F.A.C., including law enforcement and APD notice, treating the event as critical unless APD instructions say otherwise.

Census changes (admissions, transfers, discharges, hospitalizations that change where the resident lives, deaths): before accepting each new resident or transferring a resident, the Administrator gives APD written notice and waits for any required approval (SDB-01, PCS-01, PCS-06). The Administrator confirms the admission fits the licensed capacity and the resident characteristics on the license.

Within 5 calendar days after any census change, the Administrator sends the updated census in writing to the Regional Office by [METHOD] and keeps proof of sending. For a death, the Administrator also follows HW-05, and the census update follows the incident reporting timelines.

Evacuation: if the home is evacuated under the CEMP (SDA-01, HES-02), the Administrator or backup reports to the Regional Office within 6 hours, gives the residents' location and condition, and updates the Regional Office every 6 hours until residents return. Each contact is logged with date, time, person, and content.

Emergency shelter over capacity: if residents shelter somewhere that puts the shelter over its capacity, the Administrator reports it to the Regional Office within 48 hours with the location, number of residents, and reason.

Capacity or characteristics change: if the home wants a change in licensed capacity or resident characteristics, the Administrator submits a written request to the Regional Office at least 30 days before the proposed change. The request includes proof of a passed fire inspection and proof of zoning compliance (GOV-07). The change is not made until APD approves it in writing.

Annual sworn cost statement: the Administrator and [FINANCE STAFF/CPA] prepare the statement for APD-funded residents, the owner or authorized officer signs it under oath before a notary, and the Administrator submits it by the due date set by APD and keeps a copy (GOV-06). The Administrator puts the due date on the Reports Calendar when APD issues the notice.

License renewal: the Administrator submits a complete renewal application to the Regional Office at least 45 days before the license expiration date, with all documents, screenings, and a satisfactory inspection as required by Rule 65G-2.002, F.A.C. A late or incomplete renewal is treated as an initial application, so the Administrator starts preparation at least 90 days before expiration, and checks the status 30 days before submission (GOV-02).

Annual fire inspection: the Administrator schedules the annual fire inspection under ch. 69A-38, F.A.C., so an approved inspection is in hand before renewal, and sends the approved report to the Regional Office with the renewal (HES-02). Deficiencies found in any inspection are corrected before the license issues.

Closure of a home: the Administrator gives APD 30 days' written notice before closing a home. The notice includes the planned closure date and the transition plan for each resident (PCS-06). The Administrator does not set a closure date less than 30 days from the date of the notice without APD approval.

DSP supervised-hire notice: when a direct support professional is hired and begins work under supervision pending screening or other qualification requirements, the Administrator gives the Regional Office written notice within 5 days of the hire date and records the date the notice was sent (STF-02, STF-03).
Record copies: when APD requests a resident's record, the Administrator sends the copy within 2 calendar days (REC-01) and logs it on the Reports Calendar.

Quality check: each month, the Administrator compares the incident log, census log, drill records, and Reports Calendar for missed or late reports. Late or missed reports are documented with a cause and corrective action. The governing body reviews timeliness each quarter under GOV-04. The Administrator contacts the Regional Office promptly about any report that was late.

required_items.text: Written criteria and procedures in place for the admission or termination of residential services for residents

required_items.text: Written criteria relating to the use of video monitoring equipment if applicant makes use of such devices

The licensee shall have written criteria and procedures in place for the admission or termination of residential services for clients; termination procedures must be consistent with Chapter 65G-3, F.A.C. (the 2026 notice prints '(a) No change'; text taken from the prior rule.)

When determining whether to accept a person as a resident, the facility shall: 1. ensure placement does not adversely affect the health, safety, or welfare of current residents; 2. obtain the Agency's approval prior to any placement that deviates from the criteria on the licensure application; 3. provide descriptive information to the Agency on a prospective resident who is not an Agency client (IDD documentation, medical needs, behavioral issues, known criminal history).

Resident rights: the facility shall adhere to and protect resident rights and freedoms under the Bill of Rights of Persons with Developmental Disabilities (s. 393.13, F.S.), including: 1. dignity, privacy, humane care, freedom from abuse/neglect/exploitation; 2. freedom from harm, including unnecessary physical, chemical or mechanical restraint, isolation, excessive medication; 3. religious freedom; 4. services in the least restrictive conditions; 5. education and training; 6. social interaction and community activities; 7. exercise and recreation; 8. consent to or refuse treatment; 9. non-discrimination; 10. voting.

Each facility shall establish, maintain, and make available to residents and employees written house rules and regulations in consultation with residents, for the orderly operation of the group home facility.

The licensee must develop policies and procedures which detail the methods for management and accounting of any personal funds or benefits of facility residents. The policies and procedures must comply with generally accepted accounting principles. Each staff member having access to resident funds and account information must be trained in the proper implementation of these policies and procedures.

Only if a resident is to be left alone for limited periods: the licensee prepares a written plan proposing that a specified client be left alone for limited periods during the day or night; the plan must be approved by the Regional Office prior to implementation.

A licensee who uses video monitoring shall: 1. develop written criteria for determining which residents will be monitored by video camera; 2. develop written protocols for implementing video monitoring, including a. who may access video footage, b. the purpose and use of video recordings, and c. how, when, and where footage will be stored and for how long, to include a minimum thirty-day retention period. (See also (7)(b)3.-6. on consent, disclosure to the Agency and footage preservation.)

The facility shall have a written statement of policies and procedures governing actions that may be taken by direct service providers to help prevent or respond to problematic behaviors exhibited by residents, including emergency procedures and reporting requirements, consistent with s. 393.13, F.S., and Chapters 65G-4 and 65G-8, F.A.C.

Direct service providers must be trained to appropriately respond to serious and spontaneous behavioral incidents requiring emergency intervention; restraint/seclusion or physical-discomfort procedures only if certified under Chapter 65G-8 and with Local Review Committee approval; forbidden responses: 1. physical or corporal punishment; 2. (no change); 3. verbal abuse; 4. humiliation (including dark or locked time-out rooms); 5. any reactive strategy prohibited under Rule 65G-8.009.

The licensee shall develop and enforce a written policy regarding sexual activity involving residents of the facility. Such policy shall: 1. explicitly prohibit sexual activity between a resident and a covered person; 2. explicitly prohibit sexual activity involving residents under age eighteen; 3. not abridge residents' civil and legal rights (s. 393.13, F.S.); 4. address appropriate physical boundaries and standards among direct service providers and residents, including: a. dress code for direct service providers; b. mutual respect for personal space (e.g., knocking before entering a bedroom); c. parameters on who is allowed to visit whose bedroom and under what conditions; d. all residents and direct service providers sleep in separate beds; e. assisting/supervising bathing, showering, toileting, and no simultaneous bathing/toileting by staff; f. guidelines on level and type of supervision; g. open communication to encourage reporting of inappropriate sexual behavior.

The licensee shall provide direct service providers with training regarding the sexual-activity policy. Safeguards must be implemented in any facility serving one or more sexually aggressive residents or residents requiring a Safety Plan (review of history information; Safety Plan review before admission and staff training; resident or legal representative signs the Safety Plan and it is reviewed at least annually; Agency approval before sharing a bedroom; no unsupervised closed-door contact for minors; bathroom use one at a time; no obscene materials for minors).

[Standard; the notice text does not use the words 'written policy'] Medication: administration per the health care practitioner's written order; original labeled containers; locked storage accessible only to staff; daily medication administration record per Chapter 65G-7; administration, documentation, storage and error reporting per ss. 393.13 and 393.506, F.S., and Chapter 65G-7; ongoing staff re-training when medication errors occur; adverse reactions conveyed immediately to the prescriber or medical professional.

Each facility shall have a system in place to communicate recent incidents and resident information to staff on subsequent shifts, including 1. a mechanism for documenting in writing information (medical or behavioral incidents, physician or therapist orders) staff should know, and 2. a procedure to ensure the information is reviewed across all shifts.

At least one telephone accessible to direct service providers and residents for emergency use at all times; required emergency telephone numbers (including each resident's doctors and each resident's support coordinator) readily accessible at each telephone extension.

Emergency preparedness drills: dates and results of required monthly fire drills (time of day, points of exit used, evacuation time, signature of person conducting) recorded and kept one year; no fire drills between midnight and 5:00 a.m.; Regional Office staff may observe drills. (Annual fire inspection under Chapter 69A-38, F.A.C., is required under 65G-2.010(2).)

Each facility shall prepare and maintain a written comprehensive emergency management plan (s. 393.067(8), F.S.), updated as needed and annually, addressing: 1. provisions for all hazards (hurricanes, tornadoes, flooding, fires, hazardous materials, transportation accidents, power outages in severe cold/hot weather); 2. care of residents remaining in the facility (pre-disaster preparation, protecting the facility, supplies, medications, emergency power, food and water, adequate staffing, emergency equipment); 3. care of residents evacuated (identification of residents, transfer of records, evacuation transportation, sheltering, supplies, staffing, emergency equipment, medications); 4.-5. [printed as 'No change', not shown in the notice]; 6. post-disaster activities (family inquiries, medical intervention, transportation, reporting relocated residents to the county emergency management office); 7. [printed as 'No change', not shown]. Staff must be trained on the plan within 30 days of hire and annually after each update.

Missing residents procedure: after determining that a resident is missing, staff immediately call local law enforcement and ask the officer to [items (a) and (c) printed as 'No change'], assign a case number; if the officer refuses a report, document the officer's name and contact the Watch Commander; make a critical incident report per (6)(f).

Incident reporting: known or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation reported immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline (ss. 39.201, 415.1034, F.S.); critical incidents — initial notice to the Regional Office within four hours and a complete APD Incident Reporting Form (OP 3-0006) within one calendar day; reportable incidents within one calendar day; notify the legal representative and support coordinator; follow-up measures on the form within five days; list of critical and reportable incident types in (6)(f)3. and (6)(g).
All licensees with employees shall develop and maintain the following personnel policies, procedures and records: (a) Job descriptions for paid staff
Documentation of all facility staff training, including a record of training dates, training content and trainers, and staff in attendance

Separate personnel records for each full and part-time employee that contain written documentation of the employees' education, qualifications experience, references, background screening, staff training participation, and any disciplinary action taken against the employee

A weekly written schedule indicating staff coverage for at least one week in advance. Weekly schedules of actual staff coverage shall be maintained for a six-month period (provide to the Regional Office within three calendar days on request, (6)(b)).

Staff training requirements: Zero Tolerance training (detection, prevention, reporting of abuse, neglect, exploitation) before providing direct services, with a refresher every three years; basic first aid and CPR certification within 90 days (classroom, not online; at least one CPR-certified provider on site when residents are present); staff trained on residents' current behavior plans by a certified behavior analyst, with documentation in the personnel record; comply with Chapter 65G-8; written documentation of required training kept at least three years.

Safety standards: annual update of staff driving history for staff who transport residents; at least annually access the FDLE Sex Offender/Predator Database for registrants within a one-mile radius, notify staff and document the notification.

If an employee has a verified finding of abuse, neglect, exploitation or abandonment and remains employed, the licensee must submit a Corrective Action Plan to the Regional Office within 15 days containing: 1. why the employment is not terminated; 2. disciplinary action taken; 3. any training and dates; 4. how residents will be protected.

Menus shall be planned, written, and dated at least two days in advance of consumption. Resident participation in meal planning is recommended but not required. (Also (13)(e): meals are developed in accordance with residents' individual medical, behavioral, and dietary requirements; (13)(g): at least two days of fresh food and five days of staple food and drinking water supplies on hand in accordance with the menu.)

Each facility that requires medically essential service is solely responsible for any backup equipment or power supply and a planned course of action in the event of a power outage or interruption of service, in accordance with s. 366.15, F.S.

official.notes: No standalone APD policy-review checklist for group homes was located. An older version of Rule 65G-2.002 told staff to review applications using a 'Group Home Facility Checklist APD 2014-04' <cite index="8-1">(10) Agency staff shall review applications for licensure using the following forms: Foster Care Facility Checklist APD 2014-03... Group Home Facility Checklist APD 2014-04</cite>. The 2025–26 rule instead requires the license application <cite index="9-1">All applications for initial licensure as well licensure renewal must be submitted using License Application form 65G-2.002-A</cite>, whose Section 9 is the working checklist. Submission: the application is completed under oath and sent to the APD Regional Office, with renewals due at least 45 days before expiration <cite index="9-2">An application for the renewal of license must be submitted to the Agency at least 45 days prior to the expiration of the current license.</cite>. The application is complete only on receipt of all required documents, screening results and fees, and a licensure inspection is not authorized until then (proposed 65G-2.002(11)-(12)). APD's iConnect new-licensing guide lists attachments including <cite index="7-6,7-7,7-8,7-9">Admin Policies; Emergency Mgmt Plan; Professional Liability Insurance; Sexual Activity Policy</cite>, so also upload policies as separate, clearly titled files. Suggested organization: use the form's order (9.A, then 9.B) for the five form items, then a rule-based section keyed to the rule citations above (resident rights/house rules, resident funds, behavior, sexual activity, video monitoring, medication, emergency/fire, incident and missing-resident reporting, personnel and training, meals). Cross-reference each manual section to its form bullet or rule number. Caveats: (1) the form's two bullet lists are unnumbered, so 'bullet N' IDs are my own counting; (2) the rule items other than 65G-2.007 use numbering from the Jan. 6, 2026 proposed text and may differ in the adopted 3/26/2026 text; I confirmed this for 65G-2.007, where the adopted menu item is (13)(f) rather than the proposed (13)(g); (3) the Oct. 2025 form still shows the older 'residents of the facility' wording on the sexual-activity bullet, and the proposed rule text refers to a December 2025 edition, so confirm the current edition with the Regional Office. Not listed as written-policy items because the rule text does not call for a written policy: records content (resident records, property inventory, transportation log), solicitation permission, first aid kit, and optional in-service training. Form Section 4 also asks the applicant to attest that all employees receive abuse-prevention training before direct client contact. The rule text reviewed contains no explicit requirement for written complaint/grievance, theft/loss or control-of-property procedures. Check iBudget Handbook/MWSA provider requirements (Rule 59G-13.070) separately for waiver enrollment, which these documents do not cover.
